entry_text: A GSM radio access network provides the radio link between GSM mobile devices and the mobile core network.
example: The network coordinates a phone's connection as it moves from one coverage cell to another.

label: Gynaecology
entry_text: Gynaecology is the medical specialty concerned with the health and disorders of the female reproductive system.
example: A gynaecologist evaluates the cause of persistent pelvic pain.

label: Hadron physics
entry_text: Hadron physics studies particles made of quarks and gluons and the strong interaction that governs them.
example: Researchers compare measured properties of mesons with predictions about quark interactions.

label: Health economics and outcomes research
entry_text: Health economics and outcomes research examines the costs, effects and patient outcomes of healthcare interventions and systems.
example: A team compares the costs and quality-of-life outcomes of two treatment approaches.

label: Health, safety and environment
entry_text: Health, safety and environment is an organizational discipline for managing occupational health, workplace safety and environmental impacts.
example: A manufacturing site reviews worker exposure risks and wastewater controls through its HSE program.

label: Healthcare delivery science
entry_text: Healthcare delivery science studies how care is organized and provided and how delivery can improve patient outcomes and system performance.
example: A health system compares follow-up scheduling models to reduce missed visits.

label: Healthcare industry knowledge
entry_text: Healthcare industry knowledge includes how healthcare providers, insurers, suppliers and regulators interact to deliver and pay for care.
example: A project lead anticipates how insurer reimbursement rules affect a clinic's adoption of a new service.

label: Healthcare quality
entry_text: Healthcare quality concerns how well services increase the likelihood of desired health outcomes and meet accepted standards of care.
example: A hospital tracks preventable readmissions to assess a discharge improvement program.

label: Higher education law
entry_text: Higher education law concerns legal rules that govern colleges, universities and their relationships with students, staff and regulators.
example: A university attorney reviews how a disciplinary procedure meets legal obligations.

label: Higher education policy
entry_text: Higher education policy concerns decisions and rules that shape the goals, funding and operation of colleges and universities.
example: An analyst considers who gains access under a systemwide change to admissions policy.

label: Hindsight bias
entry_text: Hindsight bias is the tendency to see an outcome as more predictable after learning that it occurred.
example: After an outage, a reviewer overestimates how obvious its warning signs were at the time.

label: Historic preservation
entry_text: Historic preservation is the identification, protection and conservation of buildings, sites and landscapes with historic significance.
example: A preservation team repairs original masonry while adapting a historic building for public use.

label: Historical linguistics
entry_text: Historical linguistics studies how languages change over time and how related languages can be traced to common ancestors.
example: A linguist compares systematic sound correspondences across related languages.

label: History and Archeology
entry_text: Knowledge of historical events and their causes, indicators, and effects on civilizations and cultures.

label: History of education
entry_text: The history of education studies how teaching, schools and access to learning have changed over time.
example: A historian examines who attended newly established public schools and what they were taught.

label: History of medicine
entry_text: The history of medicine studies changes in understandings of health, medical practices and healthcare institutions over time.
example: A researcher traces how hospital sanitation practices changed as infection theories developed.

label: History of philosophy
entry_text: The history of philosophy studies philosophical ideas, arguments and schools in their historical development and context.
example: A seminar compares how ancient and modern philosophers understand the source of moral obligation.

label: History of science
entry_text: The history of science studies how scientific knowledge and practices develop within changing institutional and cultural contexts.
example: A historian examines how access to new instruments changed what astronomers could measure.

label: Hockett's design features
entry_text: Hockett's design features are proposed properties used to describe human language and compare it with other communication systems.
example: A class uses displacement to discuss how speakers can refer to events that are not present.

label: Human factors
entry_text: Human factors studies how human capabilities and limitations interact with tasks, tools and environments to inform design.
example: A team changes a control panel layout to reduce confusion during time-critical operations.

label: Human-machine interface
entry_text: A human-machine interface is the set of controls and displays through which people exchange information with a machine.
example: A pump operator adjusts the flow setpoint and reads the measured flow on a touchscreen.

label: Human musculoskeletal system
entry_text: The human musculoskeletal system consists of bones, muscles, joints and connective tissues that support the body and enable movement.
example: A therapist explains how the quadriceps and knee joint work together when climbing stairs.

label: Human rights law
entry_text: Human rights law concerns legal protections for fundamental rights and freedoms, including the obligations of states to uphold them.
example: A legal researcher compares protections for freedom of expression under national law and international treaties.

label: HVAC automation systems
entry_text: HVAC automation systems use sensors, controllers and programmed rules to regulate heating, ventilation and air conditioning.
example: A building controller adjusts airflow based on occupancy and room temperature.

label: HVAC controls
entry_text: HVAC controls are devices and logic that regulate heating, ventilation and cooling equipment to meet specified conditions.
example: A thermostat signals the heating system when room temperature falls below its setpoint.

label: Hypercompact stellar systems
entry_text: Hypercompact stellar systems are hypothesized groups of stars that remain tightly bound to a black hole displaced from its original galactic center.
example: An astronomer looks for unusual stellar velocities to distinguish a candidate from an ordinary compact star cluster.

label: Image and video compression
entry_text: Image and video compression encodes visual data in fewer bits by reducing redundancy, optionally discarding some detail.
example: A streaming service compresses a video so it can play over a slower connection.

label: Imaging informatics
entry_text: Imaging informatics concerns the collection, storage, exchange and use of medical images and their associated information.
example: A hospital links radiology images to the correct patient record for clinical review.

label: Immunization
entry_text: Immunization is the process of acquiring protection against an infectious disease, commonly by vaccination.
example: A public health program monitors immunization coverage to identify populations lacking protection.

label: Immunohaematology
entry_text: Immunohaematology studies immune responses to blood cell antigens, especially in transfusion medicine.
example: A blood bank checks compatibility between a patient's blood and potential donor units.

label: In-memory database
entry_text: An in-memory database stores its working data primarily in RAM to make reads and writes fast.
example: A scoreboard uses an in-memory database to retrieve recently updated rankings.

label: Inbound logistics
entry_text: Inbound logistics manages the movement and receipt of supplies or materials into an organization.
example: A factory schedules inbound deliveries to keep ingredients available without overloading storage.

label: Incurred but not reported
entry_text: Incurred but not reported describes insurance losses that have already occurred but are not yet known to the insurer.
example: An actuary estimates reserves for claims likely to arrive after the reporting date.

label: Indentation hardness
entry_text: Indentation hardness measures resistance to permanent deformation produced by pressing an indenter into a material.
example: A laboratory uses the size of an impression to compare two treated metal samples.

label: Individual life insurance
entry_text: Individual life insurance is coverage issued under an individual policy rather than obtained through a group plan.
example: A policyholder names family members as beneficiaries of their own policy.

label: Individualized Education Program
entry_text: An Individualized Education Program is a written U.S. special-education plan specifying a qualifying student's goals, services and supports.
example: A school team documents a learning goal and how progress will be measured.

label: Individualized Family Service Plan
entry_text: An Individualized Family Service Plan documents U.S. early-intervention outcomes and services for an eligible infant or toddler and the family.
example: A family and service coordinator agree on support for communication during everyday routines.

label: Industrial Internet of Things
entry_text: The Industrial Internet of Things connects industrial equipment, sensors and software to exchange data and support monitoring or control.
example: A plant tracks vibration readings from connected motors to schedule maintenance.

label: Industrial statistics
entry_text: Industrial statistics applies statistical methods to manufacturing, process improvement and other industrial decisions.
example: A quality engineer uses a control chart to distinguish routine variation from an unusual change.

label: Infant development
entry_text: Infant development concerns physical, cognitive, communicative and social changes during infancy.
example: A researcher observes changes in how infants respond to familiar voices.

label: Ingredient functionality
entry_text: Ingredient functionality concerns how an ingredient contributes to a food's properties or processing behavior.
example: A formulation team uses a starch's thickening properties to improve sauce consistency.

label: Integrative biology
entry_text: Integrative biology combines evidence or methods across biological disciplines and scales to explain living systems.
example: A team combines biomechanics and ecology to explain how animals move across different habitats.

label: Intellectual property
entry_text: Intellectual property concerns legal rights in certain creations, inventions, identifying marks and protected information.
example: A publishing team checks which rights it needs to reproduce an illustration.

label: Intended Nationally Determined Contributions
entry_text: Intended Nationally Determined Contributions were climate commitments proposed by countries before or in connection with joining the Paris Agreement.
example: A policy analyst compares a country's initial intended contribution with its later formally submitted contribution.

label: ISS Environmental Control and Life Support System
entry_text: The ISS Environmental Control and Life Support System maintains conditions needed for crew survival aboard the International Space Station.
example: The system manages cabin air quality and recovers reusable water.

label: IT governance
entry_text: IT governance assigns decision rights and accountability for directing and overseeing an organization's information technology.
example: A board defines who can approve major technology investments and how results will be monitored.

label: Itô's lemma
entry_text: Itô's lemma gives the differential of a function of an Itô process, accounting for the second-order contribution of stochastic variation.
example: An analyst derives the dynamics of the logarithm of a modeled asset price.

label: Knowledge graphs
entry_text: A knowledge graph organizes entities, attributes and relationships into a graph with explicit meanings for its connections.
example: A museum links artists to their works so researchers can trace shared exhibitions.

label: Labor market trends
entry_text: Labor market trends are changes over time in indicators such as employment, wages, vacancies or participation.
example: A workforce planner compares several years of vacancy rates across occupations.

label: Labour economics
entry_text: Labour economics studies how workers and employers interact and how wages, employment and working conditions are determined.
example: An economist models how access to training affects wages and job mobility.

label: Labour law
entry_text: Labour law concerns legal rules governing employment relationships, working conditions and collective worker rights.
example: A legal team reviews how a collective bargaining provision applies to a shift change.

label: Land-atmosphere interactions
entry_text: Land-atmosphere interactions are exchanges of energy, water and other materials between the land surface and the air above it.
example: A climate model uses soil moisture to estimate how much surface energy goes into evaporation.

label: Large language models
entry_text: Large language models are large machine-learning models trained to learn patterns in language and perform tasks such as generating or transforming text.
example: An assistant turns a long project update into a short summary for review.

label: Laser engineering
entry_text: Laser engineering applies optical and engineering principles to the design and integration of lasers and laser-based systems.
example: An engineer matches a laser's wavelength and beam properties to an optical measurement task.

label: Laser printing
entry_text: Laser printing uses a laser to form an electrostatic image on a photosensitive surface so toner can be transferred and fused to paper.
example: An office printer produces sharp text by depositing toner only where the page image requires it.

label: Latin American and Latino studies
entry_text: Latin American and Latino studies examines histories, cultures and societies of Latin America and Latino communities, often including cross-border connections.
example: A course compares migration narratives in Latin American and U.S. Latino literature.

label: Law and Government
entry_text: Knowledge of laws, legal codes, court procedures, precedents, government regulations, executive orders, agency rules, and the democratic political process.

label: Law enforcement operations
entry_text: Law enforcement operations concerns how agencies coordinate personnel, procedures and resources to carry out public-safety duties.
example: An agency coordinates call dispatch and traffic diversion during a road closure.

label: Law enforcement practices
entry_text: Law enforcement practices are the methods and professional procedures used to carry out, document and review law enforcement work.
example: A supervisor reviews whether officers documented incident decisions consistently.

label: Lawful interception
entry_text: Lawful interception is the legally authorized collection of specified communications or related data, subject to defined procedures and oversight.
example: A compliance team reviews whether an authorization covers the requested records.

label: Leisure education
entry_text: Leisure education helps people develop the knowledge and skills to choose and participate in personally meaningful leisure activities.
example: A community program teaches participants how to identify accessible recreational options.

label: Letterforms
entry_text: Letterforms are the designed visual shapes of written letters.
example: A type designer adjusts the curve of a lowercase a to improve readability.

label: Librarianship
entry_text: Librarianship is the profession of organizing information resources and helping people find, evaluate and use them.
example: A librarian catalogs a collection and teaches patrons to search it efficiently.

label: Linguistic morphology
entry_text: Linguistic morphology studies how meaningful units combine within words and how word forms express grammatical distinctions.
example: A linguist analyzes how a plural suffix changes a noun's number.

label: Loan agreements
entry_text: Loan agreements are contracts that define the amount borrowed, repayment terms and obligations of the borrower and lender.
example: A business reviews a loan agreement to identify its repayment schedule and collateral obligations.

label: Logistics engineering
entry_text: Logistics engineering designs and evaluates systems for moving, storing and supplying goods or materials.
example: An engineer redesigns a warehouse layout to shorten replenishment routes.

label: Lookup table
entry_text: A lookup table stores preassigned results so an input can retrieve an answer without recomputing it.
example: An embedded controller maps sensor readings to calibrated temperatures using a lookup table.

label: Machining technology
entry_text: Machining technology concerns equipment, tooling and methods for shaping workpieces by removing material.
example: A machinist chooses a milling process to produce an accurately sized slot.

label: Mainframe storage
entry_text: Mainframe storage comprises the hardware and software used to retain, organize and access data for mainframe workloads.
example: A bank allocates disk volumes to handle its overnight batch processing.

label: Margin lending
entry_text: Margin lending allows a borrower to borrow against securities held as collateral, subject to collateral requirements.
example: A brokerage requires more collateral after the market value of a pledged account falls.

label: Market capitalization
entry_text: Market capitalization is the market price per share multiplied by the number of shares outstanding.
example: An analyst calculates a company’s market capitalization using its closing share price.

label: Market depth
entry_text: Market depth describes how much buying and selling interest is available at different prices near the market price.
example: A trader inspects the order book to see whether a large order would consume several price levels.

label: Mass media
entry_text: Mass media are channels and organizations that distribute content to large audiences.
example: A radio station broadcasts a weather update to listeners across a region.

label: Master production records
entry_text: Master production records specify the standard ingredients, instructions and controls for making a defined product or batch.
example: A quality team checks a completed batch record against the approved master production record.

label: Material flow
entry_text: Material flow is the movement of physical materials through storage, processing and distribution operations.
example: A factory maps how parts move between receiving, assembly and shipping.

label: Mathematics
entry_text: Knowledge of arithmetic, algebra, geometry, calculus, statistics, and their applications.

label: Mechanic's lien
entry_text: A mechanic's lien is a statutory claim against property that can secure payment for qualifying work or materials supplied to improve it.
example: A contractor asks whether unpaid renovation work qualifies for a lien.
sense_note: Requirements and terminology vary by jurisdiction.

label: Mechanical
entry_text: Knowledge of machines and tools, including their designs, uses, repair, and maintenance.

label: Mechanical drawings
entry_text: Mechanical drawings communicate the geometry, dimensions and other requirements of parts, assemblies or mechanical installations.
example: A fabricator uses a drawing to check the diameter and location of mounting holes.

label: Mechanical, electrical and plumbing systems
entry_text: Mechanical, electrical and plumbing systems are coordinated building services that supply functions such as climate control, power, water and drainage.
example: A design team checks that ductwork and electrical conduits do not interfere above a ceiling.

label: Media ethics
entry_text: Media ethics concerns principles for making responsible decisions about gathering, creating and distributing content.
example: An editor weighs the public interest against a private person's privacy before publishing a photograph.

label: Medical devices
entry_text: Medical devices are instruments, equipment, implants or software intended for a medical purpose such as diagnosis, monitoring or treatment.
example: A clinic uses a pulse oximeter to measure a patient's blood oxygen saturation.
sense_note: Formal regulatory definitions vary by jurisdiction.

label: Medical equipment
entry_text: Medical equipment comprises physical apparatus used in clinical care, diagnosis, monitoring or treatment.
example: A clinic maintains its examination tables and patient monitors as part of its equipment inventory.

label: Medicine and Dentistry
entry_text: Knowledge of the information and techniques needed to diagnose and treat human injuries, diseases, and deformities. This includes symptoms, treatment alternatives, drug properties and interactions, and preventive health-care measures.

label: Meta tag
entry_text: A meta tag is an HTML element that provides information or instructions about a document without adding visible page content.
example: A web developer sets a viewport meta tag to help a page display properly on phones.

label: Metaverse
entry_text: The metaverse is a broad concept for persistent, shared digital spaces where people interact, often through avatars.
example: A virtual exhibition lets attendees walk through the same digital gallery and speak to one another.
sense_note: The label has no single settled technical definition.

label: Metric system
entry_text: The metric system is a decimal system of measurement built around units such as the metre and gram.
example: A designer converts millimetres to metres by dividing the measurement by 1,000.

label: Microcontrollers
entry_text: Microcontrollers are integrated circuits that combine a processor, memory and input-output interfaces for embedded control.
example: A washing machine uses a microcontroller to read the door switch and coordinate the wash cycle.

label: Microscopic anatomy
entry_text: Microscopic anatomy studies tissue and cellular structures too small to examine in detail without magnification.
example: A student distinguishes skeletal muscle from connective tissue on a microscope slide.

label: Microsite
entry_text: A microsite is a small website or distinct section created around a narrow purpose, campaign or topic.
example: A museum builds a microsite with event details and registration for a special exhibit.

label: MicroStrategy metrics
entry_text: MicroStrategy metrics are calculation objects that define how data is aggregated or otherwise computed in MicroStrategy reports and dashboards.
example: A dashboard uses a reusable metric to compute net sales by region.

label: Mill test report
entry_text: A mill test report documents the tested chemical composition and mechanical properties of a manufactured material lot, typically metal.
example: A receiving inspector compares a steel heat number with the corresponding report before accepting delivery.

label: Millimeter waves
entry_text: Millimeter waves are electromagnetic waves with wavelengths of about one to ten millimetres.
example: A short-range radar uses millimeter waves to measure object distance.

label: Mineralogy
entry_text: Mineralogy studies minerals, including their chemistry, structure, physical properties and formation.
example: A geologist distinguishes two similar minerals by comparing hardness and crystal form.

label: Mixed reality
entry_text: Mixed reality combines digital content with a view of the physical surroundings so that virtual objects can be positioned in, and may respond to, the real environment.
example: A maintenance trainee views a digital alignment marker anchored to a physical pump.
sense_note: The boundary between mixed and augmented reality varies across sources.

label: Mobile computing
entry_text: Mobile computing uses portable devices to run applications and access information away from a fixed workstation.
example: A field technician updates a maintenance record from a tablet on site.

label: Models for life contingencies
entry_text: Models for life contingencies use probabilities and cash-flow timing to value payments that depend on events such as survival or death.
example: An actuary estimates the present value of payments from a lifetime annuity.

label: Molecular engineering
entry_text: Molecular engineering designs materials or systems by controlling their structures and interactions at the molecular scale.
example: A materials researcher designs polymer chains to alter how a coating repels water.

label: Motor control firmware
entry_text: Motor control firmware is low-level code running within a motor controller to manage its sensors, timing and output signals.
example: An embedded controller adjusts its drive output when feedback shows the motor slowing.

label: Motor control software
entry_text: Motor control software comprises programs and algorithms for commanding and monitoring a motor’s speed, position or torque.
example: A machine application requests a new motor speed and tracks whether the drive reaches it.

label: Multi-agent systems
entry_text: A multi-agent system consists of multiple decision-making entities that interact in a shared environment.
example: A warehouse simulation models robots that coordinate to avoid blocking one another.

label: Multi-core processors
entry_text: A multi-core processor integrates multiple processing cores that can execute work concurrently.
example: A video editor distributes independent rendering tasks across several cores.

label: Multi-core SMP
entry_text: Multi-core symmetric multiprocessing allows a common operating system to schedule work across peer processor cores that share main memory.
example: An operating system runs separate application threads on different cores while both access shared buffers.

label: Multi-core software
entry_text: Multi-core software is designed to use multiple processor cores to execute portions of work concurrently.
example: A simulation assigns independent regions of a grid to separate worker threads.

label: Multi-touch
entry_text: Multi-touch input detects and distinguishes multiple simultaneous contacts on a touch-sensitive surface.
example: A map application turns the movement of two fingers into a zoom gesture.

label: Multicultural education
entry_text: Multicultural education uses curricula and teaching practices that recognize cultural diversity and address inequities in learning.
example: A teacher compares accounts of the same event from several cultural perspectives.

label: Multitenancy
entry_text: Multitenancy lets separate customers share a service or infrastructure while keeping their information and configuration logically isolated.
example: A shared ticketing system restricts each organization to its own support cases.

label: Music theory
entry_text: Music theory studies how elements such as pitch, rhythm, harmony and form are organized in music.
example: A student identifies the cadence that marks the end of a musical phrase.

label: Mutual exclusion
entry_text: Mutual exclusion allows at most one participant at a time to enter a critical section or use a protected resource.
example: A mutex prevents two threads from updating a shared counter at the same time.

label: Mutual funds
entry_text: A mutual fund pools investors' money to hold a portfolio managed according to a common investment objective.
example: An index mutual fund buys securities to track a stock-market benchmark.

label: Naked short selling
entry_text: Naked short selling is selling a security short without first borrowing it or arranging to borrow it for delivery.
example: A compliance officer checks whether a short sale had the required borrowing arrangement before execution.
sense_note: Legal definitions and exceptions vary by jurisdiction.

label: Nanobiotechnology
entry_text: Nanobiotechnology studies or applies interactions between biological systems and structures at the nanoscale.
example: Researchers examine whether a nanoscale coating can improve the sensitivity of a diagnostic sensor.

label: Nanocomposites
entry_text: Nanocomposites combine a base material with a distinct component that has at least one nanoscale dimension to alter material properties.
example: An engineer compares the stiffness of a polymer with and without nanoscale clay particles.

label: Nanolithography
entry_text: Nanolithography creates patterns with nanoscale features on a surface.
example: A fabrication laboratory patterns nanoscale lines on a semiconductor wafer.

label: National Airspace System
entry_text: The National Airspace System is the integrated U.S. network of airspace, air navigation facilities, air traffic services, airports and operating procedures.
example: Air traffic managers coordinate alternate routes when severe weather closes a flight corridor.

label: Native American studies
entry_text: Native American studies examines the histories, cultures, politics and contemporary lives of Indigenous peoples of North America, especially within the United States.
example: A course examines how tribal sovereignty shapes relationships with federal and state governments.

label: Natural capital
entry_text: Natural capital is the stock of natural resources and ecosystems that supports flows of goods and services.
example: An assessment counts a wetland's capacity to reduce flooding as a benefit from natural capital.

label: Natural gas pipelines
entry_text: Natural gas pipelines carry natural gas through networks for gathering, transmission or distribution.
example: A distribution pipeline delivers gas from a regulated supply point to neighborhoods.

label: Natural language generation
entry_text: Natural language generation produces text or speech from data, representations or user instructions.
example: An application converts weekly rainfall measurements into a plain-language weather summary.

label: Natural language processing systems
entry_text: Natural language processing systems analyze, transform or generate human language using computational methods.
example: A service classifies customer messages by topic so they can be routed for review.

label: Natural language understanding
entry_text: Natural language understanding interprets meaning or intent from human language in context.
example: A virtual assistant identifies that a user asking about the next train wants a departure time.

label: Nautical charts
entry_text: Nautical charts depict navigable waters, depths, hazards and aids used to plan and conduct voyages.
example: A navigator uses charted depths to check whether a vessel can safely enter a harbor.

label: Net zero
entry_text: Net zero describes a balance between greenhouse gas emissions and removals within specified boundaries and a defined period.
example: A climate inventory separates remaining emissions from credited removals when assessing a net-zero claim.
sense_note: Some targets cover carbon dioxide alone rather than all greenhouse gases.

label: Network peering
entry_text: Network peering lets independent networks exchange traffic directly under a mutual arrangement rather than routing that traffic through transit providers.
example: Two internet providers exchange customer traffic at an internet exchange.

label: Network performance
entry_text: Network performance describes how efficiently and reliably a network delivers traffic, using measures such as throughput, latency and loss.
example: An engineer tracks latency and packet loss during video calls.

label: Network topology
entry_text: Network topology describes the physical or logical arrangement of network nodes and the links between them.
example: A designer compares a star layout with a ring for connecting office switches.

label: Neural networks
entry_text: Neural networks are computational models made of connected units whose parameters are commonly learned from data.
example: An image classifier learns weights that help distinguish handwritten digits.

label: Neurobiology
entry_text: Neurobiology studies the cells, circuits and processes that underlie nervous-system function.
example: A scientist investigates how synaptic signaling changes during learning.

label: Neuromuscular medicine
entry_text: Neuromuscular medicine is a specialty concerned with diagnosis and management of conditions affecting peripheral nerves, muscles and their connections.
example: A specialist evaluates a patient with persistent weakness of unclear origin.

label: Neuromuscular system and disorders
entry_text: Neuromuscular system and disorders covers how nerves activate muscles and what happens when the relevant nerves, junctions or muscles fail to work normally.
example: A student compares weakness from muscle disease with weakness from impaired nerve signaling.

label: Neurosurgery
entry_text: Neurosurgery is the medical specialty concerned with surgical care of disorders affecting the brain, spine and peripheral nerves.
example: A neurosurgical team evaluates whether a spinal disorder is appropriate for surgery.

label: NFPA 70E
entry_text: NFPA 70E is a U.S. consensus standard for electrical safety practices in workplaces.
example: A safety team uses NFPA 70E when reviewing how workers are protected from electrical hazards.

label: Non-Facility Associated Signalling
entry_text: Non-Facility Associated Signalling lets one signaling channel control multiple digital telephony interfaces instead of requiring a separate signaling channel on each one.
example: A carrier uses a shared signaling channel for several ISDN primary-rate spans.

label: Non-fungible tokens
entry_text: A non-fungible token is a uniquely identified digital token recorded on a ledger rather than treated as interchangeable with another token of the same type.
example: A gallery issues distinct tokens associated with items in an edition.
sense_note: A token does not automatically confer ownership of a referenced work or its copyright.

label: NoSQL database
entry_text: A NoSQL database stores and queries data using models such as documents, key-value pairs, columns or graphs rather than relying chiefly on relational tables.
example: A product catalog stores items with different attribute sets as documents.

label: Nutraceuticals
entry_text: Nutraceuticals are foods, food components or related products promoted for health benefits beyond basic nutrition.
example: A researcher evaluates the evidence for a product marketed as a concentrated source of plant compounds.
sense_note: The term is not a uniform regulatory category and does not establish efficacy.

label: Object-oriented data model
entry_text: An object-oriented data model represents data as objects with identities, properties and relationships, often organized into classes.
example: A design system represents a geometric shape and its dimensions as an object in a class hierarchy.

label: Ocular pathology
entry_text: Ocular pathology studies diseases of the eye and related structures through examination of tissues and other diagnostic evidence.
example: A specialist examines an eye tissue sample to characterize abnormal cells.

label: Odor control
entry_text: Odor control aims to prevent or reduce objectionable smells by addressing their sources, transport or perception.
example: A facility encloses a waste-handling area and treats its exhaust to reduce off-site odor.

label: Official statistics
entry_text: Official statistics are figures produced or designated by public authorities under established standards for public use.
example: A statistics agency publishes a monthly unemployment rate based on a household survey.

label: Ohm's law
entry_text: Ohm's law relates voltage, current and resistance as voltage equals current times resistance for an ohmic conductor under stable conditions.
example: A technician calculates the current through a known resistor at a specified voltage.

label: Oil pipelines
entry_text: Oil pipelines transport crude oil or refined petroleum products through connected pipes and pumping facilities.
example: A pipeline moves crude oil from a storage terminal to a refinery.

label: Oncogenomics
entry_text: Oncogenomics studies genomic changes associated with cancer and their effects on disease behavior and treatment response.
example: A research team compares tumor genomes to identify changes recurring in one cancer subtype.

label: Open banking
entry_text: Open banking allows authorized third parties to access banking data or initiate supported services through secure, customer-consented interfaces.
example: A customer permits a budgeting app to read transactions from two bank accounts.
sense_note: The permitted services and consent requirements depend on the framework.

label: Open Network Computing
entry_text: Open Network Computing refers to a suite of distributed computing technologies that includes remote procedure calls and the Network File System.
example: A client uses ONC remote procedure calls to request a file operation from a server.

label: Operating systems
entry_text: An operating system manages hardware and shared resources and provides services for applications.
example: A computer's operating system schedules tasks and controls access to memory and files.

label: Operations, administration, maintenance and provisioning
entry_text: Operations, administration, maintenance and provisioning comprises functions that monitor, manage, repair and configure a telecommunications network or service.
example: An operator monitors service alarms and provisions access for a new subscriber.

label: Optical fiber
entry_text: Optical fiber is a thin transparent strand that guides light along its length for communication or sensing.
example: A fiber transmits light pulses carrying data between network transceivers.

label: Optical fiber cable
entry_text: An optical fiber cable contains protected strands that carry light signals for communication or sensing.
example: A campus network connects buildings with fiber to transmit data over long runs.

label: Optical waveguides
entry_text: Optical waveguides are structures that confine and direct light along a defined path.
example: A photonic chip sends light between its components through a patterned waveguide.

label: Oral hygiene
entry_text: Oral hygiene consists of practices that keep the mouth clean and help prevent dental and gum disease.
example: A person cleans between their teeth to remove plaque missed by brushing.

label: Order of draw
entry_text: Order of draw is the recommended sequence for collecting blood into different specimen tubes to minimize additive carryover.
example: A phlebotomist consults the laboratory's order-of-draw chart before collecting several specimens.

label: Organic composition of capital
entry_text: The organic composition of capital is Marx's concept for the ratio of constant to variable capital insofar as that ratio reflects the technical relationship between means of production and labor power.
example: A political economist uses the concept to examine how mechanization changes the relationship between expenditures on machinery and labor.

label: Organization development
entry_text: Organization development applies planned, evidence-informed interventions to improve how an organization functions and adapts.
example: A facilitator helps several departments diagnose recurring coordination problems and test a new workflow.

label: Organizational change
entry_text: Organizational change is the process by which an organization alters its structure, practices, strategy or culture.
example: A company changes reporting lines and introduces new routines after combining two teams.

label: Outbound logistics
entry_text: Outbound logistics manages the storage, handling and transport of goods from an organization to customers or distribution channels.
example: A retailer consolidates customer orders before dispatching them from a fulfillment center.

label: Outpatient surgery
entry_text: Outpatient surgery is planned to allow the patient to leave without an overnight hospital stay when recovery permits.
example: A surgical center schedules a follow-up after a patient goes home on the day of the procedure.

label: Overhead camshaft engine
entry_text: An overhead camshaft engine places one or more camshafts in the cylinder head to operate the valves.
example: An automotive student compares how single- and dual-overhead-cam layouts actuate valves.

label: Overhead valve engine
entry_text: An overhead valve engine places its valves in the cylinder head and, in common automotive usage, operates them with pushrods from a camshaft in the block.
example: A mechanic identifies a pushrod engine by inspecting the linkage that opens its valves.

label: Oxidation processes
entry_text: Oxidation processes involve loss of electrons or an increase in oxidation state, sometimes through reaction with oxygen.
example: Iron loses electrons as its surface corrodes.

label: Pandemic preparedness
entry_text: Pandemic preparedness is advance planning and capacity building to detect and respond to widespread outbreaks.
example: A public health agency exercises its plan for sharing alerts and maintaining essential services.

label: Parasympathetic nervous system
entry_text: The parasympathetic nervous system is the autonomic division that supports functions such as slowing the heart and promoting digestion.
example: A physiology student explains how parasympathetic activity helps reduce heart rate during rest.

label: Paris Agreement
entry_text: The Paris Agreement is an international climate treaty that organizes collective action through national commitments, reporting and periodic review.
example: A country submits a revised nationally determined contribution describing its emissions goals.

label: Partnership taxation
entry_text: Partnership taxation concerns how tax rules apply to a partnership and how its income, losses and other items are allocated to partners.
example: An accountant checks whether each partner's allocated income matches the applicable partnership agreement and reporting rules.

label: Path to purchase
entry_text: The path to purchase describes the interactions and decisions a buyer goes through before completing a purchase.
example: A retailer examines how product reviews and store visits influence a buyer's final choice.

label: Pathology informatics
entry_text: Pathology informatics applies information systems and data methods to diagnostic pathology and laboratory workflows.
example: A pathology service routes a scanned slide to the correct case in its reporting system.

label: Patient identification and matching
entry_text: Patient identification and matching links records and care events to the correct individual using identifying attributes and verification procedures.
example: A clinic checks for duplicate records when two entries have similar names and dates of birth.

label: Pediatric surgery
entry_text: Pediatric surgery is the specialty concerned with surgical care of infants, children and adolescents.
example: A pediatric surgical team adapts perioperative planning to a young patient's size and development.

label: Pelvic floor
entry_text: The pelvic floor is a group of muscles and connective tissues that supports pelvic organs and contributes to continence and other functions.
example: A physiotherapist diagrams how the pelvic floor supports the bladder.

label: Pelvic health
entry_text: Pelvic health concerns the function and well-being of the pelvic organs and supporting structures.
example: A clinician evaluates whether a pelvic floor disorder is contributing to a patient's symptoms.

label: Penology
entry_text: Penology studies punishment, correctional institutions and approaches to rehabilitation or reintegration.
example: A researcher compares outcomes of community supervision and incarceration for similar cases.

label: Perinatology
entry_text: Perinatology is the medical specialty concerned with high-risk pregnancy and the health of the pregnant patient and fetus around birth.
example: A maternal-fetal medicine specialist monitors a pregnancy complicated by fetal growth concerns.

label: Perioperative care
entry_text: Perioperative care encompasses the preparation, support and monitoring provided before, during and after surgery.
example: A care team verifies a patient's readiness for surgery and monitors recovery afterwards.

label: Personal Communications Service
entry_text: Personal Communications Service refers to mobile wireless voice and data services designated as PCS in telecommunications regulation.
example: A carrier operates cellular service in a licensed PCS band.
sense_note: The frequencies and regulatory scope depend on jurisdiction.

label: Personal income tax
entry_text: Personal income tax is a tax assessed on an individual's taxable income under applicable rules.
example: A taxpayer separates taxable wages from qualifying deductions when preparing a return.

label: Personnel and Human Resources
entry_text: Knowledge of principles and procedures for personnel recruitment, selection, training, compensation and benefits, labor relations and negotiation, and personnel information systems.

label: Pet insurance
entry_text: Pet insurance is coverage that reimburses or pays eligible veterinary or related expenses under a policy.
example: An owner submits a claim for a covered veterinary visit after a pet is injured.

label: Petrography
entry_text: Petrography describes and classifies rocks through close observation of their mineral composition and texture, commonly in thin section.
example: A geologist examines a thin rock slice under polarized light to identify its constituent minerals.

label: Pharmacogenetics
entry_text: Pharmacogenetics studies how inherited genetic differences influence individual responses to medications.
example: Researchers examine whether variation in one gene changes how quickly patients break down a medication.

label: Pharmacoinformatics
entry_text: Pharmacoinformatics applies computational and information methods to data about drugs and their discovery, use or effects.
example: A researcher integrates drug and target records to compare known interactions.
sense_note: Usage spans drug-discovery and clinical-information contexts.

label: Philosophy and Theology
entry_text: Knowledge of different philosophical systems and religions. This includes their basic principles, values, ethics, ways of thinking, customs, practices, and their impact on human culture.

label: Philosophy of religion
entry_text: Philosophy of religion examines concepts and arguments concerning religion, such as faith, divinity and religious experience.
example: A seminar evaluates whether a proposed account of faith requires evidence.

label: Philosophy of science
entry_text: Philosophy of science studies the concepts, methods and assumptions behind scientific inquiry and explanation.
example: A researcher compares how two philosophical accounts distinguish causal explanations from predictions.

label: PHP frameworks
entry_text: PHP frameworks provide reusable libraries and conventions for building PHP applications.
example: A developer uses a framework's routing and request-validation features to build a form service.

label: Physical security
entry_text: Physical security protects people, facilities and physical assets from unauthorized access, damage and other threats.
example: A laboratory uses controlled entry and visitor records to protect secure workspaces.

label: Physics
entry_text: Knowledge and prediction of physical principles, laws, their interrelationships, and applications to understanding fluid, material, and atmospheric dynamics, and mechanical, electrical, atomic and sub-atomic structures and processes.

label: Plastic surgery
entry_text: Plastic surgery is a surgical specialty focused on restoring or reshaping structures of the body for reconstructive or aesthetic purposes.
example: A surgical team reconstructs an area of tissue affected by an injury.

label: Platform as a service
entry_text: Platform as a service provides a managed environment for developing and running applications without administering the underlying infrastructure.
example: A team deploys an application to a managed runtime without setting up its own servers.

label: Police accountability
entry_text: Police accountability comprises mechanisms that require law enforcement agencies and personnel to explain their actions, undergo oversight and address misconduct.
example: An oversight body reviews complaints and publishes findings about recurring procedural problems.

label: Price-to-book ratio
entry_text: The price-to-book ratio compares a company's market equity value with its accounting book value of equity.
example: An analyst compares the ratios of two banks with similar accounting practices.

label: Prisoners' rights
entry_text: Prisoners' rights are legal protections that people retain while incarcerated.
example: An advocate examines whether a prison's access-to-care practices meet applicable legal standards.
sense_note: Specific protections and remedies depend on jurisdiction.

label: Private banking
entry_text: Private banking offers tailored banking and wealth services to clients with substantial assets.
example: A private banker coordinates investment reporting and credit services for a client.

label: Process management (operating systems)
entry_text: Process management is the operating system's creation, scheduling, coordination and termination of running programs.
example: An operating system suspends a process awaiting disk input and schedules another to use the CPU.

label: Process state
entry_text: A process state describes where a running program is in its execution lifecycle, such as ready, running or waiting.
example: A process moves from waiting to ready when an input operation completes.

label: Production and Processing
entry_text: Knowledge of raw materials, production processes, quality control, costs, and other techniques for maximizing the effective manufacture and distribution of goods.

label: Professional negligence in English law
entry_text: Professional negligence in English law concerns a professional's failure to meet a legally required standard of care, causing actionable loss.
example: A court considers whether an adviser acted with the care reasonably expected of someone in that profession.

label: Prosthetic devices
entry_text: Prosthetic devices replace or compensate for a missing body part or function.
example: A prosthetist fits a lower-limb prosthesis to support walking.

label: Protein-protein interaction
entry_text: A protein-protein interaction is a physical association between proteins that can affect their activity, location or stability.
example: A cell signaling study investigates whether two proteins form a complex after stimulation.

label: Psychology
entry_text: Knowledge of human behavior and performance; individual differences in ability, personality, and interests; learning and motivation; psychological research methods; and the assessment and treatment of behavioral and affective disorders.

label: PTAS reduction
entry_text: A PTAS reduction transforms an optimization problem to another so that a polynomial-time approximation scheme for the latter yields one for the former.
example: A researcher uses a PTAS reduction to transfer evidence of approximation difficulty between optimization problems.
sense_note: Formal definitions and notation vary; the key property is preservation of approximation-scheme existence.

label: Public history
entry_text: Public history interprets and presents historical evidence with or for audiences outside specialist scholarship.
example: A museum works with local residents to create an exhibit from oral histories and archival records.

label: Public-key cryptography
entry_text: Public-key cryptography uses paired public and private keys for functions such as encryption, digital signatures or secure key establishment.
example: A recipient verifies a software publisher's digital signature using the publisher's public key.

label: Public policy
entry_text: Public policy comprises choices and rules made by public institutions to address collective problems or pursue public goals.
example: A city evaluates a fare policy designed to make public transit more affordable.

label: Public Safety and Security
entry_text: Knowledge of relevant equipment, policies, procedures, and strategies to promote effective local, state, or national security operations for the protection of people, data, property, and institutions.

label: Quantitative models of the action potential
entry_text: Quantitative models of the action potential use mathematical equations to describe how membrane voltage changes as ions move across an excitable cell membrane.
example: A simulation illustrates how voltage-dependent currents give rise to a spike.

label: Quantum dot
entry_text: A quantum dot is a nanoscale material structure in which charge carriers are confined in all three spatial dimensions, yielding discrete energy levels.
example: A display uses quantum dots of different sizes to produce distinct colors.

label: Quantum Merlin Arthur
entry_text: Quantum Merlin Arthur is a complexity class for decision problems whose yes instances have a quantum witness accepted with bounded error by an efficient quantum verifier, while no instances do not.
example: Researchers classify the local Hamiltonian problem by asking what a quantum verifier can establish from a supplied quantum state.

label: Quantum spin Hall effect
entry_text: The quantum spin Hall effect is a topological phase with an insulating bulk and conducting edge states linked to electron spin and protected by time-reversal symmetry.
example: In a suitable two-dimensional material, researchers look for conduction along the sample's edges while its interior is insulating.

label: Quartile
entry_text: A quartile is one of three cut points dividing ordered data into four parts based on cumulative proportion.
example: A salary summary reports the median, or second quartile, together with the first and third quartiles.
sense_note: Sample calculation conventions differ.

label: Queer theory
entry_text: Queer theory examines how norms and institutions shape categories of sexuality and gender and how those categories are challenged.
example: A scholar analyzes how a film presents some relationships as ordinary and others as departures from a norm.

label: Question answering
entry_text: Question answering is the computational task of producing a response to a question using available information.
example: A support system retrieves a policy passage and uses it to answer a question about returns.

label: Rail safety
entry_text: Rail safety comprises rules, engineering controls and operating practices that reduce harm in rail transport.
example: A railway investigates near misses at crossings to improve warning systems.

label: Railway signalling
entry_text: Railway signalling uses signals and control systems to authorize train movements and maintain safe separation.
example: An interlocking prevents incompatible routes from being set through the same junction.

label: Random variable
entry_text: A random variable assigns a numerical value to each outcome of a random experiment according to a specified rule.
example: A random variable counts the number of heads in three coin flips.

label: Rankine cycle
entry_text: The Rankine cycle is a vapor power cycle in which a working fluid is pumped, heated, expanded to produce work and condensed for reuse.
example: An engineer uses the cycle to model a steam power plant's conversion of heat into shaft work.

label: Real estate
entry_text: Real estate is land and generally the permanent structures or improvements attached to it.
example: A valuation considers both the parcel and the building on it.

label: Real estate contracts
entry_text: Real estate contracts are agreements creating obligations around property transactions such as sale, purchase or leasing.
example: A purchase contract identifies the property, price and conditions that must be met before closing.

label: Real estate owned
entry_text: Real estate owned typically refers to property held by a lender after foreclosure or another transfer following borrower default.
example: A lender lists a foreclosed property in its real estate owned inventory.

label: Real-time payments
entry_text: Real-time payments are electronic transfers designed to make funds available to recipients within seconds or nearly so, typically around the clock.
example: A customer sends a payment that appears in the recipient's bank balance moments later.

label: Receptive and expressive language
entry_text: Receptive language is the ability to understand language, while expressive language is the ability to communicate meaning through language.
example: A clinician separately assesses whether a child follows spoken directions and can describe an event.

label: Reference range
entry_text: A reference range is an interval of laboratory values established for a defined reference population using a specified test method.
example: A laboratory reports which reference interval was used to interpret a blood test.
sense_note: A reference range is not necessarily a diagnostic or treatment threshold.

label: Refrigeration
entry_text: Refrigeration removes heat from a space or substance and transfers it elsewhere to lower or maintain its temperature.
example: A cold room moves heat outdoors to keep stored produce cool.

label: Refrigeration compressors
entry_text: A refrigeration compressor raises the pressure of refrigerant vapor and moves it through the vapor-compression cycle.
example: A heat pump’s compressor sends high-pressure refrigerant vapor toward the condenser.

label: Refugee issues
entry_text: Refugee issues concern displacement, protection and access to services or long-term solutions for people who flee their countries.
example: A policy team examines barriers refugees face when enrolling in local schools.

label: Registered Education Savings Plan
entry_text: A Registered Education Savings Plan is a Canadian registered savings arrangement for education expenses, potentially eligible for government grants or bonds.
example: A family opens an RESP to save for a beneficiary's postsecondary education.

label: Regulation SHO
entry_text: Regulation SHO is a U.S. securities regulation governing short-sale practices, including locating securities and addressing failures to deliver.
example: A broker reviews its short-sale procedures against applicable locate and close-out requirements.

label: Rehabilitation
entry_text: Rehabilitation supports people in improving or maintaining function and participation after injury, illness or another change in capacity.
example: A therapist helps a person practice daily tasks after a stroke.
sense_note: The label can also refer to legal, social or environmental restoration; the health sense is used here.

label: Reinforced masonry
entry_text: Reinforced masonry uses embedded steel or other reinforcement to help masonry carry loads it cannot readily resist on its own.
example: An engineer specifies reinforced concrete-block walls to resist lateral loads.

label: Relational database management system
entry_text: A relational database management system stores data in related tables and provides mechanisms to query, update and enforce constraints on them.
example: A retail database connects orders to customer records using a foreign key.

label: Renal nutrition
entry_text: Renal nutrition concerns dietary needs and dietary management associated with kidney disease or impaired kidney function.
example: A renal dietitian tailors a meal plan to a patient's lab results and treatment stage.

label: Renewable energy
entry_text: Renewable energy comes from sources naturally replenished on human timescales, such as sunlight, wind or flowing water.
example: A community generates electricity from wind turbines.

label: Reproductive health care
entry_text: Reproductive health care includes services that support reproductive well-being and informed decisions about contraception, fertility, pregnancy and related needs.
example: A clinic provides counseling to help patients compare contraceptive options.

label: Research methodology
entry_text: Research methodology is the rationale and design for how evidence will be collected, analyzed and interpreted to answer a research question.
example: A researcher explains why interviews are suitable for studying how participants understand a policy.

label: Residential construction
entry_text: Residential construction is the work of building, altering or repairing structures intended for people to live in.
example: A contractor coordinates framing and inspection for a new house.

label: Rights issue
entry_text: A rights issue offers existing shareholders the right to buy new shares, typically in proportion to their current holdings.
example: A shareholder decides whether to exercise rights to subscribe for newly issued shares.

label: Risk ratings
entry_text: Risk ratings classify assessed risk into numerical scores or categories using specified criteria.
example: A lender assigns exposures to risk tiers for review and monitoring.
sense_note: Criteria depend on the domain and rating scheme.

label: Rolling stock
entry_text: Rolling stock comprises wheeled vehicles that run on a railway, including locomotives, passenger cars and freight wagons.
example: A transit authority inventories trainsets before planning replacement purchases.

label: Rubber-tyred metro
entry_text: A rubber-tyred metro is an urban rail system whose vehicles use rubber tires on dedicated rolling surfaces, typically with separate guideways or guidance rails.
example: A transport engineer compares the climbing performance of rubber-tyred trains and steel-wheel trains.

label: Sales and Marketing
entry_text: Knowledge of principles and methods for showing, promoting, and selling products or services. This includes marketing strategy and tactics, product demonstration, sales techniques, and sales control systems.

label: Sales journal
entry_text: A sales journal records sales transactions in chronological order, often specifically credit sales in a specialized accounting ledger.
example: A bookkeeper posts the month's credit sales total to the general ledger.

label: SCARA robot
entry_text: A SCARA robot is an industrial robot with a selectively compliant articulated arm suited to fast positioning in a horizontal plane and vertical insertion.
example: An assembly line uses a SCARA robot to place small parts into a fixture.

label: Scholarship of teaching and learning
entry_text: The scholarship of teaching and learning is systematic inquiry into teaching and student learning whose methods and findings are made available for scrutiny and use.
example: An instructor studies the effect of a classroom activity and shares the results with other educators.

label: Secured transactions
entry_text: Secured transactions are arrangements in which a debtor grants an interest in collateral to secure payment or performance of an obligation.
example: A lender takes a security interest in equipment purchased with a business loan.

label: Smart buildings
entry_text: Smart buildings use networked sensors and controls to monitor and coordinate building systems.
example: An office building adjusts ventilation using occupancy and air-quality measurements.

label: Smart lighting
entry_text: Smart lighting uses sensors, programmable controls or connectivity to adjust lighting automatically or remotely.
example: A corridor lowers its lighting level when no movement is detected.

label: Smart meter systems
entry_text: Smart meter systems measure utility consumption and communicate readings electronically for billing, monitoring or service management.
example: An electric utility uses interval readings to analyze when demand peaks.

label: Social determinants of health
entry_text: Social determinants of health are the social and economic conditions in which people live and work that shape health outcomes.
example: A health department studies how housing instability affects continuity of care.

label: Social impact bond
entry_text: A social impact bond is an outcomes-based financing arrangement in which private or philanthropic investors fund a service and repayment depends on agreed results.
example: Investors fund a housing-support program whose public payments depend on independently measured outcomes.
sense_note: Despite the name, it need not be a conventional tradable bond.

label: Social sustainability
entry_text: Social sustainability concerns maintaining equitable and inclusive social conditions that support long-term well-being.
example: A transit plan assesses whether affordable access can be maintained across neighborhoods.

label: Sociology and Anthropology
entry_text: Knowledge of group behavior and dynamics, societal trends and influences, human migrations, ethnicity, cultures, and their history and origins.

label: Sociology of education
entry_text: The sociology of education studies how schooling and other learning institutions shape and are shaped by social relationships, culture and inequality.
example: A researcher examines how school placement practices affect opportunities across social groups.

label: Software as a service
entry_text: Software as a service delivers provider-managed applications over a network for customers to use without installing and operating the full software stack themselves.
example: A company uses a hosted customer-management application available through a browser.

label: Software-defined WAN
entry_text: Software-defined WAN uses centrally managed policies and software to route traffic across multiple wide-area network links.
example: A branch sends real-time calls over whichever available connection meets its latency policy.

label: Software engineering
entry_text: Software engineering applies systematic methods to designing, building, testing and maintaining software systems.
example: A team uses versioned builds and automated regression tests to modify a payment application safely.

label: Sovereign cloud
entry_text: A sovereign cloud is a cloud offering designed to satisfy specified sovereignty constraints on data, operations and legal jurisdiction.
example: A public agency evaluates where data is stored and who can administer the cloud services it uses.
sense_note: Requirements differ by jurisdiction and procurement context.

label: Special education
entry_text: Special education provides specially designed instruction and supports responsive to the learning needs of students with disabilities.
example: A school adapts materials and delivery to help a student meet an individualized reading goal.

label: Special education law
entry_text: Special education law governs rights, responsibilities, procedures and services relating to education for learners with disabilities.
example: A school reviews whether its reevaluation process meets applicable requirements.

label: Special hazards suppression systems
entry_text: Special hazards suppression systems are fire suppression systems designed for hazards, equipment or environments that require tailored agents or designs.
example: A facility assesses a dedicated suppression system for an enclosure containing sensitive electronics.

label: Special use airspace
entry_text: Special use airspace is airspace designated for activities that may require restrictions or advisories for other aircraft.
example: A pilot checks current information about a restricted area when planning a route.

label: Sport governance
entry_text: Sport governance concerns how sports organizations make decisions, regulate participation and ensure accountability.
example: A federation defines an independent appeals process for eligibility rulings.

label: Standard ambient temperature and pressure
entry_text: Standard ambient temperature and pressure is a reference condition commonly specified as 25 degrees Celsius and 100 kilopascals.
example: A chemistry problem states that gas properties are reported at SATP so the comparison uses the same reference conditions.
sense_note: Check the stated convention, especially when comparing it with STP or other reference conditions.

label: Static HTML
entry_text: Static HTML is markup delivered as a pre-existing document rather than generated for each individual request.
example: A site serves a published article as the same HTML document to every visitor.

label: Statistics
entry_text: Statistics develops methods for collecting, summarizing, analyzing and interpreting data under variability and uncertainty.
example: An analyst uses sampling data to estimate the prevalence of a defect with an uncertainty interval.

label: Stormwater collection systems
entry_text: Stormwater collection systems capture and convey runoff from surfaces to storage, treatment or a receiving outlet.
example: A site directs runoff from paved areas through inlets and pipes to a detention basin.

label: Student development theory
entry_text: Student development theory comprises frameworks for understanding how students change intellectually, psychosocially or in identity during education.
example: An adviser uses a developmental framework to design reflection exercises for first-year students.

label: Subordination, Non-Disturbance and Attornment Agreement
entry_text: A Subordination, Non-Disturbance and Attornment Agreement sets the priority of a lease relative to a lender's interest and defines possession and tenancy obligations following foreclosure.
example: A commercial tenant negotiates continued occupancy after foreclosure if it remains in compliance with its lease.

label: Surface properties of transition metal oxides
entry_text: Surface properties of transition metal oxides concern how the composition, structure and electronic state at their surfaces affect interactions such as adsorption and reactivity.
example: A materials scientist compares how oxygen vacancies influence adsorption on two oxide surfaces.

label: Surgery
entry_text: Surgery treats, investigates or reconstructs parts of the body through operative procedures.
example: A surgical team repairs damaged tissue in a planned operation.

label: Sustainability bond
entry_text: A sustainability bond is debt whose proceeds fund eligible projects combining environmental and social objectives.
example: An issuer earmarks proceeds for renewable energy and affordable housing.
sense_note: Distinguish from a sustainability-linked bond, whose financial terms are tied to performance targets.

label: Sustainable infrastructure
entry_text: Sustainable infrastructure is infrastructure planned, built and operated to meet service needs while accounting for long-term environmental, social and economic effects.
example: A city compares drainage options using flood resilience, maintenance costs and public benefits over their lifetimes.

label: Sustainable insurance
entry_text: Sustainable insurance incorporates environmental, social and governance considerations into insurance activities such as underwriting, products or investment decisions.
example: An insurer evaluates how future flood conditions could affect property risk and access to coverage.

label: Syndicated finance
entry_text: Syndicated finance arranges financing through a group of lenders or investors that share a transaction's funding and risk.
example: Several banks jointly provide a credit facility that would be large for one lender to fund alone.

label: Tax deduction
entry_text: A tax deduction is an amount allowed to reduce the base on which tax is calculated, rather than directly reducing the tax owed.
example: An allowable business expense reduces taxable profit before tax is calculated.

label: Tax return
entry_text: A tax return is a filing that reports information used to calculate, reconcile or disclose tax obligations for a reporting period.
example: A worker files an annual return showing income and taxes already withheld.

label: Tax shelter
entry_text: A tax shelter is an investment or arrangement intended to reduce or defer tax liability.
example: An analyst distinguishes a legally recognized tax-favored arrangement from an abusive shelter.
sense_note: The term covers arrangements with differing legal status.

label: Technical theatre
entry_text: Technical theatre encompasses the practical design and operation of stage elements such as scenery, lighting, sound and effects.
example: A backstage crew coordinates lighting and sound cues with scene changes.

label: Technology entrepreneurship
entry_text: Technology entrepreneurship identifies commercial or social opportunities and builds ventures around technically enabled products or services.
example: A founding team tests whether clinics need its scheduling prototype before committing to a product launch.

label: Telecommunications
entry_text: Knowledge of transmission, broadcasting, switching, control, and operation of telecommunications systems.

label: Theatrical techniques
entry_text: Theatrical techniques are methods performers and production teams use to convey a story, direct attention or shape an audience's experience on stage.
example: A director uses a freeze in movement to draw attention to a key line.

label: Therapy and Counseling
entry_text: Knowledge of principles, methods, and procedures for diagnosis, treatment, and rehabilitation of physical and mental dysfunctions, and for career counseling and guidance.

label: Thyroid cancer
entry_text: Thyroid cancer is a malignant growth originating in thyroid tissue.
example: A cancer registry classifies a tumor arising from thyroid follicular cells as a thyroid cancer.

label: Thyroid diseases and disorders
entry_text: Thyroid diseases and disorders affect the thyroid gland's structure or its production of hormones that regulate metabolism.
example: A clinician investigates whether a patient's symptoms reflect inadequate thyroid hormone production.

label: TL 9000
entry_text: TL 9000 is a quality management framework for the information and communications technology industry that adds sector-specific requirements and performance measurements to ISO 9001.
example: A telecommunications equipment supplier tracks defect and reliability indicators as part of its TL 9000 quality program.

label: Trace (linear algebra)
entry_text: In linear algebra, the trace of a square matrix is the sum of its main diagonal entries.
example: The trace of a diagonal matrix with entries two and five is seven.

label: Transportation
entry_text: Knowledge of principles and methods for moving people or goods by air, rail, sea, or road, including the relative costs and benefits.

label: Traumatic brain injury
entry_text: A traumatic brain injury is a disruption of brain function or structural injury to the brain caused by an external force.
example: A clinician evaluates a person for a brain injury after a fall followed by confusion.

label: Twisted pair
entry_text: Twisted pair is a cable construction in which two insulated conductors are wound around each other to reduce electromagnetic interference.
example: An Ethernet installation uses twisted pairs to transmit signals between devices.

label: Urban resilience
entry_text: Urban resilience is the capacity of a city and its communities to anticipate, withstand, adapt to and recover from disruptions.
example: A coastal city designs alternate routes and emergency services to remain functional during floods.

label: Urban sustainability
entry_text: Urban sustainability concerns meeting a city's social and economic needs while limiting long-term environmental harm and resource depletion.
example: A city pairs transit investment with affordable housing near stations to reduce dependence on private cars.

label: Urological disorders
entry_text: Urological disorders affect the urinary tract or the male reproductive organs.
example: A urology service evaluates a patient with recurring kidney stones.

label: Use of force
entry_text: Use of force concerns the application of physical compulsion and the legal, ethical and organizational standards that govern it.
example: An oversight team assesses whether the force documented in an incident complied with policy.
sense_note: The relevant standards depend on the setting and jurisdiction.

label: Utility engineering
entry_text: Utility engineering concerns the design, construction and operation of infrastructure that provides services such as power, water, gas or communications.
example: Engineers coordinate water and electrical routes before a street reconstruction.

label: Utility frequency
entry_text: Utility frequency is the nominal rate at which alternating current cycles in an electrical power grid.
example: A motor specification identifies whether it is intended for a 50-hertz or 60-hertz supply.

label: VA loans
entry_text: VA loans are mortgages that eligible borrowers can obtain with backing from the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs.
example: A lender checks whether a prospective homeowner qualifies under the VA home loan program.

label: Virtual health
entry_text: Virtual health provides healthcare services or support remotely through digital communication and monitoring technologies.
example: A patient meets a clinician by video for a follow-up appointment.

label: Virtual LAN
entry_text: A virtual LAN logically segments devices into separate data-link networks even when they share physical switching equipment.
example: An office places guest devices and employee computers in different VLANs on the same switch infrastructure.

label: Virtual private network
entry_text: A virtual private network extends private connectivity over a shared network using logical tunnels, commonly protected by encryption.
example: A worker uses a VPN to access internal company resources from a remote location.

label: Virtual reality
entry_text: Virtual reality presents an immersive computer-generated environment that can respond to a user's viewpoint or actions.
example: A trainee uses a headset to practice navigating a simulated facility.

label: Visual impairment education
entry_text: Visual impairment education adapts instruction and materials for learners who are blind or have low vision.
example: A teacher provides tactile diagrams and accessible text for a geometry lesson.

label: Wage and hour laws
entry_text: Wage and hour laws govern matters such as minimum wages, compensable time, overtime and recordkeeping.
example: A payroll team checks whether a work schedule generates overtime under the applicable rules.

label: Warehouse automation
entry_text: Warehouse automation uses machines and software to perform or coordinate warehouse tasks with less manual intervention.
example: An automated storage system retrieves a tote and delivers it to a packing station.

label: Wave phase

example: A travel organizer checks whether a planned flight-inclusive package falls within the ATOL scheme.

label: Ajax
entry_text: Ajax is a web development technique in which a browser exchanges data with a server without reloading the entire page.
