example: A search box updates its suggestions while a visitor types.

label: ÄKTA
entry_text: ÄKTA is a family of liquid chromatography systems used to separate and purify biomolecules.
example: A laboratory technician reviews chromatograms from an ÄKTA purification run.

label: Aldus PhotoStyler
entry_text: Aldus PhotoStyler was a raster graphics editor for editing and retouching photographs on personal computers.
example: A graphic artist adjusts the color of a scanned image before placing it in a publication.

label: Alexa Internet
entry_text: Alexa Internet was a web analytics service that reported website traffic estimates and popularity rankings.
example: A researcher compares archived site rankings while noting that they are estimates rather than direct traffic counts.

label: Algorithm analysis
entry_text: Algorithm analysis examines the correctness and resource requirements of an algorithm as its inputs or assumptions vary.
example: An engineer compares the memory needs of two approaches to sorting a dataset.

label: Alibaba Cloud
entry_text: Alibaba Cloud provides managed computing, storage, networking, and other cloud infrastructure services.
example: A developer deploys an application on virtual servers and stores its backups in object storage.

label: AlienVault
entry_text: AlienVault refers to security monitoring and threat-intelligence products used to collect and correlate defensive security data.
example: An operations team combines logs from several systems to review suspicious account activity.
sense_note: The name can refer to the company or its products, including Unified Security Management.

label: All-terrain vehicle
entry_text: An all-terrain vehicle is a motorized vehicle designed for travel over rough or unpaved ground.
example: A land steward uses a suitable ATV to inspect a remote access road.

label: Allergen labelling
entry_text: Allergen labelling flags ingredients or cross-contact risks that may cause allergic reactions.
example: A food manufacturer checks that a product label identifies the relevant allergens in its recipe.

label: AllJoyn
entry_text: AllJoyn was an open interoperability framework that allowed connected devices to discover and communicate with one another.
example: A home control app discovers a compatible device on a local network.

label: AlloyUI
entry_text: AlloyUI is a web interface framework built on YUI that provides reusable JavaScript components.
example: A maintainer updates the date picker in an older portal that uses AlloyUI.

label: Allyship
entry_text: Allyship is the practice of using one’s position and actions to support people facing exclusion or unequal treatment.
example: A meeting facilitator credits an overlooked colleague’s proposal and makes space for them to explain it.

label: Alooma
entry_text: Alooma was a managed data integration platform for moving data from multiple sources into analytical destinations.
example: A data engineer synchronizes application events and customer records to a data warehouse.

label: Alternative dispute resolution
entry_text: Alternative dispute resolution uses mechanisms such as mediation and arbitration to address disputes outside ordinary court proceedings.
example: Two parties ask a neutral mediator to help them negotiate a settlement.

label: Alternative Transients Program
entry_text: The Alternative Transients Program simulates electromagnetic transient behavior in electrical power systems.
example: A power engineer models the voltage transient following a switching operation.

label: Aluminium smelting
entry_text: Aluminium smelting produces metallic aluminium by electrolytically reducing alumina dissolved in a molten bath.
example: A process engineer tracks electricity use at an aluminium smelter.

label: Amazon AppStream 2.0
entry_text: Amazon AppStream 2.0 streams remotely hosted desktop applications to users without requiring a local installation of each application.
example: A university lets students use a licensed design tool through streamed sessions.

label: Amazon CloudWatch
entry_text: Amazon CloudWatch collects operational metrics, logs, and events and can alert on monitored conditions.
example: An operations team sets an alarm for an unexpectedly high error rate.

label: Amazon EMR
entry_text: Amazon EMR manages infrastructure for distributed data processing frameworks such as Apache Spark.
example: A team processes daily event files with Spark and writes summarized results to object storage.

label: Amazon Fire tablet
entry_text: An Amazon Fire tablet is a touchscreen device that runs Fire OS and supports apps and media consumption.
example: A tester checks that an interactive reading app displays correctly on a Fire tablet.

label: Amazon SageMaker
entry_text: Amazon SageMaker is a set of managed cloud tools for building, training, deploying, and operating machine-learning models.
example: An engineer evaluates a trained classifier before exposing it through a managed inference endpoint.

label: Amazon SimpleDB
entry_text: Amazon SimpleDB is a managed nonrelational data store that organizes records as items with named attributes.
example: A small application queries stored product items by a category attribute.

label: amCharts
entry_text: amCharts is a JavaScript library for creating interactive charts and geographic visualizations on the web.
example: A publisher gives readers an interactive line chart of historical temperatures.

label: American Welding Society codes
entry_text: American Welding Society codes define technical requirements for welding work within their specified scopes.
example: A welding inspector consults the applicable code when reviewing structural weld acceptance.

label: Amiga
entry_text: Amiga refers to a family of personal computers known for their multimedia capabilities and the associated Amiga platform.
example: A preservation team tests whether an archived graphics program runs in a matching Amiga environment.

label: AMX programming
entry_text: AMX programming configures and writes control logic for AMX systems that coordinate audiovisual equipment and room controls.
example: An integrator programs a touch-panel selection to switch a conference room’s display source.
sense_note: The intended sense is audiovisual control, not Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions.

label: Anaconda
entry_text: Anaconda is a distribution and package-management ecosystem for Python and R workflows, particularly data science.
example: A scientist installs a project’s dependencies in an isolated conda environment.

label: Analysis of variance
entry_text: Analysis of variance is a statistical method that compares sources of variability to test hypotheses about differences in group means.
example: A researcher tests whether mean yield differs across several treatments.

label: Anaplan
entry_text: Anaplan is a cloud planning platform that links business data, forecasts, and scenarios across departments.
example: A retailer updates a demand forecast and checks its effect on staffing and cash plans.

label: Android app development
entry_text: Android app development builds, tests, and maintains applications that run on Android devices.
example: A developer implements an offline mode and tests it on phones with different screen sizes.

label: Android UI development
entry_text: Android UI development designs and implements the screens, controls, and interaction behavior of Android applications.
example: A developer builds an accessible sign-in screen that adapts to portrait and landscape displays.

label: Anglo-American Cataloguing Rules
entry_text: The Anglo-American Cataloguing Rules prescribe how to describe library materials and select access points in catalog records.
example: A cataloguer prepares a record that makes a book discoverable under its author and title.

label: Angular
entry_text: Angular is a TypeScript-based framework for building web applications with components, declarative templates, and dependency injection.
example: A development team creates a dashboard whose components share a data service.

label: Angular CLI
entry_text: Angular CLI is a command-line tool for generating, building, testing, and maintaining Angular projects.
example: A developer generates an Angular component with a matching test file.

label: AngularJS
entry_text: AngularJS is the original JavaScript-based Angular framework that links HTML templates to application data and behavior through directives and binding.
example: A maintainer updates a form in a legacy AngularJS application.
sense_note: This is the earlier 1.x framework, not Angular 2 or later.

label: Anim8or
entry_text: Anim8or is a desktop application for polygonal 3D modeling and character animation.
example: An animator creates a simple model and poses it across keyframes.

label: Animated explainer video production
entry_text: Animated explainer video production uses scripted narration and moving visuals to teach or explain a topic.
example: An instructional team animates a parcel’s route to explain a warehouse’s fulfillment process.

label: Anma massage
entry_text: Anma is a Japanese massage tradition using manual pressure, kneading, and related bodywork techniques.
example: A practitioner explains what an Anma session involves before agreeing on areas to address.

label: Antics3D
entry_text: Antics3D was a 3D animation and previsualization application for staging scenes with characters, sets, and camera moves.
example: A film planner blocks a scene and checks the planned camera framing before shooting.

label: Antivirus software
entry_text: Antivirus software identifies and helps contain malicious programs or files through scanning and monitoring.
example: An endpoint agent quarantines a flagged attachment so a security team can review it.

label: Apache Airflow
entry_text: Apache Airflow orchestrates scheduled or triggered workflows whose tasks and dependencies are defined as directed acyclic graphs.
example: A data engineer makes a reporting task wait for two source extracts to complete.

label: Apache Ambari
entry_text: Apache Ambari is a tool for provisioning, managing, and monitoring Hadoop cluster services.
example: An administrator checks the health of distributed storage services across cluster nodes.

label: Apache Ant
entry_text: Apache Ant is a Java-based build automation tool that executes targets and tasks commonly declared in XML.
example: A maintainer builds an application and packages the result using its existing Ant build file.

label: Apache Archiva
entry_text: Apache Archiva manages repositories of software build artifacts, particularly for Maven-based projects.
example: A build team serves approved dependency versions from an internal repository.

label: Apache Beam
entry_text: Apache Beam defines batch and streaming data pipelines through a unified model that runs on supported processing back ends.
example: An engineer uses the same transformation logic for historical records and newly arriving events.

label: Apache Cassandra
entry_text: Apache Cassandra is a distributed wide-column database designed to store and serve large datasets across multiple nodes.
example: A service stores device readings by device identifier and time window.

label: Apache Cocoon
entry_text: Apache Cocoon is a web application framework that processes and transforms content through pipelines, historically centered on XML.
example: A publisher transforms structured documents into web pages using a series of content-processing stages.

label: Apache Giraph
entry_text: Apache Giraph is a distributed graph-processing framework that runs iterative computations over graph vertices and edges.
example: An analyst computes connected components in a large relationship network.

label: Apache Gump
entry_text: Apache Gump is a continuous integration system that builds related open-source projects to detect dependency and compatibility problems.
example: A project maintainer sees that a change in an upstream library breaks a downstream build.

label: Apache Jena
entry_text: Apache Jena is a Java framework for RDF data, SPARQL queries, and semantic-web applications.
example: A research team queries a graph of collections and the people connected to them.

label: Apache jUDDI
entry_text: Apache jUDDI is a Java implementation of the UDDI registry standard for publishing and discovering web services.
example: An enterprise maintains a searchable registry of service descriptions for internal applications.

label: Apache Karaf
entry_text: Apache Karaf is a modular Java runtime for deploying and managing OSGi applications and related components.
example: An operator enables a packaged feature without rebuilding the surrounding application runtime.

label: Apache Lenya
entry_text: Apache Lenya is a web content-management system built around XML documents and publication workflows.
example: An editor reviews and publishes a structured article through the site’s approval process.

label: Apache Mahout
entry_text: Apache Mahout provides scalable mathematical and machine-learning tools for processing large datasets.
example: An analyst applies distributed computation to a large feature matrix.

label: Apache Mesos
entry_text: Apache Mesos manages and allocates shared compute resources to distributed workload frameworks.
example: A cluster operator runs multiple processing frameworks on a common pool of machines.

label: Apache NiFi
entry_text: Apache NiFi designs and operates data flows for moving, routing, and transforming data between systems.
example: A team routes incoming sensor records to different destinations according to their source.

label: Apache ObJectRelationalBridge
entry_text: Apache ObJectRelationalBridge is a Java object-relational mapping tool for persisting object data in relational databases.
example: A maintainer maps an application’s order objects to tables without writing SQL for every save.

label: Apache OFBiz
entry_text: Apache OFBiz is a framework and suite of enterprise applications for functions such as order management, accounting, and commerce.
example: A retailer connects its product catalog and fulfillment records in a shared system.

label: Apache OpenEJB
entry_text: Apache OpenEJB is an implementation of the Enterprise JavaBeans container specification for running enterprise Java components.
example: A developer runs transaction-aware application services in an embedded container during tests.

label: Apache OpenNLP
entry_text: Apache OpenNLP is a Java toolkit for common statistical natural language processing tasks such as tokenization and named entity recognition.
example: A developer identifies person and organization names in a collection of articles.

label: Apache PDFBox
entry_text: Apache PDFBox is a Java library for creating, reading, and manipulating PDF documents.
example: A developer extracts searchable text from incoming PDF forms.

label: Apache PredictionIO
entry_text: Apache PredictionIO was a platform for building and deploying machine-learning prediction services.
example: A team wraps a recommendation model as an application-facing prediction service.

label: Apache Spark
entry_text: Apache Spark is a distributed computation engine for large-scale data processing and analytics.
example: A team aggregates months of event records across a cluster.

label: Apache Tiles
entry_text: Apache Tiles is a Java web presentation framework for composing pages from reusable layout fragments.
example: A team shares navigation and footer fragments across several web pages.

label: Apache TinkerPop
entry_text: Apache TinkerPop is a graph computing framework that defines common interfaces and the Gremlin traversal language.
example: A developer uses Gremlin to find connections between people and projects.

label: API design
entry_text: API design defines an interface’s operations, data contracts, and behavior so callers can use it reliably.
example: A team specifies how an orders API responds to duplicate requests and invalid input.

label: API gateway
entry_text: An API gateway is an entry point that routes API requests and can apply common controls before forwarding them to back-end services.
example: A gateway authenticates a request before routing it to the product service.

label: API management
entry_text: API management governs the publication, access, monitoring, and evolution of APIs across their lifecycle.
example: A platform team tracks usage and communicates the retirement date of an old API version.

label: Apollo GraphQL
entry_text: Apollo GraphQL is a set of tools for building, consuming, and operating GraphQL APIs.
example: A web app uses Apollo Client to fetch and cache data for its account page.

label: Appian
entry_text: Appian is a low-code software platform for building workflow and process applications.
example: An operations team creates a claims review workflow with different steps for intake and approval.

label: Apple Device Enrollment Program
entry_text: Apple Device Enrollment Program was an Apple service for automating institutional enrollment of eligible devices into mobile device management.
example: A school sets up new iPads to enroll automatically during initial setup.
sense_note: The historical DEP label should not be used interchangeably with every current Apple device management service.

label: Apple Numbers
entry_text: Apple Numbers is a spreadsheet application for working with tables, formulas, and charts on Apple platforms.
example: A household builds a monthly spending sheet with a chart that updates as entries change.

label: appletviewer
entry_text: appletviewer was a Java development tool for running and testing Java applets without opening a browser.
example: A maintainer tests an archived applet in an isolated legacy Java environment.

label: Application delivery controller
entry_text: An application delivery controller manages network traffic to applications and commonly provides load balancing, health checks, and protocol termination.
example: A controller stops routing requests to an application server that fails its health checks.

label: Application monitoring
entry_text: Application monitoring collects signals about software performance, availability, and errors to detect and investigate failures.
example: An operator traces rising response times to one slow database call.

label: Applied element method
entry_text: The applied element method represents a structure as elements connected by springs to model deformation, separation, and collapse.
example: An engineer uses the method to examine how a damaged frame redistributes loads.

label: Applixware
entry_text: Applixware was an office suite for Unix-like systems that included document, spreadsheet, and presentation tools.
example: An archivist opens an old Applixware spreadsheet in a compatible environment to recover its data.

label: AppsFlyer
entry_text: AppsFlyer is a marketing measurement platform that relates app installations and events to acquisition campaigns.
example: A marketing team compares the reported installs attributed to two ad campaigns.

label: AppSheet
entry_text: AppSheet is a low-code platform for building applications and automations over existing data sources.
example: A maintenance team turns a spreadsheet of inspection records into a mobile form.

label: Apptio
entry_text: Apptio provides business-management software for analyzing technology costs and relating spending to services and organizational units.
example: A finance partner allocates cloud spending across product teams for review.

label: apxs
entry_text: apxs is an Apache HTTP Server tool for compiling and installing extension modules as shared objects.
example: A server maintainer rebuilds an existing module for a compatible Apache installation.

label: Arachnophilia
entry_text: Arachnophilia is a text-based web authoring editor with tools for writing and editing HTML.
example: A site maintainer updates hand-written markup in an archived page.

label: ArangoDB
entry_text: ArangoDB is a multi-model database that supports documents, key-value access, and graphs in one system.
example: A service stores customer profiles as documents and queries links between related accounts.

label: Araxis Merge
entry_text: Araxis Merge is a visual tool for comparing and merging files or directory trees.
example: A developer reconciles conflicting edits to a configuration file.

label: Architectural rendering
entry_text: Architectural rendering creates a visual depiction of a building or space from drawings or a digital model.
example: A designer produces a view showing how an interior would look in afternoon light.

label: Architectural visualization
entry_text: Architectural visualization communicates built-environment designs through representations such as images, diagrams, walkthroughs, or interactive models.
example: A design team uses a walkthrough to help clients understand movement through a proposed library.
sense_note: This broader practice includes rendering rather than being identical to it.

label: ArcSight Enterprise Security Manager
entry_text: ArcSight Enterprise Security Manager collects and correlates security events to support monitoring and incident investigation.
example: A security analyst reviews correlated authentication events across several approved systems.

label: Areca Backup
entry_text: Areca Backup is a file backup tool that manages backup sets and restoration across supported storage destinations.
example: A user restores an older version of an accidentally overwritten project file.

label: Argo CD
entry_text: Argo CD is a GitOps delivery tool that compares Kubernetes deployments with declared configuration and synchronizes differences.
example: A team reviews a configuration change in Git before Argo CD applies it to a cluster.

label: ARKit
entry_text: ARKit is Apple’s framework for integrating digitally rendered objects with a device’s view of the physical world.
example: A furniture app anchors a virtual table to a floor visible through the camera.

label: Armed Forces Health Longitudinal Technology Application
entry_text: The Armed Forces Health Longitudinal Technology Application was an electronic health record system for U.S. military healthcare.
example: A clinician reviews an eligible patient’s documented outpatient visits across military facilities.

label: Arquillian
entry_text: Arquillian is a Java testing framework that runs integration tests within or against application containers.
example: A developer tests whether a dependency-injected service behaves correctly in its container.

label: Arranging catering
entry_text: Arranging catering coordinates food service, menu requirements, logistics, and timing for an event.
example: An organizer confirms dietary needs and delivery times with a caterer before a workshop.

label: Arranging conferences
entry_text: Arranging conferences coordinates venues, schedules, speakers, participants, and event operations.
example: An organizer prepares an accessible venue and resolves timetable conflicts between sessions.

label: ArtStation
entry_text: ArtStation is an online portfolio and community platform for visual artists working in fields such as games, film, and illustration.
example: A character artist publishes a portfolio piece with supporting design sketches and model views.

label: As-built drawings
entry_text: As-built drawings document the locations and details of work as actually constructed rather than only as originally planned.
example: A facilities team checks an as-built drawing before opening a wall to locate an installed conduit.

label: Ashampoo Burning Studio
entry_text: Ashampoo Burning Studio is software for creating, copying, and managing supported optical discs.
example: A user writes a verified set of archived photos to a disc supported by the drive.

label: ASP.NET Core MVC
entry_text: ASP.NET Core MVC is a .NET web framework for organizing application logic into models, views, and controllers.
example: A controller retrieves product data and passes it to a view that renders a product page.

label: ASP.NET Identity
entry_text: ASP.NET Identity is a Microsoft framework for adding user accounts, authentication, and related identity features to ASP.NET applications.
example: A developer integrates password reset and role-based access into a web application.
sense_note: Clarify whether the historical ASP.NET or ASP.NET Core identity implementation is required.

label: ASP.NET Web API
entry_text: ASP.NET Web API is a .NET framework for building HTTP services, especially APIs accessed by clients beyond web browsers.
example: A developer exposes product inventory through an endpoint used by a mobile application.
sense_note: The label can refer specifically to the earlier framework rather than ASP.NET Core web APIs.

label: Asphalt batch mix plant
entry_text: An asphalt batch mix plant produces asphalt in discrete batches by weighing and mixing heated aggregates and binder.
example: An operator checks that a production batch matches the specified mixture.

label: Assembly drawing
entry_text: An assembly drawing shows how components fit together in a product or system and may identify parts or their relationships.
example: A technician uses an exploded assembly view to locate a spacer among several fasteners.

label: Assessing patient needs
entry_text: Assessing patient needs gathers and interprets information about a patient’s health, functioning, preferences, and support requirements.
example: A care team documents mobility limitations before planning discharge support.

label: Asthma education
entry_text: Asthma education helps patients and caregivers understand asthma, recognize warning signs, and follow a clinician-approved management plan.
example: An educator checks that a patient can explain when to follow their written action plan.

label: Async/await
entry_text: Async and await are language constructs that express asynchronous operations in a sequential-looking form without necessarily blocking the executing thread.
example: A client application waits for a server response while allowing its interface to remain responsive.

label: Atlassian Confluence
entry_text: Atlassian Confluence is a collaboration platform for creating and organizing shared pages, documentation, and project knowledge.
example: A team documents design decisions on a shared page and maintains its revision history.

label: Atlassian Crucible
entry_text: Atlassian Crucible is a tool for collaborative code review and discussion of changes.
example: Reviewers annotate specific lines and track issues before accepting a change.

label: Atomic layer deposition
entry_text: Atomic layer deposition deposits thin films through repeated, self-limiting surface reactions.
example: A fabrication team uses the process to specify a uniform film thickness over a patterned surface.

label: AtScale
entry_text: AtScale provides a semantic layer that lets analytics tools use shared business metrics over underlying data platforms.
example: A company defines revenue once and uses the definition across multiple dashboards.

label: auditd
entry_text: auditd is a Linux userspace daemon that records events supplied by the Linux Audit subsystem.
example: An administrator reviews records of changes to a monitored configuration file.

label: Auditing
entry_text: Auditing systematically examines evidence to evaluate whether statements, practices, or controls meet specified criteria.
example: An auditor samples purchase records to assess whether payments received the required approvals.

label: Auditing inpatient coding
entry_text: Auditing inpatient coding checks that diagnoses and procedures recorded for admitted patients are consistently supported by clinical documentation and applicable coding rules.
example: An auditor compares an assigned procedure code with the operative report and records any discrepancy.

label: Auditing outpatient coding
entry_text: Auditing outpatient coding checks whether codes for non-inpatient encounters match the documentation and applicable coding rules.
example: An auditor compares charges for an outpatient office visit with the services documented in the record.

label: Aural rehabilitation
entry_text: Aural rehabilitation helps people with hearing loss improve communication through training, strategies, and appropriate assistive supports.
example: A clinician and client practice speech recognition and strategies for conversations in noisy spaces.

label: Aurelia
entry_text: Aurelia is a JavaScript framework for building client-side applications with components, templates, and data binding.
example: A developer binds a view to an editable customer profile model.

label: Author-it
entry_text: Author-it is a component content management and authoring platform for reusing structured content across publications.
example: A documentation team updates a shared topic once and republishes several manuals.

label: Autism therapy
entry_text: Autism therapy encompasses individualized clinical or developmental supports intended to help autistic people pursue communication, daily living, or other chosen goals.
example: A therapist and client choose a communication goal and evaluate whether a new support is useful.
sense_note: This is an umbrella term, not one treatment, and does not imply a goal of eliminating autism.

label: Auto glass installation and repair
entry_text: Auto glass installation and repair assess, repair, or replace vehicle windows while maintaining visibility and structural fit.
example: A technician replaces a cracked windshield and checks that the installation meets vehicle specifications.

label: Autodesk 123D
entry_text: Autodesk 123D was a family of consumer tools for creating and preparing digital 3D designs.
example: A hobbyist creates a simple model and exports it for fabrication.

label: Automotive detailing
entry_text: Automotive detailing thoroughly cleans, restores, and protects a vehicle’s interior and exterior surfaces.
example: A detailer cleans fabric seats and protects painted surfaces after removing road residue.

label: Autoregressive integrated moving average
entry_text: An autoregressive integrated moving-average model forecasts a univariate time series through differencing and terms based on prior values and forecast errors.
example: An analyst models weekly demand and checks whether its residuals retain time dependence.

label: Autoshade
entry_text: Autoshade was an Autodesk rendering application for producing shaded images from three-dimensional AutoCAD geometry.
example: A designer renders an older CAD model to review how its surfaces appear.
sense_note: The suggested sense is the historical Autodesk renderer.

label: AvantGo
entry_text: AvantGo was a mobile service for synchronizing web content to handheld devices for later reading.
example: A traveler downloads news to a handheld and reads it offline.

label: AVEVA PI System
entry_text: AVEVA PI System captures, stores, and contextualizes time-series data from industrial operations.
example: A plant engineer compares motor temperature readings over several shifts.

label: Aviation medical examination
entry_text: An aviation medical examination assesses whether an individual meets health requirements for a defined aviation role or certification.
example: A designated examiner evaluates an applicant’s fitness for the requested aviation medical certificate.

label: Avid Elastic Reality
entry_text: Avid Elastic Reality was a visual-effects application for morphing and warping images or video.
example: A compositor uses shape-based morphing to transition between two images.

label: Avid Media Composer
entry_text: Avid Media Composer is a nonlinear video editing application for organizing media and assembling edited productions.
example: An editor synchronizes recorded audio to camera footage and revises a sequence.

label: Amazon Web Services
entry_text: Amazon Web Services is a cloud platform providing on-demand computing, storage, networking, and other managed services.
example: A company hosts a web application using cloud compute and a managed database.

label: AWS big data
entry_text: AWS big data refers to the use of Amazon Web Services to ingest, store, process, and analyze large or complex datasets.
example: A team combines object storage and distributed processing to summarize telemetry.
sense_note: This is a service area rather than a single AWS product.

label: AWS Cloud9
entry_text: AWS Cloud9 is a cloud-based integrated development environment for editing, running, and debugging code in a browser.
example: A developer maintains an existing project from its hosted workspace.

label: AWS CloudFormation
entry_text: AWS CloudFormation provisions and manages groups of AWS resources from declarative infrastructure templates.
example: A team recreates a test environment using the same reviewed template as its staging environment.

label: AWS CloudHSM
entry_text: AWS CloudHSM provides dedicated cloud hardware security modules for managing cryptographic keys and performing cryptographic operations.
example: An application signs a document using a key controlled within a hardware security module.

label: AWS CloudTrail
entry_text: AWS CloudTrail records supported activity in an AWS account so teams can audit actions and changes.
example: An investigator checks which identity changed a storage resource’s configuration.

label: AWS CodeBuild
entry_text: AWS CodeBuild is a managed service that runs specified build and test steps and produces build artifacts.
example: A team runs regression tests and packages the application on each approved change.

label: AWS CodeCommit
entry_text: AWS CodeCommit is a managed service that hosts private Git repositories in AWS.
example: A team reviews changes in a private repository integrated with its AWS identity controls.

label: AWS Command Line Interface
entry_text: The AWS Command Line Interface invokes AWS service operations through terminal commands or scripts.
example: An administrator lists the resources that belong to a development account.

label: AWS Elastic Beanstalk
entry_text: AWS Elastic Beanstalk deploys applications while managing much of the supporting AWS infrastructure.
example: A team uploads a web application and lets the platform manage its deployment environment.

label: AWS IoT
entry_text: AWS IoT is a family of services for connecting devices, processing their messages, and managing fleets.
example: A monitoring team collects authorized temperature readings from equipment at multiple sites.

label: AWS Lambda
entry_text: AWS Lambda is a managed service that executes code on demand in response to invocations and events.
example: A file upload triggers a function that validates the file’s metadata.

label: AWS networking
entry_text: AWS networking involves configuring connectivity, routing, isolation, and traffic management for AWS resources.
example: An engineer puts a service in a private subnet and allows access through an approved endpoint.

label: AWS OpsWorks
entry_text: AWS OpsWorks was a family of AWS configuration-management offerings for automating infrastructure and application setup.
example: An operations team applies a managed configuration policy to a group of servers.

label: AWS Outposts
entry_text: AWS Outposts extends selected AWS infrastructure and services into a customer’s on-premises or colocated facility.
example: A company processes data locally while using AWS tools to operate the on-site infrastructure.

label: AWS SDK
entry_text: An AWS Software Development Kit exposes programming interfaces for calling AWS services from application code.
example: A developer uploads a file to object storage through the SDK for the application’s language.

label: AWS serverless
entry_text: AWS serverless refers to building systems with managed services that avoid direct administration of the underlying servers.
example: An order event triggers managed compute and stores a record in a managed database.

label: Axios
entry_text: Axios is a promise-based JavaScript HTTP client for browsers and Node.js.
example: A front end fetches account data and displays an error if the request fails.

label: Azure Application Insights
entry_text: Azure Application Insights monitors application performance by collecting telemetry such as requests, dependencies, exceptions, and traces.
example: An engineer traces a slow API request through its downstream service calls.

label: Azure Cognitive Services
entry_text: Azure Cognitive Services is the historical name for a family of cloud APIs that add capabilities such as language, speech, and vision processing to applications.
example: A developer adds automatic transcription using a managed speech service.

label: Azure Data Factory
entry_text: Azure Data Factory is a managed data integration service for orchestrating data movement and transformations.
example: A team schedules nightly ingestion from an operational database into an analytical store.

label: Azure DevOps
entry_text: Azure DevOps provides tools for software project tracking, source control, build pipelines, and release workflows.
example: A team links a work item to the pull request and build that implement it.

label: Azure IoT
entry_text: Azure IoT comprises cloud and device services for securely connecting and monitoring fleets of connected devices.
example: An operator tracks telemetry from remotely deployed meters.

label: Azure Monitor
entry_text: Azure Monitor collects and analyzes operational telemetry across cloud and connected resources.
example: An operations team uses a dashboard and alerts to detect an increase in service failures.

label: Azure Policy
entry_text: Azure Policy evaluates Azure resources against governance rules and can apply effects such as audit or denial.
example: An administrator audits whether deployments use approved geographic regions.

label: Azure Security
entry_text: Azure Security refers to protecting Azure workloads and data through identity, network, configuration, and monitoring controls.
example: A cloud team restricts storage access to approved identities and monitors for unauthorized changes.
sense_note: This is a broad practice, not necessarily a single Microsoft product.

label: Babylon.js
entry_text: Babylon.js is a JavaScript and TypeScript engine for rendering and interacting with 3D scenes on the web.
example: A developer adds an interactive product model to a browser-based showroom.

label: Back-end development
entry_text: Back-end development implements the services, storage, and business logic that support client applications.
example: A developer builds an order service that checks inventory before saving a purchase.

label: Backbone.js
entry_text: Backbone.js is a JavaScript library that structures web applications using models, collections, views, and routing.
example: A maintainer updates how a Backbone view responds to changes in its underlying data.

label: BACnet
entry_text: BACnet is a communication protocol for exchanging data among building automation and control systems.
example: A facilities dashboard reads room temperatures from compatible heating and ventilation controllers.

label: Bacon.js
entry_text: Bacon.js is a JavaScript library for modeling changing values and asynchronous events with functional reactive streams.
example: A web interface combines a filter selection stream with a search text stream.

label: Bacterial culture
entry_text: Bacterial culture is the growth of bacteria in a controlled laboratory setting for observation, identification, or study.
example: A microbiologist reviews a culture report to distinguish growth from a negative result.

label: Balafon
entry_text: The balafon is a wooden-key percussion instrument, usually with resonators beneath its keys, used in West African musical traditions.
example: An ensemble player performs a repeating melodic pattern on a balafon.

label: Balloon modelling
entry_text: Balloon modelling shapes inflated balloons into recognizable figures or decorative structures.
example: A performer twists balloons into a simple animal for an event.

label: Banner advertising
entry_text: Banner advertising places visual promotional units within websites, apps, or other digital displays.
example: A campaign team checks whether a display banner is legible at its intended dimensions.

label: Banyan VINES
entry_text: Banyan VINES was a network operating system that provided directory, file, and other network services.
example: An IT historian examines how a legacy office network organized users and shared printers.

label: Baseline Personnel Security Standard
entry_text: The Baseline Personnel Security Standard is a UK government framework for basic employment screening of individuals with access to government assets.
example: A recruiter documents completion of the required baseline checks before a new staff member begins work.
sense_note: This is a baseline screening framework, not a national security clearance.

label: BaseX
entry_text: BaseX is an XML database and XQuery processor for storing and querying structured documents.
example: A publishing team retrieves sections of manuals by querying their XML markup.

label: Batman.js
entry_text: Batman.js was a JavaScript framework for building client-side web applications around models, bindings, and views.
example: A maintainer troubleshoots an obsolete application whose page automatically updates when its data changes.

label: Battle management
entry_text: Battle management is the coordination of situational information, decisions, and resources during military operations.
example: A historian studies how a command structure divided responsibility for tracking events and reporting decisions.

label: Bed mobility
entry_text: Bed mobility is the ability to reposition oneself in bed or the clinical support needed to perform those movements.
example: A therapist observes how independently a patient can roll and move into a seated position.

label: Behavior change communication
entry_text: Behavior change communication uses audience research and designed messages to support adoption or maintenance of a specific behavior.
example: A community program tests which reminders make attendance at scheduled health appointments easier.

label: Benefits realisation management
entry_text: Benefits realisation management defines intended gains from an initiative and tracks whether they occur after implementation.
example: A project sponsor assigns responsibility for checking processing time several months after a new workflow launches.

label: Bereavement care
entry_text: Bereavement care provides practical, emotional, and, when appropriate, clinical support to people grieving a death.
example: A care team offers a family information about local grief support and follows up after the funeral.

label: Berkeley Data Analytics Stack
entry_text: The Berkeley Data Analytics Stack was a research software ecosystem integrating tools for distributed processing and analysis of large datasets.
example: A researcher studies how its projects combined cluster computing with analytics workloads.

label: Bidirectional-streams Over Synchronous HTTP
entry_text: Bidirectional-streams Over Synchronous HTTP is a transport specification that emulates a two-way stream using sequences of HTTP requests and responses.
example: A messaging client exchanges streaming messages over ordinary HTTP infrastructure.

label: BigFix
entry_text: BigFix is an endpoint-management platform for tracking device inventory, distributing software, and applying patches or configuration policies.
example: An administrator checks which managed devices still need an approved update.

label: Binary Ninja
entry_text: Binary Ninja is a reverse-engineering platform for examining compiled software through disassembly and intermediate representations.
example: A defender reviews an unknown executable’s high-level behavior as part of incident triage.

label: BIND
entry_text: BIND is a software implementation of the Domain Name System used to serve authoritative DNS answers or resolve names.
example: An administrator validates a zone change before publishing it on a nameserver.

label: Bioconductor
entry_text: Bioconductor is a collection of R packages and data resources for analyzing biological and genomic datasets.
example: A researcher generates exploratory plots from a published gene-expression dataset.

label: Biopython
entry_text: Biopython is a collection of Python libraries for working with biological data formats and computational biology tasks.
example: An analyst reads annotation records from a public sequence database into a table.

label: Bitly
entry_text: Bitly is a link-management service that creates shortened URLs and measures interactions with them.
example: An event team compares clicks on links printed on two different flyers.

label: BlackLine
entry_text: BlackLine provides software for managing reconciliations, close tasks, and related accounting controls.
example: An accounting team records a balance reconciliation and routes it for sign-off.

label: Blast radius analysis
entry_text: Blast radius analysis estimates which systems, users, or operations could be affected by a proposed change or failure.
example: A team maps which applications depend on a database before scheduling its maintenance.

label: Blended learning
entry_text: Blended learning purposefully combines in-person instruction with online or computer-mediated learning activities.
example: Learners review demonstrations online and use class time to practice with instructor feedback.

label: Blender Game Engine
entry_text: Blender Game Engine was Blender’s integrated runtime and authoring environment for interactive 3D experiences.
example: An archivist opens a legacy project in a compatible Blender version to inspect its logic bricks.
sense_note: The historical Blender component is distinct from later forks and unrelated engines.

label: Boa Constructor
entry_text: Boa Constructor was a Python development environment and GUI builder for applications using wxPython.
example: A maintainer opens a legacy desktop dialog and edits the layout visually.

label: Board support package
entry_text: A board support package contains the code and configuration needed to run an operating system on a particular hardware board.
example: An embedded developer uses the package to initialize a board’s supported peripherals at boot.

label: Body contouring
entry_text: Body contouring refers to surgical or nonsurgical procedures intended to change the shape of a region of the body.
example: A clinician discusses which contouring options, risks, and recovery expectations are relevant to a patient’s goals.

label: BODYATTACK
entry_text: BODYATTACK is a branded group fitness class built around aerobics, athletic movement, and conditioning exercises.
example: An instructor demonstrates a low-impact alternative during a group session.

label: BODYPUMP
entry_text: BODYPUMP is a branded group fitness class using repeated resistance exercises performed with barbells or weights.
example: A participant selects an appropriate load for the class’s squat track.

label: Bonjour
entry_text: Bonjour is Apple’s zero-configuration networking implementation for local network service discovery and name resolution.
example: A laptop discovers a compatible network printer without requiring its address to be entered manually.

label: Boolean search
entry_text: Boolean search combines search terms using logical operators to include, require, or exclude conditions.
example: A recruiter searches for analyst profiles that mention either Python or R while requiring a specified location.

label: Box API
entry_text: The Box API provides programming access to Box content, users, permissions, and related services.
example: An authorized integration uploads a report to a designated team folder.

label: Box Backup
entry_text: Box Backup is software for backing up files to a remote server and restoring them later.
example: An administrator uses a test restoration to confirm that archived files can be recovered.
sense_note: This is the backup tool named Box Backup, not a general reference to backups in the Box cloud platform.

label: Brand communication
entry_text: Brand communication expresses a brand’s identity and promises through messages and interactions across channels.
example: A service organization uses the same promise and tone in its website and customer emails.

label: Brand strategy
entry_text: Brand strategy defines the audience, positioning, and priorities that guide how an organization builds and manages its brand.
example: A company chooses to emphasize reliability rather than low price in its product and communications decisions.

label: Brand positioning
entry_text: Brand positioning defines the distinctive place a brand seeks to hold in a target audience’s mind relative to alternatives.
example: A bicycle maker positions its commuter model around easy maintenance instead of racing speed.

label: Branding
entry_text: Branding creates and maintains a recognizable identity and a coherent set of associations for an offering or organization.
example: A nonprofit applies consistent naming, visuals, and language across materials and events.

label: Breeze.js
entry_text: Breeze.js is a JavaScript library for managing client-side data entities, queries, caching, and tracked changes.
example: A business application edits related customer records locally before saving them to a server.

label: Bridal consulting
entry_text: Bridal consulting advises clients on wedding choices and can coordinate selected elements of planning and preparation.
example: A consultant helps a couple choose among vendors within their budget.

label: Brightway
entry_text: Brightway is an open-source framework for life-cycle assessment that models resource use and environmental impacts across supply chains.
example: An analyst compares modeled emissions from two packaging systems using documented inventory datasets.

label: Broadcast programming
entry_text: Broadcast programming selects and schedules content for distribution through a television, radio, or comparable broadcast service.
example: A scheduler places a local news program before a sports broadcast while meeting timing constraints.

label: Browzwear
entry_text: Browzwear is a set of digital apparel tools for designing, simulating, and reviewing three-dimensional garments.
example: A designer checks how a jacket pattern drapes on a virtual fit model before ordering a sample.

label: Brute-force search
entry_text: Brute-force search systematically checks candidate solutions without relying on a problem-specific shortcut to restrict the search.
example: A small puzzle solver tests every permitted arrangement to confirm whether one satisfies the clues.

label: Btrieve
entry_text: Btrieve is an indexed record-management system that lets software store and retrieve records through keys.
example: A maintainer retrieves an invoice directly using its index key in a legacy application.

label: Budtending
entry_text: Budtending is customer service in regulated cannabis retail, including explaining products and following sales controls.
example: A retail worker explains label information and checks the purchaser’s eligibility under store procedures.

label: Bug tracking systems
entry_text: Bug tracking systems record, prioritize, assign, and track software defects through investigation and resolution.
example: A tester files a reproducible defect and links it to the fix and verification result.

label: Building crates and skids
entry_text: Building crates and skids constructs protective or load-bearing shipping structures suited to the weight and dimensions of goods.
example: A shop assembles a supported shipping base and crate for a fragile machine.

label: Bullet Physics
entry_text: Bullet Physics is a library for simulating collisions and physical motion of objects in three-dimensional scenes.
example: A game developer uses it to make fallen crates collide and settle on a floor.

label: Bulma
entry_text: Bulma is a CSS framework that supplies reusable classes for responsive layouts and interface components.
example: A developer makes a row of cards stack vertically on narrow displays.

label: Burndown chart
entry_text: A burndown chart plots remaining planned work against time to show how completion is progressing.
example: A team spots that several tasks remain unchanged as the iteration deadline approaches.

label: Business excellence
entry_text: Business excellence is a management approach to improving performance through systematic assessment, feedback, and sustained improvement.
example: An organization assesses its service quality and selects process changes based on the findings.

label: Business integration software
entry_text: Business integration software connects applications or data sources to exchange information and coordinate processes.
example: An integration passes completed orders from an online store to a warehouse system.

label: Business process analysis
entry_text: Business process analysis studies how work currently flows and identifies sources of delay, error, cost, or duplication.
example: An analyst maps a purchase approval process and finds where requests are entered twice.

label: Butchering
entry_text: Butchering prepares meat by breaking it down, trimming it, and portioning it into usable cuts.
example: A butcher portions a larger cut to meet a store’s weight and quality specifications.

label: Butter Knife
entry_text: Butter Knife is an Android library that generates binding code from annotations connecting views and callbacks to application code.
example: A maintainer traces how a legacy screen binds its save button to a handler.

label: bzip2
entry_text: bzip2 is a lossless compression utility and format for reducing the size of files.
example: An archivist compresses a plain-text log and later recovers the original bytes.

label: C-CURE
entry_text: C-CURE is a physical security platform for access control and monitoring security events in buildings.
example: A facilities operator adjusts authorized access for a restricted office area.
sense_note: The name can refer to several related product generations.

label: C3.js
entry_text: C3.js is a JavaScript library that builds interactive charts on top of D3.
example: A developer displays monthly sales as a line chart with hover labels.

label: Cable splicing
entry_text: Cable splicing joins compatible electrical or fiber-optic conductors while maintaining their required insulation, protection, and signal continuity.
example: A qualified technician joins two fiber sections and checks the resulting signal loss.

label: cAdvisor
entry_text: cAdvisor collects resource usage and performance statistics from running containers.
example: An operator compares CPU and memory usage across containers on a host.

label: Caesarean section
entry_text: A caesarean section is a surgical procedure for delivering a baby through incisions in the abdomen and uterus.
example: A qualified care team plans a caesarean delivery when a vaginal delivery would pose unacceptable risks.

label: Caffe
entry_text: Caffe is a deep-learning framework for defining, training, and running neural-network models.
example: A researcher reproduces an older image-classification experiment from its Caffe model definition.

label: Caffe2
entry_text: Caffe2 is a deep-learning framework designed to run neural-network training or inference workloads across different deployment environments.
example: An engineer inspects an archived mobile inference workflow built with Caffe2.
sense_note: This is a separate framework from the original Caffe.

label: Cairngorm
entry_text: Cairngorm was an application architecture framework for structuring software written in Adobe Flex.
example: A maintainer traces how a legacy Flex app dispatches commands in response to interface events.

label: Cakewalk
entry_text: Cakewalk is a digital audio workstation lineage for recording, arranging, editing, and mixing music.
example: A musician edits MIDI notes and balances recorded tracks in a mix.
sense_note: The label could also refer to a software publisher or historical products under that name.

label: Probability calibration
entry_text: Probability calibration measures or adjusts whether predicted probabilities correspond to observed outcome frequencies.
example: A model evaluator checks whether events forecast at roughly 70 percent actually occur about 70 percent of the time.

label: Call admission control
entry_text: Call admission control protects service quality by deciding whether the network can accept a new call with its available capacity.
example: A network declines a new voice session when it would exceed the bandwidth budget.

label: Calyx Point
entry_text: Calyx Point is mortgage loan origination software for recording applications and managing related workflow and documentation.
example: A loan processor checks the completion status of an applicant’s required documents.

label: Camera calibration
entry_text: Camera calibration estimates how a camera projects real-world points into images, including parameters such as focal length and lens distortion.
example: A vision engineer uses images of known reference points to estimate distortion before measuring parts.

label: CANape
entry_text: CANape is Vector software for measuring and calibrating the behavior of electronic control units.
example: A validation engineer logs controller readings and compares them with reference measurements.

label: CanCan
entry_text: CanCan was a Ruby on Rails authorization library for defining what actions users may perform on application resources.
example: A developer allows ordinary users to read records but reserves editing for authorized staff.
sense_note: The later maintained fork is CanCanCan; do not assume the label refers to that fork.

label: Candidate sourcing
entry_text: Candidate sourcing identifies and engages people who may be suitable for an open or anticipated role.
example: A recruiter builds a shortlist of potential candidates using the role’s required skills and experience.

label: CanJS
entry_text: CanJS is a JavaScript framework and toolkit for building reactive web user interfaces with observable data and templating.
example: An application updates a customer list when records change without manually redrawing the entire page.

label: Cannabis and hemp extraction
entry_text: Cannabis and hemp extraction is the regulated processing of plant material to separate its chemical constituents from the plant matrix.
example: A quality reviewer checks the analytical results and traceability records for an extract batch.

label: Cannabis cultivation
entry_text: Cannabis cultivation is the production and care of cannabis plants under established growing and applicable regulatory requirements.
example: A compliance reviewer examines records showing how a permitted crop was tracked.

label: Canon EOS flash systems
entry_text: Canon EOS flash systems are compatible camera and flash components for controlling artificial light during exposure.
example: A photographer uses a compatible flash to balance a subject’s illumination against a bright background.

label: Canva
entry_text: Canva is a visual design platform for creating graphics, presentations, and related media with editable layouts and templates.
example: A community group adapts a shared event flyer for print and social media.

label: Canvas LMS
entry_text: Canvas LMS is a learning management system for organizing courses, assignments, assessment, and communication.
example: An instructor publishes a module and collects assignments through Canvas.

label: CanvasJS
entry_text: CanvasJS is a JavaScript charting library for rendering interactive data visualizations in web applications.
example: A developer builds an online chart that lets users examine a specific week’s readings.

label: Capacity management
entry_text: Capacity management aligns available resources with current and anticipated demand to maintain service performance.
example: A technology team estimates when storage demand will outgrow available capacity.

label: Capistrano
entry_text: Capistrano automates remote execution and deployment tasks for software applications.
example: A team runs a consistent release sequence across several authorized application servers.

label: Capture One
entry_text: Capture One is photography software for processing raw files, organizing images, and tethered capture.
example: A studio checks exposure and focus as images arrive from a connected camera.

label: Capybara
entry_text: Capybara is a Ruby web-testing library that simulates user interactions in a web application.
example: An acceptance test fills in a sign-up form and checks that a confirmation appears.

label: Cardiac stress testing
entry_text: Cardiac stress testing evaluates heart function under exercise or a pharmacological challenge using monitored measurements.
example: A clinician reviews the recorded response to a supervised stress test.

label: Cardiac valve repair
entry_text: Cardiac valve repair uses clinical interventions to restore function in an existing heart valve without fully replacing it.
example: A heart team evaluates whether a leaking valve can be repaired and explains the options to a patient.

label: Cardiopulmonary resuscitation
entry_text: Cardiopulmonary resuscitation is an emergency response that uses chest compressions and, where appropriate, ventilation to support circulation during cardiac arrest.
example: A trainee demonstrates resuscitation on a manikin under an instructor’s supervision.

label: Cardiovascular coding
entry_text: Cardiovascular coding translates documented heart and vascular diagnoses and procedures into standardized healthcare codes.
example: A coder checks that the codes used for a vascular intervention match the clinical record.

label: Care coordination
entry_text: Care coordination organizes treatment, communication, and follow-up among patients, caregivers, and service providers.
example: A coordinator confirms that a hospital discharge plan reaches the patient’s primary care practice.

label: Carrot2
entry_text: Carrot2 is a software library for clustering collections of text or search results into labeled groups.
example: A search interface groups articles under automatically inferred topics.

label: CARTO
entry_text: CARTO is a geospatial analytics platform for analyzing location data and creating map-based applications.
example: A transport analyst visualizes areas served by existing transit routes.

label: Cartographic design
entry_text: Cartographic design selects and arranges geographic information and visual symbols so a map communicates clearly.
example: A designer emphasizes public transit lines while de-emphasizing minor streets.

label: Case analysis
entry_text: Case analysis examines the facts, context, and alternatives in a specific situation to support an interpretation or decision.
example: A business student compares possible responses to a supplier failure using a detailed written case.

label: Case method
entry_text: The case method teaches through discussion and analysis of concrete situations rather than exclusively through lectures or abstract exercises.
example: An instructor asks students to defend different decisions as if they were the manager in a case.

label: CasperJS
entry_text: CasperJS was a scripting and testing utility for automating browser interactions through PhantomJS or SlimerJS.
example: A maintainer reads a historical browser test that verifies a site’s registration flow.

label: Casualty movement
entry_text: Casualty movement is the organized relocation or transport of an injured person to safety or appropriate care while accounting for their condition.
example: A first-aid drill evaluates whether participants coordinate a simulated handoff safely.

label: CatBoost
entry_text: CatBoost is a gradient boosting library that trains tree ensembles and includes specialized handling of categorical features.
example: An analyst trains a classification model using both transaction amounts and merchant categories.

label: CCH ProSystem fx Engagement
entry_text: CCH ProSystem fx Engagement is software for organizing audit and accounting engagement documents, workpapers, and trial balances.
example: An auditor links supporting schedules to a workpaper and routes it for review.

label: CDC Cyber
entry_text: CDC Cyber was a family of large computer systems manufactured by Control Data Corporation.
example: A computing historian investigates how a university scheduled programs on a CDC Cyber system.

label: cebas finalRender
entry_text: cebas finalRender is a rendering engine for producing images from 3D scenes with simulated lighting and materials.
example: A visual effects artist renders a scene to review its reflections and shadows.

label: Celoxis
entry_text: Celoxis is project portfolio management software for planning work, tracking delivery, and allocating resources.
example: A manager checks staffing conflicts across several projects.

label: CentiLeo
entry_text: CentiLeo is a GPU-accelerated renderer for producing images from 3D scenes.
example: A visualization artist renders a scene with complex lighting using a compatible graphics processor.

label: Cerner
entry_text: Cerner refers to a family of healthcare information systems, including electronic health record products.
example: A clinician retrieves documented laboratory results through a hospital’s Cerner system.
sense_note: The name can refer to the vendor or different products, so a specific application may need clarification.

label: Ceros
entry_text: Ceros is a platform for creating and publishing interactive digital content through visual authoring tools.
example: A design team publishes a web report with interactive illustrations and animated sections.

label: CFWheels
entry_text: CFWheels is a CFML web framework that structures applications with model-view-controller conventions.
example: A developer adds a controller action and view to display an order record.

label: Chai.js
entry_text: Chai.js is a JavaScript assertion library for expressing and checking expected conditions in tests.
example: A unit test checks that a returned record has the required properties and values.

label: Chain Conveyor
entry_text: A chain conveyor moves materials or products using one or more driven chains, sometimes with attached carriers.
example: A production line uses a chain conveyor to carry heavy fixtures between workstations.

label: Chain of custody
entry_text: Chain of custody documents who collected, handled, stored, or transferred an item and when each event occurred.
example: A laboratory records each transfer of a sealed specimen so its integrity can be evaluated.

label: Chainer
entry_text: Chainer was a Python deep-learning framework that constructed computation graphs dynamically during execution.
example: A researcher studies how a legacy Chainer model branches based on input.

label: Challenge-Handshake Authentication Protocol
entry_text: Challenge-Handshake Authentication Protocol authenticates a peer through a challenge and a response computed from a shared secret, without transmitting the secret directly.
example: A network administrator recognizes CHAP as the authentication method in a legacy link configuration.

label: Change agility
entry_text: Change agility is the ability of a person or organization to adjust effectively as conditions, priorities, or practices change.
example: A team reallocates work after a supplier delay and tests a new delivery sequence.

label: Change management planning
entry_text: Change management planning determines how a transition will be communicated, supported, implemented, and evaluated.
example: A manager prepares training and feedback channels before rolling out a new process.

label: Changing oil
entry_text: Changing oil removes used engine or machinery lubricant and replaces it with oil that meets the equipment’s requirements.
example: A mechanic records the oil and filter replacement in a vehicle’s service history.

label: Channel sales
entry_text: Channel sales reaches customers through partners such as distributors, resellers, and retailers rather than only through direct sales.
example: A software vendor trains an authorized reseller to sell and support its product.

label: Character art
entry_text: Character art develops the visual appearance of fictional characters through drawings, paintings, or digital models.
example: A game artist draws several silhouettes before modeling the selected character.

label: Chart.js
entry_text: Chart.js is a JavaScript library for rendering common data chart types using the browser’s canvas element.
example: A developer adds a chart that shows week-by-week traffic in an analytics app.

label: Chip design
entry_text: Chip design specifies and verifies the electronic circuits and layout to be fabricated in an integrated circuit.
example: An engineer checks a proposed hardware block for timing and functional correctness before fabrication.

label: Chipmunk2D
entry_text: Chipmunk2D is a physics library for simulating rigid bodies, collisions, and constraints in two dimensions.
example: A game developer models a ball bouncing between moving platforms.

label: Chordiant
entry_text: Chordiant was an enterprise software platform for customer relationship management and rules-based customer interactions.
example: A service provider maintains a legacy workflow that guides support agents through account inquiries.

label: Choreography
entry_text: Choreography composes and organizes movement in time and space for a performance.
example: A choreographer arranges the dancers’ entrances, spacing, and shared movements.

label: Chromatography software
entry_text: Chromatography software controls compatible instruments or processes and reports chromatographic measurement data.
example: A quality analyst reviews a chromatogram and checks how the software integrated its peaks.

label: Chronometer
entry_text: A chronometer is a precision timekeeping instrument, traditionally associated with navigation or certified accuracy.
example: A maritime exhibit explains how a reliable chronometer let navigators compare local time with reference time.
sense_note: In some occupational lists the term is used more broadly for a precision timer.

label: Cisco Intersight
entry_text: Cisco Intersight is an infrastructure management platform for monitoring and operating supported systems from a shared control interface.
example: An infrastructure team reviews firmware compliance for enrolled systems.

label: Cisco UCS Director
entry_text: Cisco UCS Director automates configuration and operations across supported computing, networking, and storage infrastructure.
example: An administrator uses a predefined workflow to provision a standard development environment.

label: Civil engineering design
entry_text: Civil engineering design develops and verifies plans for infrastructure and built works against conditions, safety requirements, and user needs.
example: An engineer sizes site drainage structures for the design’s expected runoff.

label: CKEditor
entry_text: CKEditor is a web-based rich text editor component for authoring and formatting content in applications.
example: A publisher embeds CKEditor in a form that lets editors add links and headings.

label: Claim processing
entry_text: Claim processing receives, validates, evaluates, and resolves requests for payment or coverage under applicable rules.
example: An insurance processor compares a submitted claim with the policy and requests missing documents.

label: Claims modeling
entry_text: Claims modeling uses statistical or computational methods to estimate claim frequency, cost, development, or related outcomes.
example: An insurer models the expected annual cost of reported property claims.
sense_note: This assumes the actuarial or insurance sense; it is not about constructing an argument.

label: Clarizen
entry_text: Clarizen was a cloud project and portfolio management platform for coordinating work, schedules, resources, and project reporting.
example: A project lead checks milestones across a program and updates a resource plan.

label: Clash detection
entry_text: Clash detection identifies incompatible intersections or clearances between components in a coordinated design model.
example: A construction coordinator finds a duct that overlaps a structural beam before installation.

label: Classification and Regression Tree
entry_text: A classification and regression tree recursively splits observations by predictor values and assigns a class or numerical prediction to each final region.
example: An analyst grows a tree to predict relative order-processing time from workload and staffing.

label: Clean Air Act
entry_text: The U.S. Clean Air Act establishes a federal framework for controlling air pollution, including air quality and emissions standards.
example: An environmental specialist identifies which air-pollution requirements are relevant to an industrial facility.
sense_note: The generic name can refer to other countries’ statutes; this definition assumes the U.S. law.

label: Clean Water Act
entry_text: The U.S. Clean Water Act establishes a federal framework for protecting water quality and regulating certain discharges of pollutants into waters.
example: A facility reviews whether a wastewater discharge needs a permit.
sense_note: This definition assumes the U.S. statute.

label: ClearDB
entry_text: ClearDB was a managed cloud database service centered on MySQL-compatible databases.
example: A developer connects an application to an existing hosted ClearDB database.

label: Client confidentiality
entry_text: Client confidentiality protects information learned through a client relationship from disclosure without appropriate authority.
example: A consultant limits circulation of a client’s records to the approved project team.

label: Clinical data repository
entry_text: A clinical data repository stores and organizes patient-related data from clinical systems for authorized retrieval or analysis.
example: A hospital makes laboratory results from several departments available through a shared record.

label: Clinical documentation improvement
entry_text: Clinical documentation improvement clarifies and completes clinical records so they accurately support patient care, coding, and reporting.
example: A specialist asks a clinician to clarify conflicting descriptions of a diagnosis without suggesting an unsupported answer.

label: Clinical laboratory phlebotomy
entry_text: Clinical laboratory phlebotomy is the collection and documentation of blood specimens for laboratory analysis.
example: A trained phlebotomist checks patient and specimen identifiers before transferring the sample to the laboratory.

label: Closed-circuit television camera
entry_text: A closed-circuit television camera sends video to a limited monitoring or recording system rather than to a public broadcast.
example: A facility uses an authorized camera to monitor access to a stockroom.

label: Cloud access security broker
entry_text: A cloud access security broker applies an organization’s security policies to its use of cloud applications or services.
example: A security team monitors whether approved cloud applications are being used to store restricted information.

label: Cloud-native development
entry_text: Cloud-native development builds software to use cloud delivery, operational automation, and independently manageable infrastructure or components.
example: A team automates deployment and scaling for a service across multiple instances.

label: CNC programming
entry_text: CNC programming specifies the controlled motions and instructions a computer numerical control machine uses to manufacture a part.
example: A machinist simulates a toolpath before running it on a milling machine.

label: Cocoa Touch
entry_text: Cocoa Touch is Apple’s application framework layer for building touch-oriented applications on iOS and related platforms.
example: A developer uses UIKit views and controllers to build a touch-based interface.

label: CocoaPods
entry_text: CocoaPods is a dependency manager that integrates libraries into projects built with Xcode.
example: A maintainer refreshes a project’s prescribed dependency versions and rebuilds it.

label: CocoonJS
entry_text: CocoonJS was a platform for packaging and running HTML5 applications and games as mobile apps.
example: A maintainer reviews how a legacy web game accesses native device features.
sense_note: This is distinct from Apache Cocoon.

label: Collaboration
entry_text: Collaboration is working with others toward a shared outcome by coordinating contributions, decisions, and responsibilities.
example: Designers and engineers jointly resolve an accessibility problem before release.

label: Collaboration software
entry_text: Collaboration software helps people exchange information, coordinate work, or jointly edit shared materials.
example: Several reviewers comment on a proposal and track decisions in a shared workspace.

label: Collaborative Planning, Forecasting and Replenishment
entry_text: Collaborative Planning, Forecasting and Replenishment is a supply-chain practice in which trading partners share plans and demand forecasts to coordinate inventory replenishment.
example: A retailer and supplier exchange demand projections ahead of a seasonal promotion.

label: Color matching
entry_text: Color matching adjusts or selects colors so a sample or output visually or instrumentally agrees with a target under specified conditions.
example: A print technician compares a proof to a reference under controlled lighting.

label: Color, material and finish design
entry_text: Color, material and finish design specifies the visible and tactile surface qualities of a product to achieve intended practical and aesthetic effects.
example: A designer chooses a textured finish that reduces visible fingerprints while supporting the product’s palette.

label: Combine harvester
entry_text: A combine harvester cuts a crop, threshes it, and separates the usable grain in one machine.
example: An operator harvests wheat and monitors how much grain is lost behind the machine.

label: Commercial loan documentation
entry_text: Commercial loan documentation records a business borrower’s obligations and the terms, conditions, and security interests associated with a loan.
example: A loan officer assembles the signed agreement and collateral records for review.

label: Commissioning, qualification and validation
entry_text: Commissioning, qualification and validation are coordinated activities for putting a system into service, verifying specified operation, and documenting consistent fitness for intended use.
example: An equipment team tests a newly installed line against requirements before documenting its authorized production use.

label: Common Criteria
entry_text: Common Criteria is a framework for specifying security requirements and evaluating information technology products against them.
example: A procurement team reads a product’s evaluation report to understand the assessed configuration and scope.

label: Common Language Specification
entry_text: The Common Language Specification defines a subset of .NET language features that libraries can follow to interoperate across supported languages.
example: A library author avoids exporting a type signature that another supported language cannot consume.

label: CommonJS
