entry_text: CommonJS defines conventions for JavaScript modules that expose exports and import dependencies through a require function.
example: A maintainer separates reusable logic into a module consumed by an older Node.js application.

label: Communication
entry_text: Communication conveys and interprets information among people through spoken, written, visual, or other signals.
example: A technician summarizes a handoff and asks the next shift to confirm the outstanding steps.

label: Communication software
entry_text: Communication software enables people or systems to exchange messages, audio, video, or other information.
example: A remote team uses a conferencing application to discuss a release decision.

label: Community advocacy
entry_text: Community advocacy represents or supports community priorities in decisions about services, resources, or policy.
example: Residents and an organizer present documented accessibility barriers to a transit board.

label: Compiler development
entry_text: Compiler development designs and implements software that translates source programs into another representation while checking and preserving their meaning.
example: A developer implements and tests a diagnostic for invalid expressions in a programming language.

label: Complaint investigation
entry_text: Complaint investigation gathers and evaluates evidence to determine the facts behind a reported problem and recommend an appropriate response.
example: An investigator interviews both parties and compares their accounts with relevant records.

label: Complex Problem Solving
entry_text: Identifying complex problems and reviewing related information to develop and evaluate options and implement solutions.

label: Compliance risk management
entry_text: Compliance risk management identifies, evaluates, and addresses exposures arising from failures to meet applicable obligations.
example: A company assigns owners to controls intended to prevent missed reporting deadlines.

label: Compliance testing
entry_text: Compliance testing checks a system, product, or process against explicit standards, requirements, or policies.
example: A reviewer samples whether access requests were approved and documented according to policy.

label: ComponentOne
entry_text: ComponentOne is a suite of reusable software components for building application interfaces, commonly in .NET environments.
example: A .NET developer uses a ComponentOne data grid to display editable records.

label: Composite pattern
entry_text: The composite design pattern organizes individual and grouped objects in a tree so clients can operate on them through a common interface.
example: A drawing program moves a single shape or a group of shapes using the same command.

label: Computational design
entry_text: Computational design uses rules, algorithms, or simulations to generate, evaluate, and refine design alternatives.
example: An architect compares many façade layouts against a daylight criterion.

label: Computer-assisted audit tools and techniques (CAATTs)
entry_text: Computer-assisted audit tools and techniques use software to gather, test, and analyze records for audit evidence.
example: An auditor tests a full transaction ledger for duplicate invoice identifiers.

label: Computer-assisted qualitative data analysis software (CAQDAS)
entry_text: Computer-assisted qualitative data analysis software helps researchers organize, code, retrieve, and compare qualitative evidence.
example: A researcher labels interview passages with themes and retrieves passages assigned to a specific theme.

label: Computer Fraud and Abuse Act
entry_text: The U.S. Computer Fraud and Abuse Act addresses specified unauthorized computer access and related conduct through federal law.
example: A compliance team consults counsel about the authorized scope of a security assessment.

label: Computerized system validation
entry_text: Computerized system validation documents evidence that a computerized system reliably fulfills its intended requirements in a defined use context.
example: A quality team verifies that an inventory system preserves audit records and correctly enforces approved access roles.

label: ComputerRx
entry_text: ComputerRx is pharmacy management software used to organize prescription processing and pharmacy operations.
example: An authorized pharmacy technician checks a prescription’s workflow status in the system.
sense_note: Confirm the exact module or product generation when those distinctions matter.

label: Concision
entry_text: Concision communicates the necessary meaning with few unnecessary words or details.
example: An editor shortens an incident update while keeping the impact and next action clear.

label: Concourse CI
entry_text: Concourse CI is an automation system for defining repeatable build, test, and delivery pipelines from tasks and resources.
example: A team runs the same test task whenever a source resource reports a new revision.

label: Concurrent engineering
entry_text: Concurrent engineering coordinates design, manufacturing, and other lifecycle work in parallel to identify trade-offs earlier.
example: A manufacturing engineer reviews tooling constraints while a design team is still revising a component.

label: Conducting tours
entry_text: Conducting tours guides visitors through a site or collection while explaining relevant features and managing the group’s movement.
example: A docent adjusts the route so all visitors can reach the selected exhibits.

label: Cone penetration testing
entry_text: Cone penetration testing evaluates subsurface conditions by measuring resistance and other responses as an instrumented cone is pushed into the ground.
example: A geotechnical engineer uses a cone penetration profile to infer changes in soil layers.

label: Confirmit
entry_text: Confirmit was a survey research and feedback platform for preparing questionnaires, collecting responses, and analyzing results.
example: A research team programs branching logic for a customer survey.

label: Conflict Catcher
entry_text: Conflict Catcher was a classic Mac OS utility for managing startup components and diagnosing conflicts among them.
example: A technician isolates a set of incompatible extensions in a legacy system.

label: Confluent
entry_text: Confluent is a data-streaming platform built around Apache Kafka that supports publishing, processing, and managing event streams.
example: An engineering team uses event streams to make inventory changes available to several services.

label: Confocal microscopy
entry_text: Confocal microscopy improves optical sectioning by rejecting out-of-focus light through a spatial aperture or equivalent optical arrangement.
example: A researcher builds a depth-resolved image stack from fluorescent material.

label: Consensus decision-making
entry_text: Consensus decision-making seeks a decision participants can support or accept after considering and addressing objections.
example: A committee revises a proposal to resolve objections before checking whether members can live with it.

label: Constant Contact
entry_text: Constant Contact is a digital marketing platform for managing contacts, sending campaigns, and collecting engagement data.
example: A nonprofit sends an event newsletter to a subscribed list and reviews link activity.

label: Constituent relationship management
entry_text: Constituent relationship management organizes interactions and records for people connected to a nonprofit, public institution, or similar organization.
example: A charity tracks donor communication preferences and volunteer involvement in one system.

label: ConstraintLayout
entry_text: ConstraintLayout is an Android layout container that positions and sizes child views according to relationships and constraints.
example: A developer anchors a button beneath a text field while keeping it centered on screens of different widths.

label: Construct (game engine)
entry_text: Construct is a game creation system for building and deploying games with visual event logic and interactive scene editing.
example: A creator defines an event that increases the displayed score when a player collects an item.

label: Constructing dental study casts
entry_text: Constructing dental study casts creates physical replicas of teeth and adjacent structures for examination, planning, or documentation.
example: A dental technician prepares a model so a clinician can examine how the patient’s upper and lower teeth fit together.

label: Construction management software
entry_text: Construction management software coordinates project information such as schedules, costs, drawings, and field records.
example: A superintendent checks revised drawings and records the day’s work from a job-site device.

label: Consumer engagement
entry_text: Consumer engagement builds and measures consumers’ active interactions with a brand, product, or service.
example: A marketer assesses whether people who receive a tutorial return to use the product.

label: Contact management software
entry_text: Contact management software stores and organizes information about people or organizations and their prior interactions.
example: A business records a contact’s preferred communication channel and recent correspondence.

label: Contact tracing
entry_text: Contact tracing identifies and communicates with people who may have been exposed to an infectious disease so appropriate public-health action can be considered.
example: A public-health team confidentially informs a person of a documented exposure and gives approved guidance.

label: Content curation
entry_text: Content curation finds, evaluates, selects, and organizes existing material for a particular audience or purpose.
example: An instructor assembles readings from several sources and explains why each is included.

label: Contingency planning
entry_text: Contingency planning prepares actions and responsibilities for plausible disruptions or changes in conditions.
example: A logistics team identifies alternate suppliers before a likely shipping interruption.

label: Continued process verification
entry_text: Continued process verification uses ongoing manufacturing data to check that an established process remains in a state of control.
example: A quality team monitors production measurements for trends after the process enters routine operation.

label: Continuous passive motion
entry_text: Continuous passive motion uses a motorized device to move a joint repeatedly through a prescribed range without active muscular effort from the patient.
example: A clinician checks that a prescribed device moves the patient’s joint within the authorized range.

label: Contour plowing
entry_text: Contour plowing follows lines of similar elevation across a slope to reduce runoff and soil erosion.
example: A grower aligns field passes with the hillside’s contours rather than straight down the slope.

label: Contract review
entry_text: Contract review examines proposed or existing terms to identify obligations, ambiguities, risks, and deviations from intended arrangements.
example: A project team compares a service agreement’s acceptance criteria with its negotiated scope.

label: ControlLogix
entry_text: ControlLogix is a Rockwell Automation platform for programmable industrial controllers and associated modules.
example: An automation engineer monitors whether an approved process sequence advances as specified.

label: ControlUp
entry_text: ControlUp provides software for monitoring and managing digital workspaces, endpoints, and virtual desktop environments.
example: An administrator checks whether slow desktop sessions share the same infrastructure bottleneck.

label: Coordination
entry_text: Adjusting actions in relation to others' actions.

label: Copier troubleshooting
entry_text: Copier troubleshooting diagnoses copying equipment problems and checks whether corrective actions restore expected operation.
example: A technician distinguishes a paper-feed fault from a print-quality problem before replacing parts.

label: Coping saw
entry_text: A coping saw is a hand saw with a narrow replaceable blade stretched in a frame for cutting curves and intricate shapes.
example: A carpenter uses a coping saw to trim decorative molding to match an adjoining profile.

label: Coppermine Photo Gallery
entry_text: Coppermine Photo Gallery is web software for publishing and managing albums, images, and related user interactions.
example: A site administrator organizes a community’s uploaded photographs into albums with appropriate permissions.

label: Copywriting
entry_text: Copywriting creates text intended to inform, persuade, or prompt a specific response from an audience.
example: A writer drafts a donation page that explains the cause and asks readers for a specific action.

label: Core Spotlight
entry_text: Core Spotlight is an Apple framework that lets applications index their content for search on the device.
example: A notes app makes a saved note discoverable from the device’s search interface.

label: CoreOS
entry_text: CoreOS refers to a container-focused Linux operating system lineage and associated tooling for running workloads on clustered infrastructure.
example: A maintainer reviews documentation for the specific CoreOS distribution in an archived cluster.
sense_note: Clarify whether the label denotes historical Container Linux, Fedora CoreOS, or another related project.

label: Corona SDK
entry_text: Corona SDK was a Lua-based development kit for creating and deploying primarily two-dimensional apps and games across platforms.
example: A game developer writes a single Lua scene and runs it on several supported mobile devices.
sense_note: This is the app development toolkit associated with Solar2D, not a renderer with a similar name.

label: Coronal polishing
entry_text: Coronal polishing removes superficial stains and plaque from the exposed surfaces of teeth using dental polishing methods.
example: A qualified dental worker documents which accessible tooth surfaces were polished.

label: Corporate communications
entry_text: Corporate communications manages official messaging and relationships with an organization’s internal and external audiences.
example: A communication team prepares consistent employee and press updates about a change in company leadership.

label: COSO framework
entry_text: The COSO Internal Control framework organizes the design and evaluation of organizational controls into complementary components and principles.
example: An internal auditor uses the framework to map how risk assessment and monitoring contribute to a reporting control.
sense_note: COSO also publishes an enterprise risk management framework; the label alone does not distinguish these.

label: Cost estimating
entry_text: Cost estimating forecasts the resources and expenditures needed to complete a project or deliver an outcome.
example: A construction estimator combines material quantities with labor and equipment rates to develop a budget.

label: Cost to serve
entry_text: Cost to serve estimates the expense of fulfilling and supporting demand for a given customer, product, or channel.
example: A distributor compares the fulfillment and support costs associated with bulk and small-volume customers.

label: CoStar Real Estate Manager
entry_text: CoStar Real Estate Manager is software for administering lease and property portfolio records and associated financial or operational workflows.
example: A lease administrator checks renewal dates and reporting information for several sites.

label: CPython
entry_text: CPython is the reference implementation of the Python language, written primarily in C.
example: A package maintainer checks that a compiled extension works with the target CPython release.

label: Crane signaling
entry_text: Crane signaling communicates authorized directions between a signal person and a crane operator using agreed visual or voice signals.
example: A lift team confirms its communication protocol during a supervised setup.

label: Create React App
entry_text: Create React App is a toolkit for starting React projects with a preconfigured development and build environment.
example: A maintainer locates the build scripts in an existing project scaffolded with Create React App.

label: CreateJS
entry_text: CreateJS is a suite of JavaScript libraries for building interactive experiences with graphics, animation, sounds, and asset loading.
example: A developer uses CreateJS to animate objects in a browser-based illustration.

label: Creative arts therapy
entry_text: Creative arts therapy uses structured engagement with artistic media as part of a therapeutic relationship and defined clinical goals.
example: A qualified art therapist incorporates drawing into a session designed around a client’s communication goals.

label: Creative problem-solving
entry_text: Creative problem-solving reframes a problem and generates and tests alternative approaches beyond familiar responses.
example: A team develops several low-cost ways to reduce misplaced equipment and prototypes the most promising one.

label: Credit risk analysis
entry_text: Credit risk analysis evaluates the likelihood and consequences of a borrower or counterparty failing to meet financial obligations.
example: An analyst studies cash flows and existing debt before assessing a borrower’s ability to repay.

label: Creo Elements/Pro
entry_text: Creo Elements/Pro was PTC’s parametric mechanical design software lineage for creating parts, assemblies, and engineering drawings.
example: An engineer changes a controlling dimension and inspects the resulting assembly update.
sense_note: Do not conflate the historical Pro product name with Creo Elements/Direct.

label: Crestron
entry_text: Crestron provides hardware and software for controlling audiovisual equipment, room systems, and automation functions.
example: A meeting room uses a Crestron controller to coordinate its display, lighting, and audio.
sense_note: The label is a vendor and product family rather than one controller or programming language.

label: Crestron programming
entry_text: Crestron programming creates control logic and interfaces for Crestron room automation and audiovisual systems.
example: An integrator programs a room interface to route an approved video source to its display.

label: Crime analysis
entry_text: Crime analysis examines incident and contextual data for patterns relevant to prevention, investigation, or resource planning.
example: An analyst checks whether reported theft patterns changed after a public reporting campaign.

label: Crime mapping
entry_text: Crime mapping uses geographic information to explore the locations and spatial patterns of reported incidents.
example: An analyst maps incident counts by area and checks whether boundaries or reporting differences influence the pattern.

label: Crime scene investigation
entry_text: Crime scene investigation documents a scene and identifies and preserves potential evidence for later examination.
example: An investigator records the location and handling history of collected evidence.

label: Critical path method
entry_text: The critical path method analyzes dependencies and duration estimates to identify the activity sequence that determines a project’s earliest completion.
example: A scheduler identifies which installation delay would move the overall completion date.

label: Critical reflection
entry_text: Critical reflection examines experience, evidence, and assumptions to reconsider judgments and improve future action.
example: A student compares a group decision with what happened and explains which assumption they would revise.

label: Critical test results management
entry_text: Critical test results management ensures that findings requiring urgent clinical attention are identified, communicated, and documented reliably.
example: A laboratory team confirms receipt of a critical result by the responsible clinician according to its protocol.

label: Critical Thinking
entry_text: Using logic and reasoning to identify the strengths and weaknesses of alternative solutions, conclusions, or approaches to problems.

label: Cross-platform app development
entry_text: Cross-platform app development builds applications intended to operate across multiple operating systems or device types, often sharing code or tooling.
example: A team tests a shared mobile application on iOS and Android while adapting platform-specific accessibility behavior.

label: CryEngine
entry_text: CryEngine is a game engine and authoring environment for building and running interactive three-dimensional applications.
example: A game team assembles terrain, lighting, and gameplay objects in a test level.

label: CU-SeeMe
entry_text: CU-SeeMe was an early Internet videoconferencing application that transmitted live video between networked participants.
example: A digital archivist describes how an early remote classroom used CU-SeeMe to connect participants.

label: Cucumber
entry_text: Cucumber is a behavior-driven development tool that executes scenarios written in a structured natural-language format against step definitions.
example: A product team and developers use an executable scenario to verify what should happen after an invalid sign-in.
sense_note: The family includes multiple language implementations; Cucumber.js is one of them.

label: Cucumber.js
entry_text: Cucumber.js is the JavaScript implementation of Cucumber that runs behavior specifications against JavaScript step definitions.
example: A test checks that a scenario describing checkout invokes the JavaScript code needed to verify the workflow.

label: Cultural sensitivity
entry_text: Cultural sensitivity recognizes that cultural practices and assumptions differ and responds respectfully without treating individuals as stereotypes.
example: A facilitator asks participants how they prefer to be addressed instead of presuming a norm.

label: Culture transformation
entry_text: Culture transformation deliberately changes shared habits, expectations, and norms within an organization.
example: Managers make post-incident review routine and track whether staff feel safer raising concerns.

label: CUnit
entry_text: CUnit is a unit-testing framework for organizing and executing tests of C code.
example: A developer runs a suite of tests for a small C library’s boundary cases.

label: Cured-in-place pipe
entry_text: Cured-in-place pipe is a rehabilitation method that forms a hardened lining inside an existing pipe instead of excavating its entire length.
example: A utility renews a deteriorated sewer segment from existing access points.

label: cURL
entry_text: curl is a command-line tool for transferring data to or from servers over supported network protocols.
example: A developer downloads a public dataset and records the response status.
sense_note: Distinguish the command-line program from libcurl, the underlying library.

label: Curriculum evaluation
entry_text: Curriculum evaluation gathers and interprets evidence to judge how well an educational program meets its goals.
example: An educator compares assessed student work with the program’s stated learning outcomes.

label: Curriculum planning
entry_text: Curriculum planning designs the sequence of learning objectives, content, experiences, and assessments for a program or course.
example: An instructor sequences prerequisite topics before assigning a capstone exercise.

label: Customer engagement planning
entry_text: Customer engagement planning specifies the activities, channels, timing, and responsibilities for interacting with customers.
example: A team schedules onboarding messages and assigns owners for follow-up calls.

label: Customer engagement strategy
entry_text: Customer engagement strategy defines why and how an organization will build meaningful customer interactions across the relationship.
example: A business chooses to prioritize relevant support at adoption milestones over frequent generic promotions.

label: Customer experience strategy
entry_text: Customer experience strategy defines the desired experience across a customer journey and coordinates changes to deliver it consistently.
example: A company brings store, delivery, and support teams together to reduce customer effort after a missed delivery.

label: Customer insight
entry_text: A customer insight is an actionable understanding of customer needs or behavior grounded in evidence rather than an observation alone.
example: A team learns from interviews and service data that customers abandon setup because they cannot locate required information.

label: Customer success
entry_text: Customer success helps customers achieve the outcomes they intended to obtain from a product or service.
example: A customer success manager agrees on adoption goals and checks whether the customer can now complete the targeted workflow.

label: Cutover planning and management
entry_text: Cutover planning and management coordinates the transition from an existing operational system to its replacement, including readiness checks and recovery arrangements.
example: A release team rehearses the switch and defines when to return to the old system if checks fail.

label: Cyara
entry_text: Cyara is a platform for automated testing and monitoring of customer interactions, especially contact center and voice workflows.
example: A contact center verifies that an incoming call reaches the correct support queue.

label: Cyber defense
entry_text: Cyber defense protects digital systems and services by reducing exposure, detecting harmful activity, and coordinating response and recovery.
example: A security team reviews access alerts and improves account protections after an incident.

label: Cyber engineering
entry_text: Cyber engineering applies engineering principles to design, validate, and maintain digital systems with defined security and resilience properties.
example: A team documents how a service isolates components and tests whether containment works under benign failure conditions.

label: Cyber Kill Chain
entry_text: The Cyber Kill Chain is a staged conceptual model that defenders use to organize observations about intrusion activity and potential opportunities to interrupt it.
example: An incident reviewer organizes already-observed evidence by stage to identify where monitoring coverage was missing.

label: Cyber threat hunting
entry_text: Cyber threat hunting is the proactive review of authorized telemetry for indications of malicious activity not already surfaced by routine alerts.
example: A defender checks whether an anomalous pattern reported in one internal system also appears in other approved logs.

label: Cyber threat intelligence
entry_text: Cyber threat intelligence turns evidence about digital threats into context that informs defensive decisions.
example: A security team assesses whether a reported threat is relevant to software the organization uses before updating priorities.

label: Cybersecurity compliance
entry_text: Cybersecurity compliance documents and demonstrates that security controls satisfy applicable policies, regulations, or standards.
example: A control owner collects evidence that restricted account access is regularly reviewed.

label: D3.js
entry_text: D3.js is a JavaScript library for binding data to web elements and building customized interactive visualizations.
example: A developer binds incident counts to map features and updates colors as a filter changes.

label: Dagger 2
entry_text: Dagger 2 is a compile-time dependency injection framework for Java applications, including Android projects.
example: A build checks whether all objects required by a feature can be provided by its dependency graph.

label: DALL·E
entry_text: DALL·E is a family of generative image models that create visual outputs from text prompts or related inputs.
example: An artist requests several conceptual images for preliminary composition review.

label: Darik's Boot and Nuke
entry_text: Darik’s Boot and Nuke was a bootable utility designed to overwrite supported computer storage media for data erasure.
example: An asset-disposal reviewer checks a historical record of an authorized disk wipe and its verification.
sense_note: Do not assume erasure suitability for other media, especially solid-state devices.

label: dashDB
entry_text: dashDB was IBM’s name for a database service oriented toward analytical workloads and data warehousing.
example: A data analyst runs aggregate queries on a historical dashDB data warehouse.
sense_note: Verify the exact legacy offering when present-day product identity matters.

label: Data center cooling
entry_text: Data center cooling manages heat and environmental conditions so computing equipment operates within intended ranges.
example: A facilities team compares inlet temperatures across racks to identify a cooling imbalance.

label: Data center design
entry_text: Data center design plans the computing facility and its power, cooling, connectivity, physical layout, and resilience requirements.
example: A design team evaluates whether a proposed equipment layout can meet both power and heat loads.

label: Data center facility management
entry_text: Data center facility management operates and maintains the building services that support a data center’s computing infrastructure.
example: A facilities manager schedules preventive maintenance of backup power and cooling equipment.

label: Data center operations
entry_text: Data center operations keeps the facility’s computing and supporting systems running through monitoring, maintenance, incident response, and planned change.
example: An operator coordinates hardware replacement with service owners to minimize downtime.

label: Data classification
entry_text: Data classification assigns data to categories according to its content, sensitivity, or business and handling requirements.
example: A records team marks payment records as restricted so additional handling controls apply.

label: Data deduplication
entry_text: Data deduplication identifies and removes or consolidates redundant copies of data while preserving needed information.
example: A storage system records identical file blocks once and points multiple files to the stored copy.

label: Data-driven decision-making
entry_text: Data-driven decision-making uses relevant evidence and analysis to inform judgment about what action to take.
example: A library compares attendance records and reader feedback before changing its opening hours.

label: Data-driven instruction
entry_text: Data-driven instruction uses evidence of learner progress or difficulty to adjust what is taught and how it is taught.
example: A teacher reteaches fractions after reviewing errors common across a class’s recent assessments.

label: Data-driven manufacturing
entry_text: Data-driven manufacturing uses operational data and analysis to guide production, quality, or maintenance decisions.
example: A plant investigates increasing scrap rates using measurements linked to production shifts.

label: Data engineering
entry_text: Data engineering designs and maintains systems that reliably ingest, transform, store, and serve data.
example: An engineer builds a pipeline that checks incoming sales records and makes validated data available for reporting.

label: Data entry (alphanumeric)
entry_text: Alphanumeric data entry accurately inputs records containing letters, numbers, and sometimes symbols into a system.
example: A clerk transcribes product identifiers containing both letters and digits and verifies each against the source.

label: Data entry (numeric)
entry_text: Numeric data entry accurately inputs data such as amounts, counts, and measured values into a system.
example: A clerk enters invoice amounts and checks that the decimal places match the source records.

label: Data modeling
entry_text: Data modeling represents entities, attributes, and relationships or other structures that determine how information is organized and used.
example: A designer models orders and line items separately so each order can contain multiple products.

label: Data pipeline
entry_text: A data pipeline is a sequence of connected processes that moves data between systems and may validate, transform, or enrich it along the way.
example: A scheduled pipeline reads new records, standardizes dates, and writes validated data to an analytics table.

label: Data Vault modeling
entry_text: Data Vault modeling structures a data warehouse around hubs for business keys, links for relationships, and satellites for descriptive history.
example: A warehouse stores supplier identifiers in a hub and records changing supplier attributes in a satellite.

label: Data visualization
entry_text: Data visualization represents data visually to help people inspect patterns, comparisons, distributions, or relationships.
example: An analyst plots a distribution rather than showing only an average so readers can see outliers.

label: Data warehouse management
entry_text: Operating and maintaining a data warehouse so consolidated data stays available, reliable, and suitable for analysis.
example: A manager tracks the overnight load and resolves a failed refresh before finance opens its dashboard.

label: Data wrangling
entry_text: Cleaning, reshaping, and combining raw data so it can be analyzed or used by another system.
example: An analyst parses inconsistent timestamps and joins the resulting records to a lookup table.

label: Database administration
entry_text: Maintaining database availability, security, integrity, and performance throughout its operation.
example: An administrator tests a backup restore before upgrading the production database.

label: Database design
entry_text: Defining a database's data structures, relationships, constraints, and access patterns to support intended uses.
example: A designer separates orders from line items and specifies how they are linked.

label: Database mirroring
entry_text: Keeping a secondary database copy synchronized with a primary to support recovery or failover.
example: A standby copy receives changes and is available if the primary database fails.

label: DB-Access
entry_text: An interactive Informix utility for issuing SQL statements and working with database objects.
example: A database operator uses DB-Access to inspect a table and run a report query.

label: DB2/400
entry_text: IBM's relational database for the AS/400 platform, now known as Db2 for i.
example: A reporting application queries customer records stored on an IBM i system.

label: DBCC
entry_text: A family of Microsoft SQL Server commands used to check database integrity and inspect or maintain database structures.
example: An administrator runs an integrity check against a restored database before returning it to service.

label: DbFit
entry_text: A framework for expressing and running database acceptance tests in a tabular format.
example: A tester documents sample rows and the expected result of a database query as an executable test.

label: DBpedia
entry_text: A linked-data project that extracts structured information from Wikipedia and makes it queryable.
example: A researcher uses DBpedia to retrieve structured place information for entries in a catalogue.

label: dbSNP
entry_text: A public reference database of genetic variants that assigns identifiers to individual variant records.
example: A scientist uses a variant's reference identifier to compare annotations across datasets.

label: DbUnit
entry_text: A Java library for testing database-dependent code with repeatable datasets and database-state assertions.
example: A test suite loads known records before checking a repository method.

label: DbVisualizer
entry_text: A graphical database client for connecting to relational databases, browsing schemas, and running SQL.
example: A developer inspects a table and exports the results of a query in DbVisualizer.

label: dc.js

example: A Java client uses JacORB to invoke an operation on a remote CORBA object.

label: JAFAN
entry_text: JAFAN refers to a family of U.S. Air Force and joint publications for administering and protecting special access programs.
example: A program security officer checks which manual applies when reviewing facility requirements.
sense_note: The label does not identify a particular JAFAN document or revision; applicability should be verified.

label: Jasmine
entry_text: Jasmine is a JavaScript testing framework that specifies expected behavior through test cases and assertions.
example: A developer writes a Jasmine test to check that a sorting function returns results in ascending order.

label: Java Archive
entry_text: The Java Archive format packages Java classes and related resources in a ZIP-based file that can contain a manifest.
example: A build packages a command-line application and its resources in a JAR with a declared entry point.

label: Java Communications API
entry_text: The Java Communications API defines Java interfaces for accessing serial and parallel communication ports.
example: A desktop application opens a serial port to read data from an attached instrument.

label: Java Persistence API 2.0
entry_text: Java Persistence API 2.0 specifies object-relational mapping and persistence for Java applications, including entity management and type-safe criteria queries.
example: A service uses an entity manager to load a customer stored in a relational table.

label: JavaScript engine
entry_text: A JavaScript engine parses and executes JavaScript programs, often compiling code or using intermediate instructions internally.
example: A browser uses its engine to execute an event handler when a user clicks a button.

label: JavaScriptCore
entry_text: JavaScriptCore is WebKit's engine for executing JavaScript code.
example: A WebKit-based application evaluates page scripts using JavaScriptCore.

label: JavaServer Faces 2.0
entry_text: JavaServer Faces 2.0 is a Java specification for constructing server-side web interfaces from reusable components with a defined request lifecycle.
example: A web form uses Facelets and JSF components to display validation errors after submission.

label: JAX-RPC
entry_text: JAX-RPC is an older Java API for invoking remote procedures using XML-based web services, commonly with SOAP.
example: A legacy Java client calls a published SOAP operation through a generated stub.

label: JAX-WS
entry_text: JAX-WS is a Java API for building and consuming XML-based web services, including SOAP services.
example: A programmer binds a Java service method to a SOAP endpoint described by WSDL.

label: JD Edwards CNC
entry_text: JD Edwards CNC is the administration discipline for installing, configuring and operating the JD Edwards EnterpriseOne technical environment.
example: An administrator builds and deploys an EnterpriseOne application package to a test environment.

label: JdbcTemplate
entry_text: JdbcTemplate is a Spring Framework class that simplifies Java database access by managing JDBC resources and repetitive query code.
example: A service uses JdbcTemplate to execute a parameterized query and map the returned rows.

label: JDesktop Network Components
entry_text: JDesktop Network Components refers to Java components intended to simplify access to networked services and data from desktop applications.
example: A desktop application uses a data provider to display results obtained from a remote service.

label: Jersey
entry_text: Jersey is a Java framework that implements the JAX-RS API for developing RESTful services and clients.
example: A Java service uses Jersey to route an HTTP GET request to an annotated resource method.

label: Jive Software
entry_text: Jive Software refers to enterprise collaboration software that supports communities, discussions and shared documents.
example: An organization uses a Jive community to publish reference documents and answer employee questions.
sense_note: The label could name the company rather than its collaboration product.

label: jMock
entry_text: jMock is a Java testing library that verifies interactions between code under test and simulated dependencies.
example: A test checks that a billing service invokes its mocked payment gateway exactly once.

label: JMockit
entry_text: JMockit is a Java testing library for substituting dependencies and verifying interactions in unit tests.
example: A test replaces a clock dependency so it can verify expiration behavior using a fixed time.

label: Job scheduling
entry_text: Job scheduling is the coordination of when tasks run, including their triggers, dependencies, resource availability and recurrence.
example: An operations team runs a reporting job only after the nightly data import completes.

label: Joint Clearance and Access Verification System
entry_text: Joint Clearance and Access Verification System was an interface within the U.S. Department of Defense personnel security system for recording and verifying clearance and access information.
example: A security office used JCAVS to check personnel eligibility before processing requests for access.
sense_note: Historical system; do not infer current availability from the name.

label: Joint Commission standards
entry_text: Joint Commission standards set accreditation requirements for health care organizations' quality, safety and operational practices.
example: A hospital reviews medication management practices against the requirements that apply to its accreditation program.

label: JointJS
entry_text: JointJS is a JavaScript library for displaying and editing interactive diagrams made from elements and links.
example: A web application uses JointJS to let users connect workflow steps visually.

label: Joomla
entry_text: Joomla is a content management system for publishing and administering websites through configurable templates and extensions.
example: A nonprofit site editor uses Joomla to publish an article without editing the site's HTML.

label: JPEG
entry_text: JPEG is a set of coding standards for compressing continuous-tone digital images, most commonly used with lossy compression.
example: A photographer saves a smaller web copy of a camera image as a JPEG.

label: JSData
entry_text: JSData is a JavaScript data-management library that provides records, relationships and adapters for application data.
example: A developer defines a record type and uses a REST adapter to load it from a server.

label: JSFiddle
entry_text: JSFiddle is a browser-based editor for combining and sharing runnable HTML, CSS and JavaScript examples.
example: A developer shares a small JSFiddle to demonstrate how a browser layout behaves.

label: jsGrid
entry_text: jsGrid is a JavaScript data-grid component for presenting and manipulating table records in a browser.
example: An admin page uses jsGrid to show a sortable inventory table with editable quantities.

label: JSON Web Token
entry_text: JSON Web Token is a compact format for transmitting claims as a JSON object, commonly signed or integrity-protected with JWS or encrypted with JWE.
example: An API verifies a signed token's issuer, audience and expiration before accepting its claims.

label: jsPerf
entry_text: jsPerf is a browser-based JavaScript benchmarking tool for comparing the execution rates of code snippets under its test harness.
example: A developer creates a benchmark to compare two array-processing expressions in the same browser.

label: JsRender
entry_text: JsRender is a JavaScript templating library that renders templates against data to produce text or HTML.
example: A page renders one product row for each item in an array using a JsRender template.

label: JsUnit
entry_text: JsUnit is a JavaScript unit-testing framework modeled on the xUnit family of test frameworks.
example: A developer uses a JsUnit assertion to verify the result of a date-formatting function.
sense_note: Multiple historical projects used similar capitalization; confirm the implementation if product-specific detail is needed.

label: JTrac
entry_text: JTrac is a web-based issue tracker for recording and organizing work items.
example: A support team records a defect in JTrac and assigns it to a developer.

label: Judgment and Decision Making
entry_text: Considering the relative costs and benefits of potential actions to choose the most appropriate one.

label: Jury instructions
entry_text: Jury instructions are the court's directions explaining the law, issues and legal standards jurors must apply in deciding a case.
example: A judge explains the applicable burden of proof to jurors before deliberations.
sense_note: The skill interpretation is preparing or communicating the instructions; the label itself names the instructions.

label: Jury management
entry_text: Jury management is the administration of jury service, including summonses, attendance, availability and assignment of jurors.
example: A court office schedules jurors and tracks which panels are available for trials.

label: Juvenile rehabilitation
entry_text: Juvenile rehabilitation supports young people involved in the justice system in changing behavior and returning safely to their communities.
example: A caseworker coordinates counseling, school attendance and reentry support for a youth leaving placement.

label: k-means clustering
entry_text: K-means clustering partitions observations into a chosen number of groups by iteratively updating cluster centroids and assigning observations to nearby centroids.
example: A retailer groups stores by similar traffic and transaction patterns after scaling the features.

label: Kahoot!
entry_text: Kahoot! is a learning platform for running interactive quizzes and activities on participants' devices.
example: A teacher runs a live review quiz and discusses the questions many students missed.

label: KairosDB
entry_text: KairosDB is a database system for ingesting and querying time-series measurements.
example: An operations team queries hourly aggregates of sensor readings.

label: Katalon Studio
entry_text: Katalon Studio is an integrated tool for creating and running automated application tests.
example: A tester records a web checkout flow and checks the resulting confirmation page.

label: Kenna Security
entry_text: Kenna Security refers to a vulnerability-management platform that prioritizes remediation using risk signals and asset information.
example: A security team ranks known vulnerabilities on its inventory to decide which fixes to deploy first.

label: Keras
entry_text: Keras is a high-level Python API for defining, training and using neural networks.
example: A developer builds a classifier as a sequence of layers and trains it on labeled images.

label: Kinesitherapy
entry_text: Kinesitherapy uses therapeutic movement and exercise to restore or improve physical function.
example: A rehabilitation clinician guides a patient through a prescribed range-of-motion exercise.

label: Kinetic typography
entry_text: Kinetic typography designs moving text to communicate timing, emphasis or meaning.
example: A title designer animates words in sync with the narrator's emphasis.

label: Knockout.js
entry_text: Knockout.js is a JavaScript library that binds interface elements to observable data in a view model.
example: A shopping page updates the price total when a user changes an item count.

label: Know Your Third Party (KY3P)
entry_text: Know Your Third Party is a third-party risk management platform for exchanging and evaluating due-diligence information.
example: A compliance team collects supplier assessment responses in a shared workflow.
sense_note: The abbreviation may also refer to a generic due-diligence practice.

label: KPI reporting
entry_text: KPI reporting measures and communicates key indicators tied to organizational goals.
example: A manager reports the weekly on-time shipment rate against its target.

label: Kyoto Protocol
entry_text: The Kyoto Protocol is an international climate treaty that set binding greenhouse-gas reduction or limitation commitments for specified parties.
example: A national emissions inventory supports reporting against an applicable commitment.

label: Kyriba
entry_text: Kyriba is treasury management software for tasks such as cash visibility, payments, liquidity planning and financial risk management.
example: A treasury analyst consolidates balances from several banks to review the day's cash position.

label: Label edge router
entry_text: A label edge router is a router at a Multiprotocol Label Switching domain boundary that adds, removes or processes packet labels.
example: An ingress router classifies incoming traffic and applies a label for its forwarding path.

label: Label printer
entry_text: A label printer produces labels carrying text, barcodes or graphics on compatible stock.
example: A warehouse worker prints barcode labels for outgoing cartons.

label: LabVIEW
entry_text: LabVIEW is a graphical programming environment for building measurement, automation and instrument-control applications.
example: A technician builds a program to acquire measurements and plot them live.

label: Landing page optimization
entry_text: Landing page optimization improves a destination web page to help visitors complete a defined action.
example: An analyst tests whether a clearer signup form raises its completion rate.

label: Lando
entry_text: Lando is a tool for configuring and running local development environments using containers.
example: A developer starts a reproducible web server and database using a project's Lando configuration.

label: Landscape painting
entry_text: Landscape painting depicts natural or built outdoor scenery using painted color, composition and perspective.
example: An artist paints a valley and uses softer colors to suggest distant hills.

label: Landscaping and yard care
entry_text: Landscaping and yard care involve designing, installing or maintaining outdoor grounds and plantings.
example: A grounds crew prunes shrubs and repairs a stretch of turf.

label: LangChain
entry_text: LangChain is a software framework for assembling language-model applications with components such as prompts, retrieval and tool calls.
example: A developer combines document retrieval and a language model to answer handbook questions.

label: Language interpretation and translation
entry_text: Language interpretation and translation convey meaning between languages, generally with interpreting for spoken or signed messages and translation for written material.
example: An interpreter relays a meeting discussion while a translator prepares its written summary in another language.

label: Language teaching
entry_text: Language teaching develops learners' comprehension and expression in a language through instruction and practice.
example: A teacher uses role-play to help beginners practice asking for directions.

label: Laser level
entry_text: A laser level projects a beam or line to establish reference points for level, plumb or alignment work.
example: An installer uses a horizontal beam to align wall-mounted cabinets.

label: LDRA Testbed
entry_text: LDRA Testbed is a software analysis and testing tool for assessing code quality, coding-standard compliance and test coverage.
example: A quality engineer checks embedded software for violations of a project's coding rules.

label: Lean principles
entry_text: Lean principles guide work improvement by defining customer value, reducing waste and improving how value-producing activities flow.
example: A production team reduces the time parts wait between inspection and assembly.

label: Learner analysis
entry_text: Learner analysis examines learners' prior knowledge, goals, needs and constraints to guide instructional decisions.
example: A course designer surveys employees' experience before selecting prerequisite exercises.

label: Learner experience design
entry_text: Learner experience design shapes activities, materials and interactions around how people engage with and learn from them.
example: A designer pairs a realistic task with immediate feedback and a guided retry.

label: Learning agility
entry_text: Learning agility is the ability to learn from experience and apply that learning in unfamiliar situations.
example: After trialing a new tool, a team member applies what worked to a different project.

label: Learning Strategies
entry_text: Selecting and using training/instructional methods and procedures appropriate for the situation when learning or teaching new things.

label: LEGO Digital Designer
entry_text: LEGO Digital Designer was a software tool for building virtual models from digital LEGO elements.
example: A builder tries different brick arrangements before assembling a physical model.

label: Less.js
entry_text: Less.js is a JavaScript implementation of a preprocessor that compiles Less syntax, such as variables and mixins, into CSS.
example: A developer defines a reusable color variable and compiles the stylesheet for a website.

label: Levelator
entry_text: Levelator is an audio processing tool that evens out variations in recorded speech levels.
example: A podcast editor uses it to balance a quiet presenter and a louder guest.

label: LIBSVM
entry_text: LIBSVM is a library for support vector machine classification, regression and related modeling tasks.
example: An analyst trains a support vector classifier to distinguish two categories of text.

label: LiDAR
entry_text: LiDAR measures distances by emitting laser light and analyzing the returned signal, often to create three-dimensional point data.
example: A survey crew maps terrain and structures along a road.

label: Life skills
entry_text: Life skills are practical abilities for managing daily responsibilities, relationships and decisions.
example: A learner makes a budget and schedules bill payments.

label: Lightcast
entry_text: Lightcast provides labor-market data and analytics about jobs, occupations and skills.
example: An analyst uses job-posting data to identify frequently requested qualifications.

label: LightGBM
entry_text: LightGBM is a library for training gradient-boosted decision tree models for classification, regression and ranking.
example: An analyst trains a model to predict customer churn from account data.

label: Lighting design
entry_text: Lighting design plans the placement, intensity, color and direction of light to support function or visual intent.
example: A designer sets light positions and levels to keep actors visible while creating a nighttime mood.
sense_note: The label spans stage, architectural and other lighting contexts.

label: LightTools
entry_text: LightTools is optical design and simulation software for modeling illumination systems and light propagation.
example: An optical engineer simulates how evenly a light guide illuminates a display.

label: LinkedIn
entry_text: LinkedIn is an online professional network for maintaining career profiles, connecting with contacts, and discovering jobs or professional content.
example: A recruiter posts a vacancy and reviews profiles of people interested in the role.

label: LinkedIn API
entry_text: The LinkedIn API provides programmatic access to authorized LinkedIn features or data under applicable permissions.
example: An application with approved access publishes content to a managed organization page.

label: Linux systems administration
entry_text: Linux systems administration involves operating and maintaining Linux hosts, including users, packages, storage, services and monitoring.
example: An administrator updates packages on a host and verifies that its scheduled services still run.

label: Liquidity forecasting
entry_text: Liquidity forecasting estimates when funds become available and when payments are due to anticipate cash shortfalls or surpluses.
example: A treasury team forecasts whether upcoming payroll will require a short-term transfer.

label: Listwise deletion
entry_text: Listwise deletion removes an entire observation from an analysis when any required variable is missing for that observation.
example: A regression omits survey responses missing either the outcome or a selected predictor.

label: LiveData
entry_text: LiveData is an Android Jetpack observable data holder that delivers updates with awareness of an observer's lifecycle.
example: An Android screen observes a view model's LiveData to display changes when the screen is active.

label: Livestreaming
entry_text: Livestreaming transmits audio, video or both to viewers with only a short delay while the event takes place.
example: A producer streams a conference talk and monitors audio and video quality during the broadcast.

label: LLM observability
entry_text: LLM observability is the practice of collecting and inspecting signals about a language-model application's execution and output quality.
example: An engineer uses traces to see whether slow answers originate in retrieval or model generation.

label: Load securement
entry_text: Load securement is the process of restraining transported cargo to prevent shifting or loss during transit.
example: A driver checks that approved restraints hold the pallets in place before departure.

label: Loan administration
entry_text: Loan administration manages the records, disbursements, payments, notices and servicing requirements of approved loans.
example: A servicing team reconciles received payments with the balances in its loan records.

label: Loan structuring
entry_text: Loan structuring designs financing terms such as amount, maturity, repayment schedule, collateral and covenants to fit the transaction's needs and risks.
example: A lender proposes seasonal payment dates based on the borrower's cash flow.

label: Loan syndication
entry_text: Loan syndication arranges financing in which several lenders participate under coordinated terms for one borrower.
example: A lead bank organizes a group of lenders to share a loan larger than any wants to hold alone.

label: Log management
entry_text: Log management collects, stores, organizes and evaluates records of events from systems and applications.
example: An operations team searches centralized logs to determine which service first reported an outage.

label: Logic diagrams
entry_text: Logic diagrams represent logical relationships or decision conditions using symbols and connections.
example: An engineer diagrams how two input signals determine an interlock status.
sense_note: May refer to circuit logic or formal decision diagrams, depending on context.

label: Logistics planning
entry_text: Logistics planning coordinates how goods and materials are stored, transported and delivered within time, capacity and cost constraints.
example: A distributor combines small shipments into routes that meet delivery windows.

label: Logo design
entry_text: Logo design creates a distinctive visual mark that represents an organization, product or brand.
example: A designer checks that a new mark remains recognizable on both an app icon and a printed sign.

label: Long short-term memory
entry_text: Long short-term memory is a recurrent neural network architecture that uses gates to retain, update or discard information across sequence steps.
example: A model uses an LSTM to incorporate earlier measurements while forecasting demand.

label: Low-code development platform
entry_text: A low-code development platform enables applications or workflows to be assembled using visual tools, reusable components and limited custom code.
example: A business team uses a visual builder to create a request form and approval process.

label: Low risk neonatal nursing
entry_text: Low-risk neonatal nursing provides routine assessment, monitoring and care for newborns who do not require intensive or high-acuity care.
example: A nurse monitors feeding, temperature and weight in a healthy newborn transition setting.

label: Low Voltage Transistor-Transistor Logic
entry_text: Low-voltage transistor-transistor logic defines digital signal-level conventions associated with TTL-compatible operation at reduced supply voltages.
example: A board designer checks that a device's logic-high and logic-low thresholds match its receiving interface.

label: Luigi
entry_text: Luigi is a Python library for organizing batch data workflows as tasks with dependencies and tracked outputs.
example: A pipeline runs a report-generation task only after producing its source dataset.

label: Lumion
entry_text: Lumion is architectural visualization software for turning design models into rendered images, animations and scenes.
example: An architect renders a building model with lighting, landscaping and surrounding context.

label: Lymphedema management
entry_text: Lymphedema management aims to control swelling caused by impaired lymph drainage and preserve function through assessment, ongoing care and appropriate treatment.
example: A trained clinician monitors limb measurements and adjusts a prescribed compression plan.

label: M2Crypto
entry_text: M2Crypto is a Python library that wraps OpenSSL functions for cryptography and secure communications.
example: A developer uses the library to inspect the metadata of a digital certificate.

label: Machine learning
entry_text: Machine learning develops models that improve at a defined task by fitting patterns to data rather than relying solely on explicitly written rules.
example: A team trains a classifier to categorize product reviews by topic.

label: Machine operation
entry_text: Machine operation involves setting up, controlling and monitoring equipment to carry out its intended task safely.
example: An operator selects the specified run settings and stops the machine when inspection reveals a fault.

label: Machine tools
entry_text: Machine tools are powered machines for cutting, shaping or finishing workpieces through controlled movement.
example: A machinist uses a lathe to turn a cylindrical part to the required diameter.

label: Macintosh Application Environment
entry_text: Macintosh Application Environment was software that allowed compatible classic Macintosh applications to run on certain Unix workstations.
example: A user opens a classic Mac application on a supported workstation through MAE.

label: macOS
entry_text: macOS is Apple's operating system for Mac computers, providing desktop, system and application services.
example: An administrator configures user access and installs an application on a Mac.

label: Mail distribution
entry_text: Mail distribution routes incoming or outgoing mail to the appropriate recipients or delivery channels.
example: A mailroom worker delivers sorted envelopes to the correct departments.

label: Mail processing
entry_text: Mail processing prepares, checks, sorts or records mail and parcels before distribution or dispatch.
example: A clerk verifies package labels and sorts items by destination.

label: Malware analysis
entry_text: Malware analysis examines suspected malicious software to understand its behavior, effects and indicators so defenders can detect or contain it.
example: A defender documents files changed by a suspected program in an isolated analysis environment.

label: Mammalian cell culture
entry_text: Mammalian cell culture maintains or grows mammal-derived cells outside their organism for research or controlled production.
example: A scientist uses cultured mammalian cells to study a cellular response to a candidate treatment.

label: Management of Financial Resources
entry_text: Determining how money will be spent to get the work done, and accounting for these expenditures.

label: Management of Material Resources
entry_text: Obtaining and seeing to the appropriate use of equipment, facilities, and materials needed to do certain work.

label: Management of Personnel Resources
entry_text: Motivating, developing, and directing people as they work, identifying the best people for the job.

label: Manure spreader
entry_text: A manure spreader is farm equipment that applies animal manure to land as a nutrient source or soil amendment.
example: A farmer uses the implement to distribute manure evenly across the area identified in a nutrient plan.

label: Map production
entry_text: Map production combines geographic data, cartographic design and publishing to create maps for an intended use.
example: A planner produces a printed map that distinguishes flood zones from roads and building footprints.

label: Map reading
entry_text: Map reading interprets a map's symbols, scale, orientation and features to determine locations or relationships.
example: A hiker uses contour lines to identify the steepest part of a planned route.

label: MapDB
entry_text: MapDB is a Java library for collections that can store data on disk or in memory.
example: A Java application keeps a large key-value index on disk using a persistent map.

label: Marine navigation
entry_text: Marine navigation plans and monitors a vessel's movement using charts, positions, environmental conditions and navigational aids.
example: A watch officer compares the vessel's position with its planned track before entering a channel.

label: Marine radar
entry_text: Marine radar detects surrounding vessels, shorelines and other reflecting objects using radio waves.
example: A watch officer checks radar contacts when visibility falls in fog.

label: Marionette.js
entry_text: Marionette.js is a JavaScript framework that builds on Backbone to organize application views, regions and related interface behavior.
example: A developer divides a dashboard into regions that display and replace their own views.

label: Maritime law enforcement
entry_text: Maritime law enforcement applies laws and regulations affecting vessels, waters or maritime activity within the agency's jurisdiction.
example: A maritime officer checks a vessel's required safety documentation during an authorized inspection.

label: Marketing management
entry_text: Marketing management plans, coordinates and evaluates the people, budgets and activities used to market offerings.
example: A manager reallocates a campaign budget after comparing acquisition results across channels.

label: Marketing strategy
entry_text: Marketing strategy defines the audiences, positioning and choices through which an offering aims to achieve market goals.
example: A startup chooses to target small clinics first and positions its software around reduced paperwork.

label: Masonry
entry_text: Masonry constructs or repairs structures by laying bricks, blocks or stone, typically using mortar or carefully fitted joints.
example: A mason replaces damaged bricks while preserving the wall's pattern.

label: Massage
entry_text: Massage applies controlled manipulation of soft tissue for comfort, relaxation or other therapeutic goals.
example: A practitioner adapts a session to the client's stated comfort and restrictions.

label: Materials testing
entry_text: Materials testing measures a material's properties or behavior under specified conditions to assess suitability or quality.
example: A technician measures the tensile strength of samples from a production batch.

label: Mathematica
entry_text: Mathematica is a computational environment for symbolic and numerical mathematics, programming and visualization.
example: An analyst solves a symbolic equation and plots its solutions in a notebook.

label: Mathematics
entry_text: Using mathematics to solve problems.

label: Matplotlib
entry_text: Matplotlib is a Python library for creating static, animated and interactive visualizations from data.
example: A scientist plots measured values with error bars.

label: McAfee Personal Firewall Plus
entry_text: McAfee Personal Firewall Plus was a personal firewall product for monitoring and controlling network traffic on a computer.
example: A user reviewed application connection requests and blocked an unauthorized program.

label: MCollective
entry_text: MCollective was a framework for issuing coordinated administrative commands across groups of machines.
example: An administrator queried service status across a set of managed hosts.

label: Meal planning and preparation
entry_text: Meal planning and preparation organize what meals are made, procure ingredients and prepare food to suit schedules and dietary needs.
example: A caregiver plans meals for the week and batches vegetables to shorten cooking time.

label: MEAN.JS
entry_text: MEAN.JS is a JavaScript application stack and project scaffold using MongoDB, Express, AngularJS and Node.js.
example: A developer starts a web application with an AngularJS interface and an Express API.
sense_note: Do not assume compatibility with current Angular from the historical name.

label: Meat cutting
entry_text: Meat cutting portions and trims meat into specified cuts while maintaining safe handling and product quality.
example: A butcher separates a larger cut into evenly sized retail portions.

label: Mechanical drafting
entry_text: Mechanical drafting creates engineering drawings that communicate dimensions, tolerances, materials and construction details of mechanical parts or assemblies.
example: A drafter adds hole positions and tolerances to a mounting plate drawing.

label: Mechanical seal
entry_text: A mechanical seal limits fluid leakage at the interface between a rotating shaft and a stationary housing.
example: A pump technician selects a seal compatible with the pumped fluid and operating conditions.

label: Media buying
entry_text: Media buying selects and purchases advertising placements from publishers, platforms or networks within a campaign plan.
example: A media buyer reserves audio ads aimed at reaching commuters.

label: Media production
entry_text: Media production creates, records and assembles content for distribution through formats such as audio, video or digital publications.
example: A producer coordinates recording and editing an interview for an online series.

label: Media relations
entry_text: Media relations manages communication with journalists and outlets to provide accurate information and respond to coverage requests.
example: A communications officer prepares a spokesperson to answer reporters' questions.

label: Media Transfer Protocol
entry_text: Media Transfer Protocol is a standard for transferring and managing media objects between a host and a connected device.
example: A user imports pictures from a portable device without mounting its storage as a disk.

label: MediatR
entry_text: MediatR is a .NET library for routing messages to handlers within an application.
example: An application sends an order command to its registered handler without coupling the caller to that handler directly.

label: Medical billing and coding
entry_text: Medical billing and coding translate documented care into standardized codes and use those codes to prepare and manage payment claims.
example: A coder checks a diagnosis code against the encounter documentation before the billing team submits the claim.

label: Medical device development
entry_text: Medical device development designs, verifies and prepares devices for health applications with attention to intended use, safety and applicable requirements.
example: An engineering team tests whether a prototype meets its stated measurement accuracy.

label: Medical device sales
entry_text: Medical device sales communicate a device's approved uses, capabilities and purchasing terms to prospective customers.
example: A representative explains device compatibility and service arrangements to a hospital purchasing team.

label: Medical office skills
entry_text: Medical office skills support administrative work in a healthcare practice, including scheduling, patient communications and records handling.
example: A coordinator schedules a follow-up and updates the patient's contact information.

label: Medical photography
entry_text: Medical photography captures clinically useful images using appropriate technique, documentation and privacy practices.
example: A trained photographer records successive clinical images with consistent framing for comparison.

label: Medical record formatting
entry_text: Medical record formatting organizes health documentation into standardized, readable structures that preserve relevant clinical information.
example: A specialist converts dictated information into sections for history, examination and assessment.

label: Medical records release
entry_text: Medical records release verifies and fulfills authorized requests to disclose health records under applicable rules and organizational procedures.
example: A records specialist checks authorization and releases only the records covered by the request.

label: Medical ventilator
entry_text: A medical ventilator supports or replaces aspects of breathing by delivering controlled gas flow or pressure.
example: A respiratory therapist monitors how a patient responds to prescribed ventilator support.

label: Mental health assessments
entry_text: Mental health assessment collects and evaluates information about symptoms, functioning and relevant history to guide care or further evaluation.
example: A clinician uses an interview and a screening measure to decide whether a more detailed evaluation is needed.

label: Menu planning
entry_text: Menu planning designs a selection of dishes for a service or period while balancing nutrition, budget, availability and customer needs.
example: A school food service team rotates main dishes and includes options for documented dietary restrictions.

label: MEP design software
entry_text: MEP design software helps engineers model, coordinate and document mechanical, electrical and plumbing systems in buildings.
example: A coordinator checks whether a proposed ventilation duct interferes with a plumbing run.

label: Merchandise management
entry_text: Merchandise management plans and controls the assortment, availability, pricing and presentation of goods for sale.
example: A retailer increases stock of a popular size before a seasonal promotion.

label: Metadata management
entry_text: Metadata management defines and maintains descriptive information about assets so they can be found, interpreted and governed.
example: A data steward records a dataset's owner, refresh schedule and variable definitions.

label: Metal detector
entry_text: A metal detector senses nearby metal objects by measuring their effects on an electromagnetic field.
example: A quality technician uses a detector to screen packaged food for unintended metal fragments.

label: Meteor.js
entry_text: Meteor is a JavaScript framework for building applications across the client and server, with facilities for synchronizing data.
example: A developer builds a shared list that updates connected browser clients as items change.

label: Meter data management
entry_text: Meter data management collects, validates, stores and provides measurements from utility meters for billing and analysis.
example: A utility flags missing hourly readings for review before calculating a bill.

label: Meter Operation Code of Practice Agreement
entry_text: The Meter Operation Code of Practice Agreement governs agreed practices for appointing and operating electricity metering services in a defined market.
example: A metering operator checks its obligations when transferring responsibility for a meter.
sense_note: Verify jurisdiction and applicable revision before citing specific requirements.

label: MicroBlaze
entry_text: MicroBlaze is a configurable soft processor core intended for integration into programmable logic devices.

label: Microchipping
entry_text: Microchipping implants a small electronic identifier so an animal or other subject can be identified with a compatible reader.
example: A shelter scans a found dog and checks its identifier against a registry.
sense_note: The common use is animal identification; distinguish implanting identifiers from fabricating microchips.

label: Microsoft 365

label: Microsoft Bookings

example: A clinic creates a booking page for consultations that reflects staff availability.

label: Microsoft Bot Framework
entry_text: Microsoft Bot Framework provides tools and interfaces for building conversational applications and connecting them to supported channels.
example: A developer connects a support bot to a messaging channel and routes inquiries to its dialog logic.

label: Microsoft Digital Image Suite
entry_text: Microsoft Digital Image Suite was a consumer application suite for editing, organizing and sharing photographs.

label: Microsoft Forms

label: Microsoft HoloLens

label: Microsoft Intune

example: An administrator checks whether enrolled laptops meet disk-encryption requirements.

label: Microsoft Language Interface Pack

example: A user installs and selects a display language to read supported menus in that language.

label: Microsoft Lists
entry_text: Microsoft Lists is a Microsoft 365 tool for tracking structured records in configurable lists and views.
example: A team creates an equipment issue list with filters for department and status.

label: Microsoft Lync
entry_text: Microsoft Lync was a business communication application for instant messaging, presence, calling and meetings.
example: A user checked a colleague's presence before starting an online call.

label: Microsoft Paint

label: Microsoft Sentinel

example: A defender investigates an alert by reviewing related sign-in and system logs.

label: Microsoft Teams live events
entry_text: Microsoft Teams live events refers to a Teams broadcast format in which designated presenters and producers deliver an event to viewers.
example: A producer manages presenters and moderated questions during an organization-wide broadcast.
sense_note: The label is feature-specific; do not infer availability or equate it to every Teams broadcast format.

label: Microsoft Teams Phone
entry_text: Microsoft Teams Phone adds telephony and call-control capabilities to Teams, with external calling through configured connectivity.
example: An organization routes calls for a main number to a queue in Teams.

label: Microsoft Transaction Server
entry_text: Microsoft Transaction Server was a Microsoft platform for running distributed components with services such as transaction coordination and resource management.
example: An enterprise application used it to coordinate a business operation across transactional resources.

label: Microsoft Visio
entry_text: Microsoft Visio is software for creating diagrams such as flowcharts, floor plans and network maps.
example: A process analyst uses Visio to document who approves each step of an invoice workflow.

label: Microsoft Works
entry_text: Microsoft Works was a consumer productivity suite offering basic document, spreadsheet and database functions.
example: A household used its spreadsheet component to track shared expenses.

label: MicroStation
entry_text: MicroStation is computer-aided design software for creating and documenting two- and three-dimensional designs.
example: An engineer drafts a roadway plan and attaches reference drawings.

label: MicroStrategy Desktop
entry_text: MicroStrategy Desktop refers to a desktop business intelligence application for exploring data and building visual analyses.
example: An analyst builds a dashboard from a sales spreadsheet.

entry_text: MicroStrategy Intelligence Server is the server tier that executes and distributes MicroStrategy analytics and manages associated queries and services.
example: A report request is processed by the server and returned to a browser client.

label: MicroStrategy Report Services
entry_text: MicroStrategy Report Services refers to functionality for designing formatted analytical documents and reports.
