label: MicroStrategy Software Development Kit
entry_text: The MicroStrategy Software Development Kit provides programming interfaces and development resources for extending or embedding MicroStrategy features.

label: MicroStrategy Transaction Services
entry_text: MicroStrategy Transaction Services supports data-entry and write-back workflows from analytics interfaces to configured data sources.

label: MicroStrategy Visual Insight
entry_text: MicroStrategy Visual Insight was a visual data-discovery tool for building interactive analyses and dashboards.
example: An analyst drags fields into a chart to explore revenue differences across regions.

label: MicroStrategy Web
entry_text: MicroStrategy Web is a browser interface for accessing reports, dashboards and related business intelligence tools.
example: A manager opens a shared dashboard in a browser and filters it to their region.

label: MIKE URBAN

example: A civil engineer simulates how heavy rainfall affects flows through a stormwater network.

label: Military standards and specifications
entry_text: Military standards and specifications prescribe requirements for materials, equipment, services or processes in military acquisition and operation.
example: A procurement specialist checks whether a supplier's test evidence satisfies a contractually referenced specification.

label: Mind mapping
entry_text: Mind mapping organizes related ideas visually around a central topic using branching associations.
example: A team maps possible causes of delivery delays around a central problem.

label: MITRE ATT&CK
entry_text: MITRE ATT&CK is a knowledge base and framework that organizes observed adversary behavior into tactics and techniques for security analysis.
example: A defender maps known security alerts to ATT&CK categories to identify gaps in monitoring.

label: Mobile application design
entry_text: Mobile application design plans an application's functionality, interactions and presentation for mobile devices and contexts.
example: A designer maps how a commuter would complete a ticket purchase with one hand.

label: Mobile UI design
entry_text: Mobile UI design creates the visual and interactive controls through which users operate a mobile application.
example: A designer chooses button sizes and spacing that make a form easy to tap.

label: Mobile UX design
entry_text: Mobile UX design improves how users accomplish goals in mobile contexts by addressing workflows, usability and accessibility.
example: A researcher observes people using an app on a crowded platform and identifies where the process breaks down.

label: ModelOps
entry_text: ModelOps coordinates the deployment, monitoring, governance and maintenance of analytical models across their operational lifecycle.
example: A model owner tracks production versions and triggers review when validation metrics decline.

label: ModelSim
entry_text: ModelSim is an electronic design simulation tool for testing hardware description language models.
example: An engineer uses a testbench to verify a counter's expected sequence in a simulation.

label: Modern methods of construction
entry_text: Modern methods of construction describe approaches that improve building production through techniques such as off-site manufacture or standardized assemblies.
example: A builder installs factory-made wall panels to reduce on-site assembly time.
sense_note: This is an umbrella term; qualifying methods vary across programs.

label: MODO
entry_text: MODO is a three-dimensional content-creation application for modeling, texturing, rendering and animation.
example: An artist models a product, applies materials and renders a studio image.

label: Moist heat sterilization
entry_text: Moist heat sterilization uses controlled moist heat to inactivate microorganisms, including resistant forms, in compatible materials.
example: A facility uses a validated steam sterilization cycle for compatible instruments.

label: Mold setting
entry_text: Mold setting installs, aligns and prepares a mold in manufacturing equipment for a production run.
example: An operator secures a replacement mold and verifies its alignment before production.

label: Molding
entry_text: Molding forms a material into a defined shape using a mold or cavity.
example: A manufacturer forms plastic housings in a mold that defines their dimensions.
sense_note: This is a general manufacturing sense; distinguish casting, injection molding and architectural moldings where needed.

label: Moldings installation and maintenance
entry_text: Moldings installation and maintenance fit, secure, finish and repair decorative or protective trim on surfaces.
example: A carpenter cuts and fits replacement trim around a damaged doorway.

label: Molecular docking
entry_text: Molecular docking computationally estimates how two molecules might fit together and ranks plausible binding arrangements.
example: A researcher compares simulated poses of candidate compounds in a known protein binding site.

label: Molecular modelling
entry_text: Molecular modelling uses computational representations of molecules to study their structure, interactions or properties.
example: A chemist compares predicted conformations of a small molecule.

label: Molisch's test
entry_text: Molisch's test is a qualitative chemistry assay that indicates the possible presence of carbohydrates by a characteristic color reaction.
example: A laboratory instructor uses it to distinguish a carbohydrate-containing sample from a negative control.

label: Moment.js
entry_text: Moment.js is a JavaScript library for parsing, formatting, comparing and manipulating dates and times.
example: A developer formats a stored date for display in a report.

label: MonetDB
entry_text: MonetDB is a column-oriented database management system designed for analytical workloads.
example: An analyst runs aggregates over selected columns of a large transaction table.

label: MongoEngine
entry_text: MongoEngine is a Python object-document mapper for defining and working with MongoDB documents as Python objects.
example: A developer defines fields and validation rules for a customer document class.

label: Mongoose
entry_text: Mongoose is a JavaScript object data modeling library for MongoDB that provides schemas, validation and database operations.
example: A Node.js application uses a Mongoose schema to validate order records before saving them.

label: MongoVue
entry_text: MongoVue was a graphical desktop client for browsing and querying MongoDB databases.
example: A developer used its interface to inspect documents in a test collection.

label: Monitoring
entry_text: Monitoring/Assessing performance of yourself, other individuals, or organizations to make improvements or take corrective action.

label: Mortgage Electronic Registration System
entry_text: The Mortgage Electronic Registration System is a U.S. registry for tracking specified mortgage interests and servicing rights electronically.
example: A mortgage servicer checks the registry to identify the servicer recorded for a loan.

label: Mosaic art
entry_text: Mosaic art creates images or patterns by arranging small pieces of material such as tile, glass or stone.
example: An artist arranges colored tile fragments to make a decorative wall panel.

label: Motion graphics
entry_text: Motion graphics design communicates information or mood by animating designed visual elements over time.
example: A designer animates a sequence of icons to explain the stages of a service.

label: Motion graphics software
entry_text: Motion graphics software creates and composites animated visual elements such as text, shapes and illustrations.
example: An editor animates a lower-third graphic over an interview clip.

label: Motor control algorithms
entry_text: Motor control algorithms determine drive commands that make an electric motor meet targets such as position, speed or torque.
example: A controller adjusts drive commands to maintain a conveyor's requested speed when its load changes.
sense_note: This is the engineering sense, not computational models of biological motor control.

label: Movable Type
entry_text: Movable Type is a content management and publishing platform used to manage blogs and websites.
example: An editor schedules an article and publishes it using a site template.
sense_note: Here the name denotes the software, not physically movable printing type.

label: Moz Pro
entry_text: Moz Pro is a suite of search engine optimization tools for tasks such as keyword research, site auditing and rank tracking.
example: An analyst identifies pages with broken internal links during a site audit.

label: MP/M
entry_text: MP/M was a multiuser, multitasking operating system in the CP/M family.
example: Several terminal users could run compatible programs on a shared system using MP/M.

label: MRI Software
entry_text: MRI Software provides software for managing real estate operations such as leasing, property accounting and portfolio administration.
example: A property manager tracks lease expirations across several buildings.
sense_note: The name refers to real estate software, not medical imaging.

label: MSTest
entry_text: MSTest is Microsoft's framework for defining and running automated unit tests in .NET applications.
example: A developer marks a method as a test and asserts the expected value of a calculation.

label: Mud pump
entry_text: A mud pump circulates drilling fluid through a drilling system under pressure.
example: A drilling crew uses the pump to send fluid through the drill string during a borehole operation.

label: MuleSoft
entry_text: MuleSoft is an integration platform for connecting applications and data through APIs and integration workflows.
example: An installer links a sales application to an order system so the two can exchange records.

label: Multi-core programming
entry_text: Multi-core programming structures work to run correctly and efficiently across multiple processor cores.
example: A developer splits image processing into independent tasks that run on separate cores.

label: Multi-device design
entry_text: Multi-device design makes an experience usable across device types by adapting layout, controls and workflow to their capabilities.
example: A designer reworks a dense desktop table into a compact touch-friendly view for phones.

label: Multichannel marketing
entry_text: Multichannel marketing coordinates campaigns across multiple ways of reaching an audience.
example: A retailer launches a product through email, paid search and in-store displays.

label: Music instruction
entry_text: Music instruction teaches musical knowledge and skills through demonstrations, guided practice and feedback.
example: A teacher helps a beginner count rhythms before playing a piece.

label: Nagle's algorithm
entry_text: Nagle's algorithm reduces the number of small TCP segments by buffering small writes while earlier data remains unacknowledged, unless enough data accumulate to fill a segment.
example: An application sends several short messages that TCP combines into a larger segment rather than transmitting each immediately.

label: Naive Bayes
entry_text: Naive Bayes is a probabilistic classification method that applies Bayes' rule while treating features as conditionally independent given each class.
example: A spam filter combines evidence from terms in a message to estimate its class.

label: NameNode
entry_text: A NameNode is the Hadoop Distributed File System service that maintains the filesystem namespace and manages metadata about data blocks.
example: A client asks the NameNode where to find the blocks of a requested file.

label: NAnt
entry_text: NAnt is a build automation tool that runs XML-defined tasks, commonly for .NET projects.
example: A legacy build uses NAnt to compile software and package the resulting artifacts.

label: Nasotracheal suctioning
entry_text: Nasotracheal suctioning is a clinical procedure that removes airway secretions using suction through a catheter passed via the nose.
example: A trained clinician performs it when clinically indicated for a patient unable to clear secretions.

label: National Geothermal Data System
entry_text: The National Geothermal Data System was a U.S. data-sharing initiative providing discoverable information relevant to geothermal resources.
example: A researcher locates mapped well and temperature records for a preliminary resource assessment.
sense_note: Current service availability is not implied.

label: Nationwide Multistate Licensing System
entry_text: The Nationwide Multistate Licensing System provides infrastructure for managing licenses and registrations in participating financial services jurisdictions.
example: A mortgage company submits an application and tracks required filings through the system.

label: NativeScript
entry_text: NativeScript is a framework for building native mobile applications with JavaScript or TypeScript and access to native platform APIs.
example: An app developer builds a mobile interface using native controls from a shared codebase.

label: Natural language processing
entry_text: Natural language processing develops computational methods to analyze, interpret or generate human language.
example: A system extracts organization names from a set of news articles.

label: Navigational aid
entry_text: A navigational aid is a device, signal or reference that helps a navigator determine position or follow a safe route.
example: A mariner checks a channel marker against the chart before turning.

example: A coordinator checks where a planned duct intersects a structural beam.

label: NedGraphics
entry_text: NedGraphics provides design software for textile workflows such as creating patterns and preparing woven, printed or knitted designs.
example: A textile designer previews how a repeat pattern will look across a length of fabric.

label: Needle localization
entry_text: Needle localization is a clinical technique that uses imaging and a needle-guided marker or wire to identify a target for a subsequent procedure.
example: A specialist marks a nonpalpable breast lesion for the surgical team.
sense_note: Distinguish preoperative localization from diagnostic biopsy.

label: Negotiation
entry_text: Bringing others together and trying to reconcile differences.

label: Neonatal intensive care nursing
entry_text: Neonatal intensive care nursing provides specialized assessment, monitoring and treatment support for critically ill or premature newborns.
example: A nurse monitors an infant's response to respiratory support in a neonatal intensive care unit.

label: .NET development
entry_text: .NET development builds and maintains applications using the .NET runtime, libraries and language ecosystem.
example: A developer builds a C# web API and tests the behavior of its endpoints.

label: Net Promoter Score

example: A service team computes NPS from a survey and examines the comments behind the ratings.

label: Nette

example: A developer uses Nette forms to validate input and render errors to the user.

label: Network intrusion detection system
entry_text: A network intrusion detection system monitors network traffic for signs of suspicious or prohibited activity and generates alerts.
example: A defender reviews an alert for an unusual pattern of connection attempts.

label: Nexpose
entry_text: Nexpose is a vulnerability assessment tool that scans authorized assets and reports identified weaknesses for remediation.
example: A security team reviews a scan report to prioritize missing security updates.

example: A developer builds a product page with server-rendered data and client-side controls.

label: ngAnimate

example: An AngularJS list fades new rows in as they are inserted.

example: An administrator starts a background batch job at lower CPU priority than interactive workloads.

label: NICE Workforce Management
entry_text: NICE Workforce Management supports staffing forecasts, scheduling and adherence monitoring, particularly in contact centers.
example: A supervisor plans shifts using forecast call volumes.

label: Nightwatch.js
entry_text: Nightwatch.js is a JavaScript framework for automating browser interactions and end-to-end tests.
example: A test opens a product page, adds an item and checks that it appears in the cart.

label: NIH Stroke Scale
entry_text: The NIH Stroke Scale is a standardized clinical assessment that scores neurological deficits associated with stroke.
example: A trained clinician records a score to help track changes over time.

label: NIST Cybersecurity Framework
entry_text: The NIST Cybersecurity Framework organizes outcomes for managing and communicating organizational cybersecurity risk.
example: A team compares its existing security practices with a target profile to identify gaps.

example: A system owner uses the framework's monitor step to plan ongoing review of controls.

label: NIST SP 800-53
entry_text: NIST SP 800-53 catalogs security and privacy controls for information systems and organizations.
example: A team selects relevant controls for managing account access and documenting related safeguards.

label: NIST SP 800 series
entry_text: The NIST SP 800 series contains special publications providing guidance on information security and related privacy and risk topics.
example: An engineer locates the publication applicable to an organization's security assessment.

label: Nonverbal communication

example: A developer runs nosetests to discover and execute tests in a legacy project.

example: A team links decision notes to tasks in a searchable project workspace.

label: npm

example: A developer installs the dependency versions recorded in a project's lockfile.
sense_note: May refer specifically to the command-line tool or the registry ecosystem.

entry_text: Nuance PDF Converter refers to a family of PDF utilities for creating, editing or converting PDF documents.

example: A dietitian documents an intake problem and the factors contributing to it.

label: Nutrition intervention

example: A dietitian and patient agree on a practical change and a way to monitor it.

label: Nutritional assessment
entry_text: Nutritional assessment gathers and evaluates information such as intake, weight history and clinical findings to characterize nutritional status.
example: A clinician compares diet records and recent weight changes to assess potential concerns.

label: Nutritional screening
entry_text: Nutritional screening uses a brief structured check to flag people who may need more complete nutritional assessment.
example: A hospital asks about recent unexpected weight loss at intake.

label: Nuxt

example: A developer builds a product page whose initial content can be rendered on the server.

label: NW.js

example: A developer bundles a web-based editor as a desktop application that can open local files.

label: OBD-II

example: A technician reads a stored diagnostic code with a compatible scan tool.

label: Object-oriented design
entry_text: Object-oriented design organizes software around objects and their responsibilities, interactions and interfaces.
example: A designer separates account state from transaction processing while defining how objects communicate.

label: Object-oriented programming
entry_text: Object-oriented programming implements programs using objects that combine data and behavior, with mechanisms such as encapsulation and polymorphism.
example: A graphics program calls the same draw method on different kinds of shapes.

label: Observability
entry_text: Observability is the ability to infer a system's internal behavior from emitted signals such as logs, metrics and traces.
example: An engineer follows traces and latency metrics to identify which dependency slows a request.

label: OCLC Connexion

example: A cataloger updates the description of a book and records that the library holds it.

label: OCUnit

label: Office 365

label: OneTrust

example: A privacy team tracks requests to access personal information and their resolution status.

label: Online demonstration

example: A trainer shares a screen and shows a participant how to complete a form.

label: OpenAPI Specification

label: OpenNI

sense_note: The label may occur as a legacy brand; verify applicable product documentation.

label: OpenTSDB
entry_text: OpenTSDB is an open-source database system for storing and querying large volumes of time-series measurements.
example: An operations team queries a week of server utilization measurements by host.

label: Operation and Control
entry_text: Controlling operations of equipment or systems.

label: Operational risk mitigation
entry_text: Operational risk mitigation identifies and reduces potential losses arising from failures in people, processes, systems or external events.
example: A finance team adds independent approval to a payment workflow to reduce processing errors.

label: Operationalizing AI
entry_text: Operationalizing AI moves an AI system into sustained use with deployment, monitoring, governance and maintenance processes.
example: A team sets up model monitoring and a fallback workflow before releasing an automated classifier.

label: Operations Analysis
entry_text: Analyzing needs and product requirements to create a design.

label: Operations analytics
entry_text: Operations analytics analyzes operational data to understand performance and make decisions about processes, resources or service delivery.
example: A warehouse analyst identifies which picking steps contribute most to delays.

label: Operations Monitoring
entry_text: Watching gauges, dials, or other indicators to make sure a machine is working properly.

label: Ophthalmic surgical assisting
entry_text: Ophthalmic surgical assisting supports eye surgery by preparing equipment, maintaining sterile conditions and assisting the surgical team within assigned duties.
example: An assistant checks that the surgeon's specified instruments and supplies are ready before a procedure.

label: Optical power meter
entry_text: An optical power meter measures optical signal power, commonly in fiber-optic systems.
example: A technician measures received signal power at the end of a fiber link to check its loss budget.

label: Optimization software
entry_text: Optimization software uses mathematical algorithms to search for solutions that improve a stated objective subject to constraints.
example: A planner uses a solver to minimize staffing costs while covering every required shift.

label: Optitex
entry_text: Optitex is digital design software for developing apparel patterns and simulating how garments fit and drape.
example: A pattern maker previews a jacket in three dimensions before cutting a sample.

label: Oracle Advanced Queuing
entry_text: Oracle Advanced Queuing provides database-integrated message queues for asynchronous communication between applications.
example: An order service enqueues an event that a separate fulfillment process consumes.

label: Oracle Application Framework
entry_text: Oracle Application Framework is a Java-based framework for building web interfaces and business applications in Oracle E-Business Suite.
example: A developer extends a self-service page while retaining the application's navigation and data model.
sense_note: Often identified as OA Framework; distinguish from Oracle Application Development Framework.

label: Oracle Application Integration Architecture
entry_text: Oracle Application Integration Architecture provides frameworks and integration assets for connecting enterprise applications through service-oriented patterns.
example: A team uses a common message structure to exchange order data between separate applications.

label: Oracle Autonomous Database
entry_text: Oracle Autonomous Database is a managed Oracle cloud database service that automates many provisioning, maintenance and tuning tasks.
example: A team deploys a reporting database without scheduling routine patching itself.

label: Oracle BI Answers
entry_text: Oracle BI Answers is an Oracle Business Intelligence interface for creating ad hoc analyses against a business data model.
example: An analyst builds a sales-by-region table by selecting dimensions and measures.

label: Oracle Business Activity Monitoring
entry_text: Oracle Business Activity Monitoring tracks business events and process metrics to support dashboards and alerts.
example: An operations manager monitors the number of orders approaching their processing deadline.

label: Oracle Clinical
entry_text: Oracle Clinical is software supporting capture, management and validation of clinical study data.
example: A study data manager reviews validation findings before finalizing a dataset.

label: Oracle Cloud
entry_text: Oracle Cloud is Oracle's portfolio of cloud infrastructure, platform services and applications provided remotely.
example: A team runs a database and its application on managed cloud resources.
sense_note: The label may mean the broad portfolio or Oracle Cloud Infrastructure specifically.

label: Oracle EU Sovereign Cloud
entry_text: Oracle EU Sovereign Cloud is an Oracle cloud offering designed for workloads subject to European data residency and operational sovereignty requirements.
example: An organization evaluates whether its hosting arrangement satisfies internal European residency requirements.
sense_note: No particular regulatory compliance is guaranteed solely by using the offering.

label: Oracle Fixed Assets
entry_text: Oracle Fixed Assets is an enterprise accounting module for recording, depreciating, transferring and retiring fixed assets.
example: A controller records the acquisition of equipment and runs its periodic depreciation calculation.

label: Oracle GoldenGate
entry_text: Oracle GoldenGate is software for capturing and replicating data changes between supported systems.
example: A reporting system receives updates from an operational database without relying on periodic full copies.

label: Oracle HRMS
entry_text: Oracle HRMS is an enterprise software suite for managing human resources records and related workforce processes.
example: A personnel team records a new employee's assignment and maintains their employment history.

label: Oracle OLAP
entry_text: Oracle OLAP is Oracle technology for multidimensional analysis of data, including aggregation across business dimensions.
example: An analyst explores revenue totals by region, product and quarter.

label: Oracle Primavera
entry_text: Oracle Primavera is a family of project management tools used for scheduling, resource planning and project controls.
example: A project planner uses a schedule to identify construction tasks on the critical path.

label: Oracle Reports
entry_text: Oracle Reports is a toolset for designing and publishing formatted reports from database data.
example: A developer creates a report template that renders a monthly transaction summary.

label: Oracle Workflow
entry_text: Oracle Workflow provides facilities for defining, routing and tracking business processes and notifications.
example: A purchase request is routed to the approvers defined in its workflow.

label: Oral cancer screening
entry_text: Oral cancer screening looks for signs that warrant further evaluation through visual or tactile examination of the mouth and surrounding areas.
example: A dental clinician refers a patient for evaluation of an unexplained oral lesion.

label: Organizational culture change
entry_text: Organizational culture change works to shift shared norms and everyday behaviors through consistent leadership, incentives and practices.
example: A department reinforces a new safety culture by rewarding reports of near misses.

label: Organizational leadership
entry_text: Organizational leadership guides people and decisions toward shared goals while managing resources, alignment and accountability.
example: A leader clarifies priorities when two teams compete for the same resources.

label: OrientDB
entry_text: OrientDB is a database engine that supports document and graph data models.
example: A developer stores customer records and traverses relationships between related accounts.

label: Orthopaedic nursing
entry_text: Orthopaedic nursing provides care for people with musculoskeletal injuries, conditions or procedures.
example: A nurse monitors comfort and mobility goals after a patient's joint surgery.

label: OpenTelemetry
entry_text: OpenTelemetry is a set of open specifications and libraries for generating, collecting and exporting telemetry such as traces, metrics and logs.
example: An engineer instruments a service to export request traces to an observability backend.
sense_note: OpenTelemetry is instrumentation and transport infrastructure, not itself an analytics backend.

label: OutSystems
entry_text: OutSystems is a low-code platform for building, deploying and maintaining enterprise applications.
example: A developer uses visual tools to assemble an approval app and connect it to business data.

label: Over-the-road driving
entry_text: Over-the-road driving operates commercial vehicles over extended routes while managing schedules, cargo, vehicle condition and driving requirements.
example: A driver plans stops for a multistate delivery and completes the required vehicle checks.

label: Overhead cost analysis
entry_text: Overhead cost analysis identifies and evaluates indirect costs and how they are allocated across activities, products or departments.
example: An accountant compares production support costs when revising allocation rates.

label: Overhead crane operation
entry_text: Overhead crane operation uses a bridge, gantry or similar overhead crane to lift and move loads within operating limits.
example: A trained operator follows an approved lift plan to place a component at a workstation.

label: package.json
entry_text: A package.json file is a JSON manifest that describes a JavaScript project or package and may declare dependencies, scripts and entry points.
example: A maintainer adds a test script and declares project dependencies in its manifest.
sense_note: It is a configuration format, not an executable tool.

label: Packaging machine operation
entry_text: Packaging machine operation sets up and monitors equipment that fills, wraps, seals or labels goods for distribution.
example: An operator checks that package seals and labels meet specifications during a run.

label: Padrino
entry_text: Padrino is a Ruby web application framework built on Sinatra that adds project organization and application components.
example: A developer adds admin routes and templates to a small web application.

label: Page layout
entry_text: Page layout arranges text, images and white space on a printed or digital page to support readability and intent.
example: A designer positions headlines and columns to create a clear reading order.

label: Pallet building
entry_text: Pallet building arranges and secures goods on a pallet for stable storage, handling or shipment.
example: A warehouse worker stacks cartons within load limits and secures them before dispatch.

label: Palm OS
entry_text: Palm OS was an operating system for handheld devices such as Palm organizers and some early smartphones.
example: A user synchronized appointments between a Palm OS organizer and a desktop computer.

label: pandas
entry_text: Pandas is a Python library for manipulating labeled tabular and time-series data.
example: An analyst joins two tables by customer identifier and calculates totals by month.

label: Paperwork Reduction Act
entry_text: The Paperwork Reduction Act is a U.S. federal law governing many agency information collections and their burden on the public.
example: An agency estimates respondent burden when preparing an information collection for review.

label: Parallel computing
entry_text: Parallel computing executes multiple parts of a computation at the same time using multiple processing resources.
example: A scientific program distributes independent simulations across available processors.

label: PARI/GP
entry_text: PARI/GP is a computational mathematics system focused on number theory, with a C library and an interactive GP interface.
example: A mathematician factors an integer and experiments with number-theoretic functions in GP.

label: Parrot AR.Drone
entry_text: Parrot AR.Drone was a small remotely operated quadcopter with onboard cameras and networked controls.
example: A robotics student used its camera to observe a marked indoor test course.

label: Passport.js
entry_text: Passport.js is authentication middleware for Node.js applications that supports different login mechanisms through strategies.
example: A web service uses a strategy to handle sign-in through an approved identity provider.

label: Pathlore
entry_text: Pathlore refers to learning management software used to administer training, enrollment and progress records.
example: A training administrator assigns employees to a course and checks completion.
sense_note: Legacy product label; confirm the exact edition before claiming features beyond learning management.

label: Patient coordination
entry_text: Patient coordination organizes appointments, referrals, communications and care transitions among patients and providers.
example: A coordinator ensures a specialist has the referral documents and confirms the appointment with the patient.

label: Patient education
entry_text: Patient education helps people understand health information and participate in decisions or self-care appropriate to their needs.
example: A clinician uses teach-back to check whether a patient understands follow-up instructions.

label: Patient transfer
entry_text: Patient transfer moves a patient safely between positions, surfaces or care locations while managing mobility and continuity of care.
example: A care team uses the appropriate equipment to move a patient from a bed to a chair.
sense_note: May refer to physical movement or transfer of care between facilities; document the intended sense.

label: Pattern Lab
entry_text: Pattern Lab is a tool for developing and previewing reusable interface patterns and their composition into pages.
example: A front-end team checks how a card component works in multiple layouts.

label: Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard
entry_text: The Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard defines security requirements for protecting payment card data in applicable environments.
example: A merchant documents controls around the systems that handle cardholder data.

label: PDF conversion
entry_text: PDF conversion changes a file to PDF or transforms a PDF into another format while managing formatting and data fidelity.
example: A user converts a text-based PDF to an editable document and checks table alignment.

label: PDF generation
entry_text: PDF generation creates a PDF document from source content, templates or application data.
example: A billing service renders a PDF invoice from order and payment records.

label: PDF.js
entry_text: PDF.js is a JavaScript library for parsing and rendering PDF documents in a web environment.
example: A browser application uses PDF.js to display document pages without a separate viewer plug-in.

label: PDF viewer
entry_text: A PDF viewer renders PDF content for reading, navigation and related tasks such as searching or annotation where supported.
example: A reviewer searches a PDF manual for a part number.

label: PDFlib
entry_text: PDFlib is a programming library for generating and processing PDF documents.
example: An application uses PDFlib to create reports that embed fonts and charts.

label: PDFNet
entry_text: PDFNet is a software development kit for adding PDF viewing, editing, conversion or processing capabilities to applications.
example: A document application uses the SDK to add comments to PDF pages.

label: PDFtk
entry_text: PDFtk is a tool for manipulating PDF files, including combining, splitting and rotating pages.
example: A user assembles several separate scans into a single multi-page PDF.

label: Peachtree Accounting
entry_text: Peachtree Accounting was desktop accounting software for small-business bookkeeping, invoicing and financial reporting.
example: A bookkeeper recorded customer invoices and produced a balance sheet.
sense_note: Legacy brand; do not infer capabilities of current Sage products.

label: Pelvic floor rehabilitation
entry_text: Pelvic floor rehabilitation assesses and treats pelvic floor muscle dysfunction to improve symptoms and function.
example: A qualified clinician develops an individualized plan based on an assessment of movement and symptoms.

label: Percona XtraDB
entry_text: Percona XtraDB was an enhanced InnoDB-compatible storage engine developed for MySQL-family database servers.
example: A database administrator evaluated XtraDB when tuning a legacy transactional workload.
sense_note: Do not confuse the storage engine with the Percona XtraDB Cluster product.

label: PerformanceAnalytics
entry_text: PerformanceAnalytics is an R package for analyzing financial returns, investment performance and portfolio risk.
example: An analyst plots the drawdown history of a set of monthly returns.

label: Periscope
entry_text: Periscope was a social video platform for broadcasting live video and interacting with viewers.
example: A presenter streamed a live event and responded to comments during the broadcast.
sense_note: The platform hint suggests the discontinued streaming service; distinguish an optical periscope and Periscope Data.

label: Periscope Data
entry_text: Periscope Data was a business intelligence platform for querying data and sharing dashboards and analyses.
example: An analyst publishes a dashboard driven by SQL queries against a data warehouse.

label: Permit to work
entry_text: Permit to work is a formal safety control that authorizes specified work only under documented conditions, responsibilities and precautions.
example: A site supervisor reviews and authorizes a permit before a contractor begins covered work.

label: Personal Printer Data Stream
entry_text: Personal Printer Data Stream is an IBM printer command language for describing page content and controlling compatible printers.
example: A legacy application sends PPDS commands to format text on a supported printer.

label: Personal protective equipment
entry_text: Personal protective equipment consists of items worn to reduce exposure to hazards that remain after other controls are applied.
example: A worker uses appropriate eye protection during a designated workshop task.

label: Personalization
entry_text: Personalization adapts content, products or interactions to an individual's context, behavior or stated preferences.
example: A news service lets readers prioritize stories from topics they choose.

label: Persuasion
entry_text: Persuading others to change their minds or behavior.

label: PEST analysis
entry_text: PEST analysis examines political, economic, social and technological factors in an organization's external environment.
example: A strategy team evaluates how changing consumer habits and new technology could affect a market entry.

label: Pet insurance sales
entry_text: Pet insurance sales explain animal insurance products, terms and exclusions and assist customers with purchases under applicable rules.
example: A representative explains waiting periods and coverage limits for a prospective policy.

label: Phalcon
entry_text: Phalcon is a PHP web framework implemented in part as a native extension.
example: A developer uses its routing and model components to build a database-backed web application.

label: PhantomJS
entry_text: PhantomJS was a scriptable headless browser based on WebKit and used for automated page interactions.
example: A team used it to render test pages without a visible browser window.
sense_note: Historical tool; do not imply current support or browser compatibility.

label: Pharmaceutical batch documentation
entry_text: Pharmaceutical batch documentation records the materials, processing steps, checks, deviations and approvals for a specific pharmaceutical production batch.
example: A quality reviewer checks that the reported lot numbers match the approved material records.

label: Pharmacy operations
entry_text: Pharmacy operations coordinate the workflow, inventory, staffing and quality controls that support dispensing and related services.
example: A pharmacy manager monitors order queues and verifies that stock records reflect received items.

label: Photo retouching
entry_text: Photo retouching makes targeted corrections or enhancements to a photograph while maintaining the desired appearance and fidelity.
example: An editor removes scanner dust without altering the image's subject.

label: phpBB
entry_text: phpBB is web forum software for hosting threaded discussions and managing users, categories and moderation.
example: A moderator creates a support category and manages posts reported by members.

label: phpDesigner
entry_text: phpDesigner is a development environment for writing, editing and debugging PHP and related web code.
example: A developer uses the editor to trace an error in a PHP page.

label: phpdocx
entry_text: phpdocx is a PHP library for generating and modifying Microsoft Word documents in DOCX format.
example: A service creates personalized reports from a reusable document template.

label: PhpED
entry_text: PhpED is an integrated development environment for developing and debugging PHP applications.
example: A programmer sets a breakpoint to inspect a variable during local execution.

label: PHPExcel
entry_text: PHPExcel was a PHP library for reading, writing and manipulating spreadsheet files.
example: A legacy application used PHPExcel to export a workbook with a summary worksheet.
sense_note: Distinguish this historical project from its successor PhpSpreadsheet.

label: phpFox
entry_text: phpFox is software for building online communities and social networking websites.
example: An organization creates a community site with member profiles and groups.

label: phpGroupWare
entry_text: phpGroupWare was a web-based collaboration suite providing shared tools such as calendars and contacts.
example: A team used its shared calendar to coordinate meeting times.
sense_note: Historical product label.

label: phpLDAPadmin
entry_text: phpLDAPadmin is a web interface for browsing and administering LDAP directories.
example: An administrator reviews directory entries through its browser interface.

label: phpList
entry_text: phpList is software for managing mailing lists and sending email campaigns to their subscribers.
example: A nonprofit sends a newsletter to an opted-in mailing list.

label: PHPMailer
entry_text: PHPMailer is a PHP library for composing and sending email, with support for SMTP and multipart messages.
example: A web application sends a receipt email with a plain-text version and a PDF attachment.

label: phpPgAdmin
entry_text: phpPgAdmin is a web-based administration tool for PostgreSQL databases.
example: A database administrator inspects the columns and constraints in a test database.

label: PHPUnit
entry_text: PHPUnit is a PHP testing framework for writing and running automated tests and assertions.
example: A developer tests whether a price calculation rounds correctly for a sample order.

label: phpWebSite
entry_text: phpWebSite was a content management system for creating and administering websites with modular components.
example: A site editor used it to publish a news article and a calendar entry.
sense_note: Historical product label.

label: PhpWiki
entry_text: PhpWiki is wiki software written in PHP that allows users to create and collaboratively edit pages.
example: A team maintains a set of linked reference pages for recurring procedures.

label: Physical modelling synthesis
entry_text: Physical modelling synthesis generates sound by simulating the behavior of a sound-producing physical system.
example: A synthesizer models how a plucked string vibrates and loses energy over time.
sense_note: The label is interpreted in its audio-synthesis sense.

label: Physical vapor deposition
entry_text: Physical vapor deposition applies a thin coating by vaporizing material and depositing it onto a surface in a controlled environment.
example: A manufacturer coats a component with a thin wear-resistant layer.

label: Piano playing
entry_text: Piano playing uses keyboard technique, musical interpretation and coordination to perform music on a piano.
example: A pianist balances the loudness of accompaniment and melody while playing a piece.

label: Pilates
entry_text: Pilates is a method of controlled exercise emphasizing coordination, breathing and muscular control.
example: An instructor guides a participant through a controlled movement while cueing breathing.

label: Pinterest
entry_text: Pinterest is a visual discovery platform where users find, save and organize images and linked ideas into collections.
example: A designer collects reference images in a project board.

label: Pipeline pigging
entry_text: Pipeline pigging sends an internal device through a pipeline to clean, separate materials or inspect its condition.
example: An operator reviews the inspection records from a pig run to plan maintenance.

label: Pivotal Tracker
entry_text: Pivotal Tracker was an agile project management tool that organized software work into stories, backlogs and iterations.
example: A team used its backlog to prioritize features for a forthcoming iteration.

label: Pixel art
entry_text: Pixel art creates digital images by deliberately arranging and coloring individual pixels or small pixel clusters.
example: A game artist creates a character sprite that remains readable at a low resolution.

label: PixiJS
entry_text: PixiJS is a JavaScript rendering library for displaying high-performance two-dimensional graphics on the web.
example: A developer uses animated sprites to display a game scene in a web page.

label: Plant design
entry_text: Plant design plans the layout, equipment and supporting systems of a facility to meet process, safety and operating requirements.
example: An engineering team positions equipment to allow maintenance access and efficient material flow.
sense_note: The likely sense is industrial facility design, not arranging plants in a landscape.

label: Plant Design Management System
entry_text: The Plant Design Management System was a three-dimensional computer-aided design system for industrial plant layouts and equipment models.
example: An engineer coordinates piping routes with structural components in a shared plant model.
sense_note: The generic label is interpreted as the product commonly abbreviated PDMS.

label: PlateSpin Migrate
entry_text: PlateSpin Migrate is software for transferring server workloads between supported physical, virtual or cloud environments.
example: An administrator migrates an existing server workload to a virtual environment and validates its operation.

label: PlateSpin Protect
entry_text: PlateSpin Protect replicates server workloads and supports their recovery after service disruption.
example: A team tests failover for a protected workload in a recovery environment.

label: Play therapy
entry_text: Play therapy uses play within a therapeutic relationship to help children express experiences and develop coping skills.
example: A trained therapist observes themes as a child uses figures to tell a story.

label: PLINK
entry_text: PLINK is a command-line toolset for managing genotype data and running population genetics or association analyses.
example: An analyst checks missing genotype calls before comparing cohorts.
sense_note: The uppercase label suggests the genetics tool; distinguish PuTTY's Plink.

label: Plumbing drawing
entry_text: Plumbing drawing documents pipe routes, fixtures and connections for plumbing systems.
example: A drafter marks fixtures and drainage routes on a floor plan.

label: Plumbing plans examination
entry_text: Plumbing plans examination reviews plumbing drawings and supporting documents against applicable requirements for approval.
example: An examiner requests a missing drainage layout detail.

label: Point-to-Point Tunneling Protocol
entry_text: Point-to-Point Tunneling Protocol tunnels PPP traffic over an IP network and was historically used for virtual private networks.
example: An administrator identifies it in legacy remote-access documentation.
sense_note: Identifying this legacy protocol is not an endorsement for new deployments.

label: Police baton
entry_text: A police baton is a handheld impact weapon issued in some law-enforcement settings under agency policy and legal controls.

label: Policy analysis
entry_text: Policy analysis evaluates policy options, effects and tradeoffs to inform decisions.
example: An analyst compares the distributional effects of two transit funding proposals.

label: Policy research and analysis
entry_text: Policy research and analysis gathers evidence about a public or institutional issue and evaluates how it informs policy choices.
example: A researcher synthesizes evaluations to compare alternative housing policies.

label: Poll Everywhere
entry_text: Poll Everywhere collects and displays audience responses during presentations or events.
example: An instructor displays anonymous responses to a concept check.

label: Polycom
entry_text: Polycom refers to a product family for business voice and video communication.
example: A company equips a conference room with an audio and video device.
sense_note: Could also name the company or a particular model.

label: Positive airway pressure
entry_text: Positive airway pressure uses pressurized airflow to help maintain an open airway or support breathing.
example: A clinician checks whether a patient can comfortably use a prescribed device.
sense_note: The technique includes multiple modes.

label: POSIX
entry_text: POSIX is a family of standards specifying portable operating-system interfaces, including APIs and shell utilities for Unix-like environments.
example: A developer uses a standardized interface to build software for multiple compatible operating systems.

label: Post Office Protocol
entry_text: Post Office Protocol retrieves email from a server and is commonly used in its POP3 version.
example: An email client downloads messages from a configured POP3 mailbox.

label: PostCSS
entry_text: PostCSS lets JavaScript plugins analyze or transform CSS.
example: A build uses a plugin to add selected browser prefixes before publishing stylesheets.

label: PostgreSQL
entry_text: PostgreSQL is an open-source relational database system supporting SQL, transactions and extensible data features.
example: A service stores orders and queries them using joins and aggregates.

label: Postman
entry_text: Postman designs, sends, documents and tests API requests.
example: A developer checks a response body and status code from an internal test endpoint.

label: Postorder traversal
entry_text: Postorder traversal visits a node's children before the node itself, conventionally visiting left before right for a binary tree.
example: A program calculates a directory's total size after calculating the sizes of its subdirectories.

label: PouchDB
entry_text: PouchDB is a JavaScript database library for storing documents locally and synchronizing with compatible remote services.
example: A form saves entries offline and synchronizes them when connectivity returns.

label: Power Automate
entry_text: Power Automate is a Microsoft tool for automating tasks and workflows across applications and services.
example: A workflow requests manager approval whenever a form is submitted.

label: Power flow study
entry_text: A power flow study calculates operating conditions in an electrical network under specified load and generation assumptions.
example: An engineer checks line loading and bus voltages for a proposed expansion.

label: Power tool operation
entry_text: Power tool operation uses electrically, pneumatically or otherwise powered tools to perform work under appropriate controls.
example: A trained worker uses a powered drill to prepare holes for a fixture.

label: Powered industrial truck operation
entry_text: Powered industrial truck operation controls forklifts and similar workplace equipment for moving materials within safe operating limits.
example: A trained operator moves a palletized load to an approved storage location.

label: PowerSchool
entry_text: PowerSchool provides software for managing student information and other school administration processes.
example: A school office records student enrollment and checks attendance.

label: Pre-sales engineering
entry_text: Pre-sales engineering uses technical expertise to determine whether a proposed solution meets a prospective customer's requirements.
example: An engineer builds a proof of concept for a requested integration.

label: Predictive analytics software
entry_text: Predictive analytics software builds, evaluates or applies statistical and machine learning models to forecast outcomes from data.
example: An analyst uses software to estimate demand from past sales.

label: Predictive modelling
entry_text: Predictive modelling fits a model to estimate unknown outcomes using available inputs.
example: A team predicts delivery times from past orders and evaluates errors on new data.

label: Presentation design
entry_text: Presentation design organizes a message into clear visual material suited to its audience and setting.
example: A designer replaces a dense slide with a labeled chart and an explanatory sentence.

label: Presentation software
entry_text: Presentation software creates and delivers structured visual presentations, typically as sequences of slides.
example: A trainer prepares slides with diagrams and presenter notes.

label: PrestoDB
entry_text: PrestoDB is a distributed SQL query engine for running analytical queries across data sources without requiring the engine to own the storage.
example: An analyst uses connected sources to combine data-lake events with information from a database.

label: Preventive dental care
entry_text: Preventive dental care reduces the risk or progression of oral disease through routine care, monitoring and education.
example: A dental team provides preventive services and teaches the patient how to improve daily oral hygiene.

label: Prezi
entry_text: Prezi is presentation software that can arrange content on a visual canvas and navigate between areas through animated transitions.
example: A presenter zooms from a project overview into each workstream.

label: Price negotiation
entry_text: Price negotiation seeks an agreed price and related terms through discussion of value, constraints and alternatives.
example: A buyer offers a larger order in exchange for a volume discount.

label: PrimeRx
entry_text: PrimeRx is pharmacy management software supporting prescription processing, inventory and dispensing workflows.
example: A pharmacy records prescription status and monitors related inventory.

label: PRINCE2
entry_text: PRINCE2 is a structured project management method organizing governance, roles and work around controlled stages and business justification.
example: A project board reviews the business case and next-stage plan before authorizing further work.

label: Principles for Responsible Banking
entry_text: The Principles for Responsible Banking provide a framework for aligning banking strategy and practice with sustainable development and tracking impacts.
example: A participating bank assesses its major impacts and sets targets for areas it can influence.

label: Print design
entry_text: Print design prepares visual material for physical printing with attention to layout, typography, color and production constraints.
example: A designer sets the bleed on a brochure to meet the printer's specifications.

label: Printed circuit board design
entry_text: Printed circuit board design arranges components and conductive traces while meeting electrical, mechanical and manufacturing requirements.
example: An engineer checks that connectors and traces fit a sensor board and its enclosure.

label: Privacy impact assessment
entry_text: A privacy impact assessment identifies how an activity handles personal information, evaluates risks and documents safeguards.
example: A team checks whether a service form collects more information than needed.

label: Privileged access management
entry_text: Privileged access management controls, monitors and limits the use of accounts or credentials with elevated permissions.
example: An administrator receives approved temporary access that expires after a maintenance window.

label: Problem solving
entry_text: Problem solving identifies a gap or obstacle, develops possible responses and evaluates whether a chosen solution works.
example: A support team compares explanations for delivery errors and tests the most likely cause.

label: Process hazard analysis
entry_text: Process hazard analysis systematically examines what could go wrong in a process and evaluates potential consequences and safeguards.
example: A team reviews a proposed facility change to identify hazards requiring further controls.

label: Process improvement
entry_text: Process improvement measures how work performs and changes steps or conditions to achieve better results.
example: A team removes redundant approval steps and checks whether turnaround time improves.

label: Process management
entry_text: Process management defines, coordinates, monitors and maintains how recurring work is performed.
example: A supervisor assigns owners and checks whether cases move through each required stage.

label: Process piping
entry_text: Process piping is the design, installation or maintenance of piping that conveys fluids used in an industrial process.
example: A designer specifies an appropriate piping layout for moving material between vessels.
sense_note: The label may denote the system itself or the associated work discipline.

label: Processing.js
entry_text: Processing.js was a JavaScript implementation for running Processing-style graphics programs in a web browser.
example: An artist used it to display an interactive drawing on a webpage.
sense_note: Distinguish it from the Processing desktop environment and p5.js.

label: Procore
entry_text: Procore is a construction management platform for coordinating project information, work and participants.
example: A contractor uses it to track requests for information and project documents.

label: Product analysis
entry_text: Product analysis evaluates a product's characteristics, performance or market fit to inform decisions.
example: A team compares proposed features with customer needs and development constraints.

label: Product analytics
entry_text: Product analytics uses behavioral and product data to understand how people use a product and where outcomes can improve.
example: A team analyzes which step of onboarding accounts for the most abandonment.

label: Product benchmarking
entry_text: Product benchmarking compares a product against other offerings or defined standards using consistent criteria.
example: A reviewer measures battery life across comparable devices using the same test conditions.

label: Product catalogue management
entry_text: Product catalogue management maintains the accuracy, structure and distribution of records describing products and offerings.
example: A catalog manager updates product dimensions and propagates the approved values to storefronts.

label: Product leadership
entry_text: Product leadership coordinates teams and decisions around product goals, priorities and delivery.
example: A product leader aligns engineering and design on which customer problem to address first.

label: Product quality assurance
entry_text: Product quality assurance establishes and applies practices that help ensure products meet requirements and reduce defects.
example: A team defines acceptance criteria and reviews defect patterns before release.

label: Product requirements documentation
entry_text: Product requirements documentation records what a product or change must do, for whom, and under what constraints or acceptance conditions.
example: A product manager writes measurable criteria for a returns workflow.

label: Product strategy
entry_text: Product strategy decides which users and problems a product will serve and how it will achieve and sustain its intended outcomes.
example: A team focuses its roadmap on reducing onboarding costs for small organizations.

label: Production support
entry_text: Production support maintains the operation of deployed systems through monitoring, incident response and service recovery.
example: A support engineer investigates why an application stopped processing scheduled work.
sense_note: The wording may also refer to supporting a manufacturing line.

label: Productivity management
entry_text: Productivity management measures and improves how effectively time and resources are converted into useful outputs.
example: A manager adjusts how work is assigned after measuring bottlenecks and rework.

label: Professionalism
entry_text: Professionalism applies the conduct, reliability, ethical judgment and communication expected in a work setting.
example: A team member discloses a conflict of interest before participating in a purchasing decision.

label: Profitability management
entry_text: Profitability management monitors and improves the relationship between revenues and costs across activities or offerings.
example: A manager compares contribution margins before deciding whether to change a service package.

label: Program evaluation
entry_text: Program evaluation systematically assesses a program's implementation, effectiveness or other outcomes against explicit questions and criteria.
example: An evaluator studies whether a tutoring program reached its intended students and improved attendance.

label: Program optimization
entry_text: Program optimization changes software to improve resource use or performance while preserving required behavior.
example: A developer profiles a slow report and rewrites the operation that dominates its runtime.
sense_note: The likely sense is computer-program optimization; in management it can mean improving program performance.

label: Programmatic media buying
entry_text: Programmatic media buying uses software to automate the selection and purchase of advertising placements.
example: A campaign automatically bids for suitable ad impressions subject to its budget and targeting rules.

label: Programmer's Hierarchical Interactive Graphics System
entry_text: Programmer's Hierarchical Interactive Graphics System is a standard interface for creating and manipulating structured, interactive computer graphics.
example: An application builds a hierarchy of graphic objects that can be edited and transformed as groups.

label: Programming
entry_text: Writing computer programs for various purposes.

label: Project benchmarking
entry_text: Project benchmarking compares a project's practices or metrics with suitable references to identify differences and improvement opportunities.
example: A team compares its construction lead times with those of projects using similar scope and constraints.

label: Project management
entry_text: Project management plans, coordinates and controls resources and work to deliver a defined outcome within project constraints.
example: A project manager tracks dependencies and resolves a schedule conflict before it delays delivery.

label: Project scoping
entry_text: Project scoping defines a project's objectives, included and excluded work, deliverables, boundaries and constraints.
example: A team specifies that the first release will migrate current records but not archived records.

label: Project status reporting
entry_text: Project status reporting communicates progress, risks, decisions and expected outcomes relative to a project plan.
example: A project lead reports which milestones are complete and flags a dependency threatening the next one.

label: Prometheus
entry_text: Prometheus is an open-source monitoring system that collects time-series metrics and supports queries and alerting rules.
example: An engineer sets an alert for sustained error rates above the service target.

label: Prompt engineering
entry_text: Prompt engineering designs and evaluates inputs and instructions to improve a model's responses for a specified task.
example: A developer tests whether a prompt with examples improves extraction accuracy on held-out documents.

label: Proofreading
entry_text: Proofreading checks a near-final text for errors in spelling, punctuation, grammar and presentation consistency.
example: An editor catches a misspelled name and inconsistent numbering before publication.

label: Proposal development
entry_text: Proposal development analyzes a request and produces a written offer explaining the proposed approach, costs and evidence of capability.
example: A team drafts a technical plan and budget in response to a request for proposals.

label: Proposal management
entry_text: Proposal management coordinates contributors, requirements, reviews and deadlines for preparing and submitting a proposal.
example: A manager tracks compliance items and schedules final reviews before submission.

label: Proposal strategy
entry_text: Proposal strategy defines the positioning, evidence and approach used to make a proposal persuasive and competitive.
example: A bidder emphasizes documented reliability because the buyer gives it a high evaluation weight.

label: Prosecutor's management information system
entry_text: A prosecutor's management information system records and organizes information about cases, parties and proceedings for a prosecutorial office.
example: A legal office tracks upcoming hearings and the status of active cases.
sense_note: Could denote the historical PROMIS product or this category of case-management system; verify the named implementation.

label: Protein characterization
entry_text: Protein characterization uses analytical methods to determine properties of proteins, such as identity, composition, structure or function.
example: A laboratory compares analytical measurements to check whether purified protein samples are consistent.

label: Protein structure prediction
entry_text: Protein structure prediction estimates a protein's three-dimensional conformation from its sequence and other available information.
example: A researcher compares candidate structural models to interpret the shape of a protein domain.

label: Protocol-oriented programming
entry_text: Protocol-oriented programming structures software around behavioral interfaces called protocols and types that conform to them.
example: A Swift developer defines a rendering protocol and writes code that accepts multiple conforming types.

label: Prototype JavaScript Framework
entry_text: Prototype JavaScript Framework is a historical JavaScript library with helpers for DOM operations, events and asynchronous web requests.
example: A legacy page uses Prototype to update a region after a server response.
sense_note: Distinguish the named library from JavaScript's prototype-based object model.

label: Prototyping
entry_text: Prototyping creates an early representation of a product or solution to investigate ideas before committing to a full build.
example: A design team tests a clickable mockup to see whether users understand a navigation change.

label: Protractor
entry_text: Protractor was an end-to-end testing framework built on WebDriver for web applications, particularly Angular applications.
example: A team used it to test whether a form submission reached the expected page.
sense_note: Historical framework; do not infer current support.

label: Data provenance
entry_text: Data provenance records where data originated and how it was transformed or transferred.
example: A reviewer traces an aggregate back to the source records and transformation steps.

label: Public-Key Cryptography Standards
entry_text: Public-key cryptography standards specify interoperable formats, algorithms, and procedures for systems using paired public and private keys.
example: An engineer checks a signing service against the applicable signature standard.

label: Pug
entry_text: Pug is a template language and engine with indentation-based syntax for generating HTML.
example: A site renders a list of products from records using one Pug template.

label: Punctuation
entry_text: Punctuation uses conventional written marks to organize text and clarify its structure and meaning.
example: An editor uses commas to separate items in a list.

label: PuPHPet
entry_text: PuPHPet was a configuration generator for provisioning Vagrant development environments with Puppet.
example: A developer used it to generate a repeatable local PHP development setup.

label: Puppet
entry_text: Puppet automates system configuration by specifying the desired state of managed resources.
example: An administrator sets the same package and configuration across servers.

label: Puppeteer
entry_text: Puppeteer is a JavaScript library for controlling web browsers programmatically.
example: A developer captures a screenshot after a test page loads.

label: PuTTY
entry_text: PuTTY is a terminal client for connections such as SSH and serial sessions.
example: An administrator opens an authorized SSH session for routine maintenance.

label: PyMongo
entry_text: PyMongo is the MongoDB driver for Python, providing access to collections and database operations.
example: A Python service uses it to read application records.

label: PyTables
entry_text: PyTables is a Python package for managing and querying structured data in HDF5 files.
example: An analyst reads a subset of a large scientific dataset stored in HDF5.

label: Python for data analysis
entry_text: Python for data analysis is using Python and its libraries to prepare, examine, and interpret data.
example: An analyst groups sales records by month and checks for missing values.

label: Python Server Pages
entry_text: Python Server Pages are a server-side templating approach that embeds Python logic in pages rendered into HTML.
example: A historical web application inserts a record into a generated HTML page.
sense_note: Multiple implementations share this label. This definition describes the general technique.

label: Python Tools for Visual Studio
entry_text: Python Tools for Visual Studio provides Python editing, debugging, and project support within Microsoft Visual Studio.
example: A developer inspects variable values while stepping through a Python program.

label: PyTorch
entry_text: PyTorch is a tensor-computing library with automatic differentiation for building and training machine-learning models.
example: A developer computes gradients for a model during training.

label: QARun
entry_text: QARun was a Compuware tool for automating functional tests of application interfaces.
example: A tester replayed a recorded sequence to check a desktop application.
sense_note: Historical product. Verify branding and supported platforms from vendor archival material.

label: Qlik Sense
entry_text: Qlik Sense is an analytics platform for exploring data and building interactive visualizations and dashboards.
example: A team connects an operations dataset to a dashboard with filters.

label: QlikView
entry_text: QlikView is a business intelligence product for building and using interactive data analysis applications.
example: A manager filters a sales analysis document by region.

label: QS/1
entry_text: QS/1 is a name associated with software used to manage pharmacy operations.
example: A pharmacy uses management software to track prescriptions and dispensing workflows.
sense_note: Verify whether the intended sense is the company, the brand, or a specific product line.

label: Qualitative data analysis
entry_text: Qualitative data analysis interprets nonnumeric evidence to identify themes, patterns, and meanings.
example: A researcher codes interview transcripts and compares recurring themes.

label: Quality Control Analysis
entry_text: Conducting tests and inspections of products, services, or processes to evaluate quality or performance.

label: Queue management system
entry_text: A queue management system coordinates how waiting items or people are ordered, routed, and served.
example: A clinic routes waiting patients to available service counters.
sense_note: Examples use service queues, while the general label may also occur in computing.

label: QuickTime VR
entry_text: QuickTime VR was an Apple technology for viewing interactive panoramas or rotatable objects.
example: A museum visitor could pan around a digitized exhibit space.

label: Qumu
entry_text: Qumu is an enterprise video platform for publishing, streaming, and managing organizational video.
example: A company distributes a recorded training session to staff.
sense_note: Verify whether the label is intended to refer to the platform or the company.

label: QuoteWerks
entry_text: QuoteWerks is a quoting and proposal tool for assembling sales offers with products, prices, and terms.
example: A salesperson prepares and revises an itemized customer quote.

label: Rack elevation drawings
entry_text: Rack elevation drawings depict the physical position and height of equipment in a rack.
example: An installer checks which rack units are reserved for a network switch.

label: Radare2
entry_text: radare2 is an open-source framework for inspecting and analyzing compiled programs.
example: A developer inspects their own compiled program to understand its binary layout.

label: Rally Software
entry_text: Rally Software is an agile delivery management platform for planning and tracking work across teams.
example: A product team tracks stories and dependencies across iterations.

label: Rancher
entry_text: Rancher is a management platform for operating and administering Kubernetes clusters.
example: An operations team views multiple clusters through one management interface.

label: Random forest
entry_text: A random forest combines many randomized decision trees to make a prediction by aggregating their outputs.
example: A classifier combines votes from trees trained with different samples or feature subsets.

label: Random testing
entry_text: Random testing evaluates a system using test inputs sampled from a specified domain or distribution.
example: A tester generates varied valid input sizes for a library.

label: Randomization
entry_text: Randomization uses chance to assign treatments, choose observations, or vary order according to a stated procedure.
example: A study randomly assigns participants to two conditions.

label: RavenDB
entry_text: RavenDB is a document database for storing and querying structured data as documents.
example: An application stores each customer profile as a document.

label: Ray tracing
entry_text: Ray tracing calculates light transport or visibility by following rays and evaluating their intersections with scene geometry.
example: A renderer traces a ray to determine what surface is visible at a pixel.

label: React
entry_text: React is a JavaScript library for constructing user interfaces from components whose output can change with data.
example: A developer builds a list component that updates as filters change.

label: ReactiveX
entry_text: ReactiveX is a family of libraries and interfaces for composing and transforming asynchronous streams through observable sequences.
example: An application filters and combines streams of interface events.

label: Reading Comprehension
entry_text: Understanding written sentences and paragraphs in work-related documents.

label: Reading gauges
entry_text: Reading gauges is interpreting indicated measurements on an instrument scale or display.
example: A technician reads a pressure indicator in the units marked on the dial.

label: Reading technical drawings
entry_text: Reading technical drawings is interpreting dimensions, views, symbols, and specifications in technical documentation.
example: A craftsperson identifies a hole diameter and its tolerance from a drawing.

label: Reading to children
entry_text: Reading to children is presenting a written text aloud in ways that help young listeners follow and engage with it.
example: An educator pauses after a picture-book page to ask what happened.

label: ReadyAPI
entry_text: ReadyAPI is a software suite for testing and validating application programming interfaces.
example: A quality engineer checks that a test API returns the expected response fields.

label: Real estate market analysis
entry_text: Real estate market analysis uses property, transaction, supply, and demand information to evaluate market conditions.
example: An analyst compares recent sales of similar properties in the same area.

label: Recruitment consulting
entry_text: Recruitment consulting advises organizations on finding, assessing, and hiring people for defined roles.
example: A consultant helps a team clarify requirements and structure candidate evaluation.

label: Red teaming
entry_text: Red teaming is a structured, authorized challenge to an organization's assumptions, controls, or system behavior from an adversarial perspective.
example: A review team independently challenges the assumptions in an incident response plan before leadership approves it.

label: REDCap
entry_text: REDCap is a web platform for building and managing structured data collection instruments, especially for research studies.
example: A research coordinator builds a validated baseline survey with fields for consent and participant identifiers.

label: Reduction (complexity)
entry_text: A reduction transforms instances of one computational problem into instances of another under stated resource constraints so a solution to the latter helps solve the former.
example: A proof establishes hardness by transforming instances of a known hard problem into cases of a scheduling problem.

label: Refrigerated transport
entry_text: Refrigerated transport maintains a controlled temperature range for goods while they move between locations.
example: A carrier records temperature readings across a shipment of perishable food to document whether the cold chain held.

label: Regulatory CMC
entry_text: Regulatory CMC is the preparation and maintenance of chemistry, manufacturing, and controls information for a regulated medicinal product.
example: A regulatory specialist prepares documentation showing how a manufacturer verifies the quality of each released lot.

label: Reinforcement learning
entry_text: Reinforcement learning develops policies for sequential decisions from experience and rewards, with the goal of maximizing expected cumulative reward.
example: A simulated agent learns when to recharge by comparing the long-term rewards of different decisions.

label: Reltio
entry_text: Reltio is a cloud master data platform for reconciling and managing records about shared business entities across sources.
example: A data steward reviews whether two customer records from different systems represent the same organization.

label: Renewable energy sales
entry_text: Renewable energy sales involves matching buyers' energy needs with renewable systems or supply arrangements and explaining their costs and terms.
example: A salesperson compares rooftop solar quotes for a customer using the building's electricity bills.

label: Repairing
entry_text: Repairing machines or systems using the needed tools.

label: Reporting
entry_text: Reporting gathers, checks, and presents findings or status information for a defined audience and purpose.
