label: Stakeholder communication
entry_text: Stakeholder communication exchanges relevant information and feedback with people or groups affected by a decision, project, or organization.
example: A project lead explains a schedule change to affected teams and records which dependencies need follow-up.

label: Standards of Training, Certification and Watchkeeping
entry_text: The Standards of Training, Certification and Watchkeeping are international maritime requirements for minimum seafarer training, credentials, and watchkeeping practices.
example: A shipping operator checks that a crew member's certification matches assigned watch duties.

label: Stanislavski's system
entry_text: Stanislavski's system is an approach to actor training that develops believable performances by examining given circumstances, objectives, and purposeful action.
example: An actor rehearses a negotiation scene by identifying what the character wants from the other person.

label: Star and snowflake schemas
entry_text: Star and snowflake schemas organize analytical data around fact tables and dimensions, with snowflake schemas further normalizing dimension data into related tables.
example: A warehouse designer keeps product category in one dimension for a star schema but separates it into a linked table in a snowflake schema.

label: Statement on Auditing Standards No. 70
entry_text: Statement on Auditing Standards No. 70 was a U.S. auditing standard for reporting on controls at service organizations relevant to their customers' financial reporting.
example: An auditor reading an archived file distinguishes a report issued under SAS 70 from its later reporting frameworks.
sense_note: Historical standard; do not treat it as current guidance.

label: Statements on Standards for Attestation Engagements
entry_text: Statements on Standards for Attestation Engagements are U.S. professional standards governing engagements in which practitioners examine, review, or perform agreed procedures on specified subject matter or assertions.
example: An accounting firm identifies the applicable guidance before accepting an agreed-upon procedures engagement.

label: Statistical software
entry_text: Statistical software implements tools for managing data, estimating models, testing hypotheses, and visualizing results.
example: A researcher uses statistical software to fit a regression and plot its residuals.

label: Sterile technique
entry_text: Sterile technique uses controlled practices and barriers to keep designated materials and areas free from contamination by viable microorganisms.
example: A clinical team monitors the sterile field and replaces an item if its sterility is compromised.

label: STM32 Nucleo
entry_text: STM32 Nucleo is STMicroelectronics' family of development boards for prototyping with STM32 microcontrollers.
example: An engineer tests a sensor interface on a Nucleo board before designing a custom circuit.

label: Stochastic modelling
entry_text: Stochastic modelling represents uncertain system behavior using random variables or probability processes.
example: A planner models different passenger arrival times to estimate the distribution of queue lengths.

label: StormCAD
entry_text: StormCAD is Bentley storm sewer design and analysis software for evaluating drainage networks under modeled rainfall and hydraulic conditions.
example: An engineer checks whether a modeled pipe network can convey runoff from the design storm.

label: Stormwater monitoring
entry_text: Stormwater monitoring measures runoff quantity, quality, or associated conditions to evaluate drainage performance and impacts on receiving waters.
example: A municipality compares monitored sediment levels before and after upgrading a detention basin.

label: Strategic decision-making
entry_text: Strategic decision-making selects actions with long-term consequences by weighing goals, evidence, alternatives, risks, and resource commitments.
example: A nonprofit compares expanding into a new city with improving its existing program before allocating its budget.

label: Strategic prioritization
entry_text: Strategic prioritization ranks competing initiatives according to objectives, expected impact, urgency, feasibility, and constraints.
example: A team prioritizes stabilizing an essential service over adding a feature with little demonstrated demand.

label: Strategic procurement
entry_text: Strategic procurement aligns purchasing and supplier decisions with long-term goals for value, risk, availability, and performance.
example: A hospital assesses supply continuity and service terms alongside unit price when choosing a supplier.

label: Strength training
entry_text: Strength training uses progressively challenging muscular resistance to develop force production and related physical capacities.
example: A supervised exercise program tracks changes in how much resistance a participant can handle with sound technique.

label: Stress testing (computing)
entry_text: Computing stress testing deliberately exposes a system to unusually demanding but authorized workloads to observe limits, degradation, and recovery.
example: A team increases simulated traffic in a test environment and records when response times exceed the target.

label: Stretch wrapping
entry_text: Stretch wrapping uses tensioned elastic film to hold items together or secure a load for handling and transport.
example: A warehouse wraps cartons on a pallet so the stack stays together during transit.

label: Structural calculations
entry_text: Structural calculations apply engineering mechanics and design requirements to estimate load effects, capacity, stability, or deflection in a structure.
example: An engineer calculates the expected deflection of a floor beam under specified loads.

label: Structural detailing
entry_text: Structural detailing translates structural design requirements into drawings or models that specify dimensions, connections, reinforcement, and assembly details.
example: A detailer shows where reinforcing bars overlap around a concrete opening.

label: Structure chart
entry_text: A structure chart diagrams the hierarchy of software modules and their calling or data relationships.
example: A designer diagrams how an invoice routine calls separate modules to compute taxes and format totals.
sense_note: Interpreted as structured software design, not an organizational chart.

label: Student development
entry_text: Student development concerns how students grow intellectually, socially, personally, and professionally and how educational settings support that growth.
example: A student affairs team designs advising activities that help first-year students make more independent decisions.

label: Student recruitment
entry_text: Student recruitment attracts and informs prospective students and supports their progression toward application or enrollment.
example: An admissions team offers a program information session and follows up with applicants about required materials.

label: Student's t-test
entry_text: Student's t-test uses a t statistic to test a hypothesis about a mean or mean difference under specified assumptions.
example: A researcher uses a paired t-test to assess the average change between two measurements on the same participants.
sense_note: Distinguish equal-variance two-sample Student tests from Welch's variant.

label: Stuttgart Neural Network Simulator
entry_text: The Stuttgart Neural Network Simulator is a software package for constructing, training, and studying artificial neural networks.
example: A researcher teaching historical neural network methods loads a small classifier and examines its learned weights.
sense_note: Historical software commonly abbreviated SNNS.

label: Sublime Text
entry_text: Sublime Text is a text and source code editor with syntax highlighting, search, and extensibility through packages.
example: A developer uses project-wide search to find where an outdated configuration name appears.

label: Substance abuse assessment
entry_text: Substance use assessment evaluates patterns, risks, consequences, and related needs to guide professional decisions about support or treatment.
example: A clinician gathers a history and uses a validated questionnaire before discussing options with a patient.
sense_note: The label uses older terminology; screening alone does not establish a diagnosis.

label: Substantive testing
entry_text: In auditing, substantive testing examines transaction details, balances, disclosures, or analytical relationships to detect material misstatements.
example: An auditor compares selected recorded sales with invoices and shipment evidence.

label: SuperTest
entry_text: SuperTest is a JavaScript library for testing HTTP server behavior by sending requests and asserting response properties.
example: A developer checks that an application returns the expected status and JSON fields for a test request.

label: Supplier quality engineering
entry_text: Supplier quality engineering uses engineering methods to qualify suppliers, assess production processes, and prevent or resolve defects in supplied components.
example: An engineer reviews a supplier's process capability after repeated parts fail a dimensional check.

label: Supplier quality management
entry_text: Supplier quality management establishes and monitors supplier quality requirements, performance, and corrective actions over the relationship.
example: A purchasing team reviews supplier defect trends and tracks corrective actions to completion.

label: Surgical incision
entry_text: A surgical incision is a deliberate cut into tissue made to provide access for an operation or procedure.
example: A surgical trainee reviewing an anatomy diagram identifies the marked access site for a planned procedure.

label: Surgical suturing
entry_text: Surgical suturing uses stitches to approximate tissues, close a wound, or secure tissue or material during a procedure.
example: A supervised learner uses a simulation model to assess whether the edges remain aligned after closure.

label: Sustainability risk management
entry_text: Sustainability risk management identifies, evaluates, and responds to environmental and social uncertainties that could affect operations, stakeholders, or long-term goals.
example: A company assesses whether water scarcity at key suppliers could disrupt production and harm local communities.

label: Sustainable investment management
entry_text: Sustainable investment management incorporates financially relevant sustainability factors or explicit sustainability objectives into investment research, decisions, ownership, and monitoring.
example: A fund manager compares portfolio companies' transition risks against the fund's stated mandate.

label: Svelte
entry_text: Svelte is a web user-interface framework that compiles components into JavaScript and coordinates updates when application state changes.
example: A developer binds a filter control to the displayed list in a Svelte component.

label: SvelteKit
entry_text: SvelteKit is an application framework built on Svelte that adds routing, data loading, rendering, and deployment integration.
example: A developer creates a route that loads product details on the server and renders a page.

label: Swagger UI
entry_text: Swagger UI renders OpenAPI descriptions as interactive documentation for exploring API operations and, when configured, making requests.
example: A developer reads a documented request schema and tries the operation against an authorized sandbox.

label: Swedish massage
entry_text: Swedish massage is a style of manual massage using gliding strokes, kneading, and other soft-tissue techniques commonly associated with relaxation.
example: A massage therapist tailors the pressure and pace of a relaxation session to a client's preferences.

label: SWIFT network
entry_text: The SWIFT network carries standardized, authenticated financial messages between participating institutions without itself moving the underlying funds.
example: A bank sends a payment instruction through SWIFT while settlement occurs through separate accounts or systems.

label: Sybase Unwired Platform
entry_text: Sybase Unwired Platform was middleware for developing and managing enterprise mobile applications connected to back-end systems.
example: A maintenance team traces how a legacy offline field application synchronized records with its enterprise database.
sense_note: Historical name later associated with SAP Mobile Platform; verify version for specific capabilities.

label: Synthesizing information
entry_text: Synthesizing information combines evidence and ideas across sources into an integrated account while preserving important disagreements, limitations, and context.
example: An analyst combines interviews and service records to explain where their findings agree and where more evidence is needed.

label: Syskey
entry_text: Syskey was a legacy Windows utility for configuring additional protection of account database keys at system startup.
example: A Windows migration specialist recognizes Syskey in historical documentation and checks which replacement security controls apply.
sense_note: Retired feature; not a recommendation to use it.

label: Sysomos
entry_text: Sysomos was a social media analysis and management platform used to track mentions, trends, and audience activity.
example: An analyst examines archived reports on public mentions of a campaign across social channels.
sense_note: Historical branding and capabilities may differ by module.

label: System.Data
entry_text: System.Data is the .NET namespace that provides ADO.NET abstractions and in-memory structures for working with data sources.
example: A developer uses a DataTable to hold structured query results for a desktop application.

label: System implementation
entry_text: System implementation brings a designed system into operation by configuring, integrating, testing, deploying, and transitioning it into use.
example: A team migrates stock records, verifies them against the old system, and trains warehouse staff before switching over.

label: System recovery
entry_text: System recovery restores a failed or disrupted system and its data to a usable condition based on recovery objectives and verified procedures.
example: A team restores a known backup and checks that critical transactions can be read before resuming service.

label: SystemJS
entry_text: SystemJS is a JavaScript module loader that resolves and loads supported module formats at runtime, including System.register modules.
example: A web application loads an independently deployed UI module without bundling it into the host application.

label: Systems Analysis
entry_text: Determining how a system should work and how changes in conditions, operations, and the environment will affect outcomes.

label: Systems Evaluation
entry_text: Identifying measures or indicators of system performance and the actions needed to improve or correct performance, relative to the goals of the system.

label: Systems management
entry_text: Systems management administers and monitors computing infrastructure, including configuration, updates, inventory, and availability.
example: An IT team stages operating system updates and tracks which managed devices still need them.
sense_note: Interpreted as IT infrastructure management.

label: Table data gateway
entry_text: A table data gateway is an application design pattern that centralizes access to the rows of a database table or view in a single gateway object.
example: An application sends customer insert and lookup operations through one gateway instead of scattering SQL throughout the code.

label: Table etiquette
entry_text: Table etiquette is the set of context-dependent social conventions for behavior, consideration, and communication during shared meals.
example: A guest checks with the host before following an unfamiliar custom at a formal meal.

label: Tableau
entry_text: Tableau is a visual analytics platform for connecting to data and creating interactive charts, dashboards, and reports.
example: An analyst builds a dashboard that lets viewers filter service delays by month and region.
sense_note: Interpreted as the software, not a staged picture or arrangement.

label: Tabular Data Stream
entry_text: Tabular Data Stream is a wire protocol used by SQL Server and related database systems to exchange requests and tabular results with clients.
example: A driver developer checks how metadata and result rows are represented in a database response.

label: Taking messages
entry_text: Taking messages means recording and relaying a caller's or visitor's information accurately, completely, and to the appropriate recipient.
example: A receptionist records a callback number and repeats it to confirm accuracy before forwarding the message.

label: Talent management
entry_text: Talent management coordinates how an organization attracts, develops, deploys, and retains people with the capabilities it needs.
example: A manager reviews skills gaps and assigns development opportunities before filling a future leadership role.

label: Tanium
entry_text: Tanium is an endpoint management and security platform for obtaining device visibility and carrying out authorized management actions.
example: An administrator checks managed computers for an approved software update and follows up on missing installations.

label: Tank truck
entry_text: A tank truck is a road vehicle fitted with a tank to transport bulk liquids, gases, or certain dry materials.
example: A carrier chooses a food-grade tank truck for transporting milk between a dairy and a processing facility.

label: Tape measure
entry_text: A tape measure is a flexible graduated strip used to measure lengths, distances, or circumferences.
example: A carpenter measures the clear width of an opening before cutting a shelf.

label: Tape recorder
entry_text: A tape recorder captures audio by magnetically recording it on moving tape and can reproduce the recorded signal during playback.
example: An archivist plays a recorded interview on compatible equipment for digitization.
sense_note: Interpreted as audio tape recording; magnetic tape also supports data or video recording.

label: Team leadership
entry_text: Team leadership guides a group toward shared goals by clarifying priorities, coordinating work, supporting members, and making decisions.
example: A team lead resolves conflicting assignments and agrees on a sequence that frees a blocked colleague.

label: Teamwork
entry_text: Teamwork is the coordinated contribution of people who share information, divide responsibilities, and support one another toward a common goal.
example: Editors and designers share drafts early so each can address changes before the publication deadline.

label: Technical leadership
entry_text: Technical leadership uses expertise and judgment to set technical direction, resolve tradeoffs, guide contributors, and maintain standards.
example: An engineering lead compares designs with the team and records why one meets the reliability constraints better.

label: Technical record-keeping
entry_text: Technical record-keeping creates and maintains traceable records of technical actions, observations, decisions, and changes.
example: A maintenance technician records the equipment identifier, work performed, and post-service check results.

label: Technical writing
entry_text: Technical writing explains specialized information or procedures accurately and clearly for the intended audience and task.
example: A writer turns engineering notes into troubleshooting instructions with expected outcomes and escalation points.

label: Technology Design
entry_text: Generating or adapting equipment and technology to serve user needs.

label: Technology roadmap
entry_text: A technology roadmap relates capability needs and planned technical changes over time to goals, dependencies, and decision points.
example: A team sequences a database upgrade before a feature that depends on a newer capability.

label: Tekla
entry_text: Tekla is Trimble's family of structural design, analysis, modeling, and detailing applications.
example: A steel detailer uses Tekla Structures to prepare a model that includes fabrication connections.
sense_note: Product-family label; verify intended application.

label: Telecommunications equipment installation
entry_text: Telecommunications equipment installation places, connects, configures, and verifies hardware used to carry communications signals.
example: A technician installs approved fiber equipment and documents test results before service handoff.

label: Telegraphy
entry_text: Telegraphy is the long-distance transmission of messages encoded as discrete signals, historically including electrical pulses over wires.
example: A museum demonstration shows how a receiver interprets timed signals as letters in Morse code.

label: Telephone etiquette
entry_text: Telephone etiquette is the practice of speaking, listening, and handling calls with clarity, courtesy, and respect for privacy.
example: A receptionist asks permission before placing a caller on hold and returns with an update.

label: Telescoping gauge
entry_text: A telescoping gauge transfers an internal dimension from a hole or opening to an external measuring instrument.
example: A machinist captures the diameter of a bore with a telescoping gauge and reads it with a micrometer.

label: Television programming
entry_text: Television programming selects, schedules, or commissions content for a television channel or service to meet audience and operational goals.
example: A scheduler places a weekly documentary in a time slot where its intended audience is likely to watch.
sense_note: Could also denote the television content itself; interpreted as the work of organizing it.

label: Temporal.io
entry_text: Temporal is a platform for durable application workflows that records execution history and coordinates work, retries, and recovery across failures.
example: An order workflow resumes after a worker restarts without restarting its completed sequence from the beginning.
sense_note: Temporal.io is the project and vendor website naming.

label: TensorFlow
entry_text: TensorFlow is an open-source machine learning platform for representing tensor computations and building, training, or deploying models.
example: A researcher trains an image classifier and evaluates it on held-out examples using TensorFlow.

label: Software testing
entry_text: Software testing evaluates software behavior against expectations by examining or exercising it under defined conditions.
example: A tester checks that an expired reset link is rejected and a valid test link produces the expected screen.

label: TestNG
entry_text: TestNG is a Java testing framework that supports annotated tests, configuration methods, parameterization, and grouping.
example: A developer runs a parameterized checkout test with several input combinations.

label: Theano
entry_text: Theano was an open-source Python library for defining and optimizing mathematical expressions on multidimensional arrays, including automatic differentiation.
example: A researcher examining older neural network code identifies how Theano created the gradient used to update parameters.
sense_note: Historical project; do not infer maintenance status of forks.

label: Theory of change
entry_text: A theory of change explains how and why activities are expected to contribute to intended outcomes, including intermediate steps and assumptions.
example: A nonprofit maps how coaching might improve interview performance and states the conditions needed for it to improve hiring outcomes.

label: Therapeutic interventions
entry_text: Therapeutic interventions are planned actions intended to alleviate symptoms, improve functioning, or support recovery in a care context.
example: A clinician selects a supervised exercise program to help a patient regain functional mobility.
sense_note: Broad label spans physical health, mental health, and other therapeutic contexts.

label: Thin film coating
entry_text: Thin film coating applies a thin layer of material to a surface to change properties such as optical behavior, wear, adhesion, or conductivity.
example: An optical engineer applies and evaluates an antireflection coating on a lens.

label: Third party risk management
entry_text: Third party risk management identifies, assesses, monitors, and treats risks arising from suppliers, partners, contractors, or other external relationships.
example: An organization checks a cloud vendor's recovery commitments and reviews its performance annually.

label: Threading (manufacturing)
entry_text: Threading forms a helical ridge or groove on an internal or external surface so parts can engage with matching threads.
example: A machinist verifies that a tapped hole accepts the specified fastener and meets its thread gauge requirements.

label: Threat modeling
entry_text: Threat modeling systematically examines an asset or system's design, trust boundaries, and plausible adverse events to prioritize defenses.
example: A team diagrams who can access a document store and checks whether its authorization rules match the stated trust boundaries.

label: Three.js
entry_text: Three.js is a JavaScript library that abstracts browser graphics rendering to create interactive three-dimensional scenes.
example: A developer creates a rotatable 3D preview of a product for a web page.

label: Thyroid biopsy
entry_text: A thyroid biopsy collects cells or tissue from the thyroid for microscopic or other diagnostic evaluation.
example: A clinician reviews a biopsy report to help characterize a thyroid nodule.

label: Thyroid ultrasound
entry_text: Thyroid ultrasound uses sound waves to image the thyroid gland and assess features such as its size and nodules.
example: A clinician compares ultrasound measurements from two examinations to assess whether a nodule has changed.

label: TIBCO ActiveMatrix
entry_text: TIBCO ActiveMatrix is a suite of enterprise middleware products for integrating applications and building, deploying, or managing services and processes.
example: An integration team connects two enterprise applications and monitors exchanges through an ActiveMatrix product.
sense_note: The label names a product family; the exact component is unspecified.

label: TIBCO Designer
entry_text: TIBCO Designer is a graphical development environment used in legacy TIBCO products to configure integration resources and processes.
example: A maintainer opens a historical BusinessWorks project to trace where its message mappings are defined.
sense_note: Legacy design tooling; verify product and version.

label: TIBCO Enterprise Message Service
entry_text: TIBCO Enterprise Message Service is enterprise messaging middleware that implements Java Message Service APIs and supports queues and topics.
example: An order service publishes a message to a queue for later processing by another application.

label: TIBCO iProcess Suite
entry_text: TIBCO iProcess Suite is business process management software for defining, executing, and tracking workflows that may include assigned human work.
example: An operations team routes applications to reviewers and reports where cases are waiting.

label: TIBCO Spotfire
entry_text: Spotfire is a visual analytics platform for interactively exploring data and developing analyses or dashboards.
example: An engineer compares sensor readings by equipment type and filters the views to inspect a suspected trend.

label: Time Management
entry_text: Managing one's own time and the time of others.

label: Time Protocol
entry_text: The Time Protocol is a simple network protocol that returns a binary count of seconds since the beginning of 1900 for time retrieval.
example: A network historian identifies the Time Protocol in an archived system and distinguishes it from NTP.
sense_note: Interpreted as the specific RFC 868 protocol, not network time protocols in general.

label: TinyDB
entry_text: TinyDB is a lightweight Python document database that commonly stores records in a local JSON file.
example: A small command-line utility keeps a local set of bookmarked items and queries their tags.
sense_note: Interpreted as the Python library; TinyDB also names a wireless sensor network query system.

label: Tire balancing and rotation
entry_text: Tire balancing corrects uneven wheel-assembly mass distribution, while rotation periodically changes tire positions to help distribute wear.
example: A shop corrects a measured wheel imbalance and rotates the tires according to the vehicle's recommended pattern.

label: TOGAF
entry_text: TOGAF is an enterprise architecture framework and methodology for developing, managing, and governing architecture aligned to organizational goals.
example: An architecture team uses the framework to describe a target operating model and plan the transition from current systems.

label: TokuDB
entry_text: TokuDB was a MySQL-compatible storage engine designed for high insertion rates using fractal tree indexes and compression.
example: A database engineer plans a migration away from TokuDB while checking how its indexes and compression affect the workload.
sense_note: Historical storage engine; availability varies by product version.

label: Agent tool use
entry_text: Agent tool use is the selection and invocation of external functions by an agent, followed by interpretation of their results within defined permissions and task constraints.
example: An assistant calls an approved calendar lookup and checks returned availability before suggesting meeting times.

label: Toon Boom
entry_text: Toon Boom is a family of animation and storyboard software used to plan and produce digital animated productions.
example: An animator uses Toon Boom Harmony to rig a character and revise its poses across a shot.
sense_note: The label may denote the vendor or one of several products.

label: TopSolid
entry_text: TopSolid is a suite of computer-aided design and manufacturing tools for designing parts, assemblies, and manufacturing processes.
example: A manufacturer uses TopSolid to model a fixture and prepare compatible machining operations.

label: Torch (machine learning)
entry_text: Torch is an older Lua-based scientific computing and machine learning framework with tensor and neural network libraries.
example: A researcher examines an archived Lua Torch model to understand its layer definitions before porting it.
sense_note: Distinguish original Torch, often called Torch7, from Python-based PyTorch unless the source equates the label.

label: Tourism management
entry_text: Tourism management plans and operates visitor services and destinations while considering demand, service quality, sustainability, and local impacts.
example: A destination manager adds off-season activities and monitors whether demand shifts away from congested peak weeks.

label: Track and trace
entry_text: Track and trace records the identity, movement, and history of items or consignments so their current state and prior locations can be established.
example: A food distributor follows a batch identifier from supplier receipt through shipments to several stores.
sense_note: Broad supply-chain sense; other domains may use dedicated variants.

label: TrackWise
entry_text: TrackWise is quality management software used to manage regulated or controlled processes such as deviations, audits, and corrective actions.
example: A manufacturer logs a deviation and links it to a corrective action and effectiveness check.
sense_note: Verify edition where cloud and legacy implementations differ.

label: Traffic Alert and Collision Avoidance System
entry_text: Traffic Alert and Collision Avoidance System is an airborne system that monitors nearby transponder-equipped aircraft and alerts crews to potential conflicts, with applicable versions providing resolution advisories.
example: A flight training simulator demonstrates how a crew distinguishes a traffic advisory from a resolution advisory.

label: Traffic collision reconstruction
entry_text: Traffic collision reconstruction uses physical evidence and engineering analysis to estimate the sequence and dynamics of a road crash.
example: A reconstruction specialist compares vehicle damage, scene measurements, and recordings to assess competing accounts of a collision.

label: Training and development needs assessment
entry_text: A training and development needs assessment identifies performance or capability gaps and determines whether training or another intervention would address them.
example: An evaluator separates unfamiliarity with a new process from delays caused by an unavailable tool before recommending training.

label: Training material development
entry_text: Training material development creates instructional content, practice opportunities, and assessment materials aligned with learning objectives and audience needs.
example: A trainer builds a job aid, worked example, and exercise for a new warehouse receiving process.

label: Trans-Proteomic Pipeline
entry_text: The Trans-Proteomic Pipeline is a software suite for processing, validating, and interpreting mass-spectrometry evidence in proteomics.
example: A researcher uses pipeline reports to compare confidence in peptide identifications across archived datasets.

label: Transaction monitoring
entry_text: Transaction monitoring reviews transactions and patterns against rules, models, or expectations to identify activity requiring investigation.
example: A financial compliance analyst reviews why a flagged set of account transfers departed from expected activity.
sense_note: Often financial crime or fraud monitoring, but operational transaction monitoring is also possible.

label: Transient expression
entry_text: Transient expression is the temporary production of a gene product in cells without establishing stable long-term expression in the population.
example: A student distinguishes a short-lived expression signal in a research report from evidence of a stable cell line.

label: Trauma-focused cognitive behavioral therapy
entry_text: Trauma-focused cognitive behavioral therapy is a structured psychotherapy that combines trauma-focused and cognitive behavioral methods to address trauma-related symptoms, commonly in children and adolescents and with caregiver involvement when appropriate.
example: A trained clinician works with a child and caregiver within an individualized trauma recovery plan.
sense_note: Capitalized TF-CBT usually refers to a specific manualized model, not all trauma-focused CBT approaches.

label: Travel coordination
entry_text: Travel coordination organizes transportation, accommodation, timing, documentation, and changes around travelers' needs and constraints.
example: A coordinator rebooks an accessible transfer after a flight schedule changes.

label: Treatment planning
entry_text: Treatment planning translates findings and patient goals into a proposed sequence of care actions, monitoring, and reassessment.
example: A rehabilitation team agrees with a patient on functional goals and how recovery will be measured.
sense_note: The broad label does not specify a clinical discipline.

label: Treemap
entry_text: A treemap depicts hierarchical or grouped data as nested rectangles whose areas represent a selected quantity.
example: A financial dashboard shows department budgets as rectangles sized by expenditure.

label: Trendline
entry_text: A trendline is a fitted or smoothed line that summarizes the predominant direction or pattern in plotted observations.
example: An analyst overlays a fitted line on monthly sales and inspects where individual months depart from it.

label: Troubleshooting
entry_text: Determining causes of operating errors and deciding what to do about it.

label: TV production
entry_text: TV production coordinates the preparation, recording, and postproduction of content intended for television distribution.
example: A production team schedules interviews, records footage, and edits it into a timed documentary episode.

label: Twitch
entry_text: Twitch is a livestreaming platform that combines broadcast video with viewer interaction such as live chat.
example: A creator streams a demonstration and appoints moderators to help manage the audience chat.

label: Twitter advertising
entry_text: Twitter advertising is the use of paid placements and campaign tools on the service historically named Twitter to reach defined audiences.
example: A campaign manager compares the cost per registration of two promoted posts.
sense_note: Platform later branded X; historical tools and present offerings may differ.

label: Twitter marketing
entry_text: Twitter marketing uses content, community interaction, and sometimes paid promotion to achieve communication goals on the service historically named Twitter.
example: A nonprofit schedules public updates and tracks which posts lead to event signups.
sense_note: Platform later branded X; the label does not imply paid advertising only.

label: Typography
entry_text: Typography arranges type through choices such as typeface, size, spacing, and line length to support reading and convey hierarchy or character.
example: A designer increases line spacing and distinguishes heading weights to make a long article easier to scan.

label: Ubersuggest
entry_text: Ubersuggest is an SEO research application for exploring search keywords, ranking estimates, competitors, and site issues.
example: A content strategist compares estimated demand for several candidate search phrases before planning an article.

label: UglifyJS
entry_text: UglifyJS is a JavaScript parser, compressor, and mangler used to shrink source files while preserving intended behavior.
example: A build process produces a smaller script by removing unnecessary whitespace and shortening local variable names.

label: UI patterns
entry_text: UI patterns are reusable solutions to recurring interaction and interface design problems.
example: A designer uses progressive disclosure to keep optional invoice controls out of the default form.

label: UIKit
entry_text: UIKit is Apple's framework for constructing interfaces and handling user interaction and application events on supported platforms such as iOS and iPadOS.
example: An iOS developer uses a view controller to present a list and handle selection.
sense_note: Distinct from the UIkit front-end web framework.

label: UIkit (web framework)
entry_text: UIkit is a front-end web framework that supplies CSS and JavaScript components for building interfaces.
example: A developer combines UIkit grid and navigation components to lay out a responsive page.
sense_note: Distinct from Apple's UIKit.

label: UiPath
entry_text: UiPath is an automation platform for designing, running, and managing software workflows, including robotic process automation.
example: A team builds an approved workflow that copies validated invoice data between existing business applications.

label: UltraTax CS
entry_text: UltraTax CS is tax preparation software used by tax professionals to prepare and electronically file supported returns.
example: A preparer imports client information and reviews diagnostics before submitting an authorized return.

label: Ultraviolet-visible spectroscopy
entry_text: Ultraviolet-visible spectroscopy measures how a sample absorbs or transmits ultraviolet and visible light as a function of wavelength.
example: An analyst compares a sample's absorbance against calibration standards to estimate concentration.

label: Unbounce
entry_text: Unbounce is a web platform for creating and testing landing pages used in marketing campaigns.
example: A campaign team compares conversion rates for two approved versions of a registration page.

label: Underscore.js
entry_text: Underscore.js is a JavaScript utility library with functions for working with collections, objects, functions, and templates.
example: A developer uses its grouping function to organize records by a shared category.

label: Unified endpoint management
entry_text: Unified endpoint management administers computers, mobile devices, and other endpoints through a common platform for configuration, policies, updates, and inventory.
example: An IT team checks laptop and phone compliance with organization policy from a shared console.

label: Unisys MAPPER
entry_text: Unisys MAPPER is a legacy data management and application development environment for interactive reporting and business applications.
example: A modernization team maps a historical MAPPER report to the equivalent fields in a replacement application.
sense_note: Historical product naming may vary; verify the installation.

label: Unity (game engine)
entry_text: Unity is a game engine and editor for building and deploying interactive two-dimensional and three-dimensional applications.
example: A developer attaches a C# script and collider to a character object and tests its movement in a scene.

label: Unreal Editor
entry_text: Unreal Editor is the graphical authoring environment for Unreal Engine, used to construct levels, set up assets, and configure gameplay.
example: A level designer places lights and collision geometry and previews a playable route in the editor.

label: Usability testing
entry_text: Usability testing observes people attempting representative tasks to identify where an interface or service helps or hinders their work.
example: A researcher watches participants attempt to update a delivery address and notes where they hesitate or fail.

label: UsabilityHub
entry_text: UsabilityHub was the name of a remote design research platform, later branded Lyssna, for collecting feedback through tasks such as first-click and preference tests.
example: A designer compares where participants initially click on two proposed navigation layouts.
sense_note: Legacy name.

label: Use case diagram
entry_text: A use case diagram represents external actors and the goal-oriented interactions they have with a system, without detailing the steps inside each interaction.
example: A diagram shows that customers can request refunds while only managers can approve certain requests.

label: User Datagram Protocol
entry_text: User Datagram Protocol is a connectionless transport protocol that sends discrete datagrams without guaranteeing delivery, ordering, or duplicate suppression.
example: A voice application uses UDP for audio frames because it can tolerate occasional missing frames.

label: User experience design
entry_text: User experience design shapes how a person understands, uses, and feels about a product or service across interactions and contexts.
example: A team redesigns an appointment journey from finding availability through changing a booking after confirmation.

label: User interface design
entry_text: User interface design defines the presentation and behavior of the controls, content, and feedback through which a person interacts with a system.
example: A designer specifies the labels, focus states, and error messages for a payment form.

label: User provisioning software
entry_text: User provisioning software creates, updates, and deactivates accounts and assigned access in response to authorized identity lifecycle changes.
example: An organization removes departing workers' access to connected applications when their accounts are deactivated.

label: User research
entry_text: User research systematically studies people's needs, behaviors, contexts, and experiences to inform design and product decisions.
example: Researchers interview appointment schedulers and observe their work before proposing changes to the booking workflow.

label: UX writing
entry_text: UX writing creates the words in a product or service interface that help people understand options, complete tasks, and recover from errors.
example: A writer changes a vague error into a message that explains which field needs correction and preserves entered information.

label: Data validation
entry_text: Data validation checks whether data conforms to rules for type, format, range, consistency, or other intended-use requirements.
example: An import rejects a record with an invalid date and reports which field failed the check.

label: Validation protocols
entry_text: A validation protocol is a documented plan that specifies how evidence will be gathered to show that a system, process, or method meets requirements for its intended use.
example: A manufacturing team defines test cases and acceptance limits before assessing a new inspection system.
sense_note: Broad quality or compliance sense; the domain and governing standard are unspecified.

label: Valuation of options
entry_text: Valuation of options estimates the value of contingent rights to transact under specified terms by modeling factors such as underlying price, volatility, time, and exercise rules.
example: An analyst compares model prices of otherwise similar options with different expiration dates.
sense_note: Financial derivative sense; other contexts can refer to real options or comparing alternatives.

label: Value proposition
entry_text: A value proposition states the benefit an offering promises to a defined audience and why it is worth choosing over alternatives.
example: A scheduling tool's proposition explains how clinic staff can reduce missed calls without adding another shift.

label: Value stream analysis
entry_text: Value stream analysis examines the end-to-end flow of work and information needed to deliver a result to identify delay, waste, or opportunities for improvement.
example: A clinic maps the steps from referral to appointment and finds that requests sit in an unreviewed queue between teams.

label: Variable-frequency drive
entry_text: A variable-frequency drive controls the speed or torque of a compatible AC motor by varying the frequency and voltage of its electrical supply.
example: A facility varies pump speed to match demand rather than running the pump at a single speed.

label: Variance analysis
entry_text: Variance analysis compares actual results with planned or standard values and investigates reasons for material differences.
example: An accountant separates a materials cost overrun into differences attributable to purchase prices and quantities used.
sense_note: Interpreted as managerial accounting; distinguish from statistical analysis of variance.

label: Varnish Cache
entry_text: Varnish Cache is a reverse proxy that caches eligible HTTP responses and serves them without contacting the origin on every request.
example: A publisher uses it to serve cached copies of public article pages during a surge.

label: VAX 4000
entry_text: The VAX 4000 is a family of Digital Equipment Corporation computer systems based on the VAX instruction set architecture.
example: A systems historian identifies peripherals compatible with an archived VAX 4000 configuration.
sense_note: Historical product family; configurations vary by model.

label: VAX 8000
entry_text: The VAX 8000 is a series of higher-end Digital Equipment Corporation systems implementing the VAX instruction set architecture.
example: A computer archivist identifies a VAX 8800 system from its model documentation.
sense_note: Historical product series; not a single configuration.

label: VAXELN
entry_text: VAXELN was a Digital Equipment Corporation environment for developing and running real-time applications on supported processors, notably VAX systems.
example: A preservation team reviews VAXELN task documentation to understand a legacy industrial controller.
sense_note: Historical environment; verify exact version and target hardware.

label: Vector search
entry_text: Vector search retrieves items by comparing numerical vector representations using a distance or similarity measure, often with an approximate nearest-neighbor index.
example: A document search system retrieves paragraphs whose embeddings are close to the embedding of a question.

label: VectorWise
entry_text: VectorWise is a former name associated with the Actian Vector analytical database, a column-oriented system using vectorized query execution.
example: An analyst runs aggregations over selected columns in a large fact table.
sense_note: Historical product naming; distinguish vectorized SQL execution from embedding similarity search.

label: Veeva
entry_text: Veeva provides cloud software for life sciences operations such as clinical, regulatory, quality, and commercial workflows.
example: A regulatory team manages approved document versions in a Veeva Vault application.
sense_note: Vendor and product-family label; exact Veeva application is not specified.

label: Vehicle inspection
entry_text: Vehicle inspection examines a vehicle against specified safety, condition, emissions, or other criteria and records findings.
example: An inspector documents tread condition and verifies that required exterior lights work.

label: Vehicle maintenance
entry_text: Vehicle maintenance preserves safe and reliable operation through scheduled service and correction of identified faults.
example: A fleet technician replaces worn brake components and records the repair for future service planning.

label: Vendavo
entry_text: Vendavo provides pricing, quoting and margin software for business-to-business sales.
example: A team checks whether a proposed discount meets its margin target.

label: Vendor management
entry_text: Vendor management oversees supplier selection, performance and relationships.
example: A buyer reviews supplier delivery and quality records.

label: Vendor payments
entry_text: Vendor payments are the verification, authorization and settlement of amounts owed to suppliers.
example: An accounts-payable clerk matches an invoice to a purchase order before payment.

label: Ventilator management
entry_text: Ventilator management is clinical oversight of mechanical breathing support and the patient’s response.
example: A respiratory care team reviews whether a patient is ready for less support.

label: Verbal and physical intervention
entry_text: Verbal and physical intervention combines communication to de-escalate situations with authorized physical measures when needed for safety.
example: A trained care worker uses calm communication to de-escalate a tense interaction.
sense_note: Scope depends on training, setting and authorization.

label: Version control
entry_text: Version control records changes to files so contributors can compare, recover and combine revisions.
example: A developer identifies the change that introduced a bug.

label: Vestibular rehabilitation
entry_text: Vestibular rehabilitation uses therapy to improve function affected by dizziness or balance disorders.
example: A therapist tracks whether treatment improves a patient’s ability to walk while turning their head.

label: Video advertising
entry_text: Video advertising uses paid video placements to deliver promotional messages.
example: A nonprofit sponsors a short event announcement.

label: Video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery
entry_text: Video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery is chest surgery performed through small incisions with a video camera.
example: A thoracic surgical team uses a camera to view an area of lung.

label: Video.js
entry_text: Video.js is a web video player library that provides a customizable browser playback interface.
example: A publisher displays an interview with captions.

label: Video marketing
entry_text: Video marketing uses video content to communicate with audiences and pursue marketing goals.
example: A software company publishes a product walkthrough.

label: Video remote interpreting
entry_text: Video remote interpreting connects an interpreter and participants through video.
example: A remote interpreter helps a patient communicate during a clinic visit.

label: Videoconferencing
entry_text: Videoconferencing connects people in different locations through live audio and video.
example: A distributed design team reviews a prototype on a call.

label: Virtual design and construction
entry_text: Virtual design and construction uses digital models and coordinated workflows to plan and deliver built projects.
example: A team identifies intersections between pipes and beams in a shared model.

label: Virtual production
entry_text: Virtual production combines digital environments or effects with live production workflows.
example: A director frames actors against a digital backdrop on an LED wall.

label: Virus culture
entry_text: Virus culture refers to growing viruses in living host systems in controlled settings.
example: A virology team distinguishes evidence of infectious virus from a test that detects only genetic material.

label: VISI
entry_text: VISI is a CAD and CAM software suite used in manufacturing workflows such as mold and die design and machining.
example: A tool designer models a mold component before manufacturing it.
sense_note: Interpreted as the manufacturing software.

label: VisiCalc
entry_text: VisiCalc was an early electronic spreadsheet for entering and calculating data in rows and columns.
example: A planner changes an estimate and sees the revised budget totals.

label: Visier
entry_text: Visier provides workforce analytics tools for examining employee and staffing data.
example: An analyst compares turnover across departments.

label: Vision rehabilitation
entry_text: Vision rehabilitation helps people with vision loss use strategies, tools and environmental adaptations to perform everyday activities.
example: A specialist helps a reader choose magnification and adjust task lighting.

label: Visme
entry_text: Visme is a design platform for creating presentations, infographics and other visual content.
example: A communications team makes an infographic from an annual report.

label: VisSim
entry_text: VisSim is a block-diagram simulation tool for modeling dynamic systems.
example: An engineer studies how a modeled controller responds to a changing input.
sense_note: This is the VisSim simulation tool, not PTV Vissim traffic modeling.

label: Visual odometry
entry_text: Visual odometry estimates a camera’s motion from successive images.
example: A robot estimates motion by following image features across frames.

label: Visual storytelling
entry_text: Visual storytelling uses imagery and sequence to communicate events, relationships or a point of view.
example: A film shows a character’s isolation through progressively wider shots.

label: VMware Aria Automation
entry_text: VMware Aria Automation automates the delivery and management of cloud infrastructure and applications.
example: An infrastructure team publishes a virtual machine template for developers to request.

label: VMware Aria Automation Orchestrator
entry_text: VMware Aria Automation Orchestrator builds workflows that automate actions across connected systems.
example: An administrator automates steps for an approved virtual machine request.

label: VMware Aria Operations
entry_text: VMware Aria Operations monitors infrastructure and workload performance, capacity and health.
example: An administrator checks which cluster is approaching its capacity limit.

label: VMware Aria Operations for Logs
entry_text: VMware Aria Operations for Logs aggregates and analyzes log data for monitoring and troubleshooting.
example: An operator compares error messages from several hosts during an outage.

label: VMware Aria Suite
entry_text: VMware Aria Suite bundles tools for cloud infrastructure operations and automation.
example: A team coordinates infrastructure provisioning with capacity tracking.
sense_note: Packaging can differ by release.

label: Vocational rehabilitation counseling
entry_text: Vocational rehabilitation counseling helps people with disabilities pursue employment goals and locate relevant supports.
example: A counselor helps a job seeker consider training and workplace accommodations.

label: Voice UI design
entry_text: Voice UI design defines how users interact with systems through spoken input and responses.
example: A designer adds a clarifying question for ambiguous spoken commands.

label: VPython
entry_text: VPython supports the creation of interactive three-dimensional visualizations with Python.
example: An instructor visualizes a planet’s motion in a simulated orbit.

label: Vue.js
entry_text: Vue.js is a JavaScript framework for building reactive, component-based interfaces.
example: A Vue component updates a displayed list when its data changes.

label: Vulkan
entry_text: Vulkan is a cross-platform API for explicit control of graphics and compute work on compatible hardware.
example: A renderer submits drawing commands to a GPU using Vulkan.

label: Vulnerability assessment
entry_text: Vulnerability assessment identifies and prioritizes weaknesses in authorized systems according to risk.
example: A security team checks component inventories to prioritize patching.

label: Vyond
entry_text: Vyond is a platform for making animated videos with configurable characters, scenes and media assets.
example: A training team creates an animated orientation video.

label: Wainscot panelling
entry_text: Wainscot panelling covers the lower part of a wall with a protective or decorative finish.
example: A carpenter fits panels below the rail in a hallway.

label: WASAPI
entry_text: WASAPI is the Windows Audio Session API for accessing playback and capture audio streams.
example: An audio program sends sound to a selected endpoint.

label: Waste characterisation
entry_text: Waste characterisation describes waste by attributes such as composition, amount and hazardous properties.
example: A recycler estimates the share of recyclable packaging in a waste stream.

label: Waste minimisation
entry_text: Waste minimisation reduces the quantity or harmfulness of waste generated.
example: A workshop changes its cutting layout to produce fewer offcuts.

label: Watchkeeping
entry_text: Watchkeeping means maintaining an assigned lookout or operational watch and handing over relevant information when relieved.
example: A ship’s watch officer records nearby traffic and passes the situation to the next officer.
sense_note: The label can also refer to watches outside maritime work.

label: watchOS
entry_text: watchOS is Apple’s operating system for Apple Watch devices.
example: A developer tests how a workout display behaves on a watch.

label: Watcom SQL
entry_text: Watcom SQL was a relational database product that preceded the SQL Anywhere line.
example: A database specialist checks old Watcom SQL scripts before migrating a legacy application.

label: Water-based pipe coating
entry_text: Water-based pipe coating uses a coating carried primarily in water to protect or finish a pipe surface.
example: A technician evaluates adhesion on a coated pipe sample.

label: Water quality modelling
entry_text: Water quality modelling uses mathematical or computational models to estimate how physical, chemical or biological conditions affect water quality.
example: A watershed team compares modeled nutrient levels under different runoff scenarios.

label: Web crawling
entry_text: Web crawling automatically discovers and retrieves accessible web pages, often by following links.
example: A documentation team crawls its own website to find broken links.

label: Web development
entry_text: Web development creates and maintains websites and browser-based applications.
example: A developer builds a contact form and verifies that it works on mobile devices.

label: Web filtering
entry_text: Web filtering controls which web requests or content users may access according to a policy.
example: A school network blocks access to sites in categories disallowed by its policy.

label: WebCT
entry_text: WebCT was a learning management system for delivering and administering online courses.
example: An instructor posts course readings and reviews assignment submissions in a legacy WebCT course.

label: WebCTRL
entry_text: WebCTRL is a building automation platform for monitoring and controlling building equipment and conditions.
example: An operator reviews ventilation alarms from several buildings in a common interface.

label: WebDriver
entry_text: WebDriver is a standardized interface for controlling browser behavior programmatically, commonly for automated testing.
example: A test opens a page, clicks a button and checks the displayed confirmation.

label: WebDriverJS
entry_text: WebDriverJS refers to JavaScript tooling for driving browsers through WebDriver, particularly Selenium’s JavaScript bindings.
example: A tester writes a JavaScript check that verifies a modal can be closed.
sense_note: The label has also been used for other JavaScript WebDriver clients.

label: Website optimization
entry_text: Website optimization improves measured website performance or outcomes by diagnosing issues and testing changes.
example: A team compresses large images to reduce page load time.
sense_note: The goal may be speed, accessibility, conversion or another measurable outcome.

label: Website wireframing
entry_text: Website wireframing sketches the structure, layout and navigation of a website before detailed design or implementation.
example: A designer maps the search results and filtering controls in a low-fidelity layout.

label: WebVR
entry_text: WebVR was an experimental browser API for accessing virtual reality devices and presenting virtual environments from web pages.
example: An archivist examines a legacy browser demo that used WebVR to display a scene in a headset.
sense_note: Distinct from its successor, WebXR.

label: Weed control
entry_text: Weed control manages unwanted plants to reduce harm to crops, landscapes or ecosystems.
example: A gardener uses mulch to reduce weed establishment in a planting bed.

label: WhatsApp
entry_text: WhatsApp is a messaging service that supports text, media and voice or video calls.
example: A volunteer team uses a WhatsApp group to coordinate an event.

label: Wi-Fi 6
entry_text: Wi-Fi 6 is the Wi-Fi generation based on IEEE 802.11ax, which improves efficiency and capacity in busy wireless networks.
example: A campus equips a crowded classroom with Wi-Fi 6 access points for many simultaneous devices.

label: Wi-Fi Direct
entry_text: Wi-Fi Direct lets compatible devices establish a direct Wi-Fi connection without joining an existing access point.
example: A phone sends a document to a nearby compatible printer without joining the office network.

label: Wi-Fi test engineering
entry_text: Wi-Fi test engineering designs and runs tests for wireless behavior, compliance and interoperability.
example: An engineer measures how well a device maintains connectivity while moving between access points.

label: Wildlife observation
entry_text: Wildlife observation records animal presence, behavior or habitat use through attentive field observation.
example: A naturalist logs the time, habitat and behavior of birds seen along a survey route.

label: Will and testament preparation
entry_text: Will and testament preparation documents a person’s directions for administering and distributing their estate after death.
example: A legal professional records a client's instructions about beneficiaries and an executor.
sense_note: Formal requirements vary by jurisdiction.

label: Windows 10
entry_text: Windows 10 is a Microsoft desktop operating system released after Windows 8.1 and before Windows 11.
example: A technician checks whether a driver supports the installed Windows 10 edition.

label: Windows 7
entry_text: Windows 7 is a Microsoft desktop operating system that succeeded Windows Vista.
example: An archivist sets up Windows 7 to inspect the behavior of a legacy application.

label: Windows 8
entry_text: Windows 8 is a Microsoft desktop operating system that introduced a touch-oriented Start screen alongside the desktop.
example: A support specialist helps a user switch between the Start screen and a desktop program.

label: Windows Meeting Space
entry_text: Windows Meeting Space was a Windows Vista application for local collaboration, sharing and presentation.
example: A user shares a presentation with participants in a legacy Windows Vista session.

label: Windows Performance Analyzer
entry_text: Windows Performance Analyzer examines recorded Windows performance traces using graphs and tables.
example: An engineer inspects a trace to see whether CPU or disk activity coincides with a slow launch.

label: Windows Performance Recorder
entry_text: Windows Performance Recorder collects tracing data about Windows system and application activity.
example: A developer records a trace during an unusually slow program startup.

label: Windows Performance Toolkit
entry_text: Windows Performance Toolkit is a Microsoft collection of tools for recording and analyzing Windows performance data.
example: A team captures a startup trace with Windows Performance Recorder and analyzes it with Windows Performance Analyzer.

label: Windows software development
entry_text: Windows software development creates and maintains software intended to run on Microsoft Windows.
example: A developer builds and tests a desktop application against supported Windows versions.

label: Windows software trace preprocessor
entry_text: The Windows software trace preprocessor helps instrument source code for collecting diagnostic trace messages on Windows.
example: A driver developer adds trace statements to distinguish startup events during troubleshooting.
sense_note: Commonly abbreviated WPP.

label: Windows support
entry_text: Windows support diagnoses and resolves issues encountered by users or systems running Windows.
example: A technician investigates why a user’s application no longer starts after an update.

label: Windows systems administration
entry_text: Windows systems administration configures, maintains and monitors Windows-based computers and services.
example: An administrator applies approved settings consistently to a group of managed workstations.

label: Windows Vista
entry_text: Windows Vista is a Microsoft desktop operating system released between Windows XP and Windows 7.
example: A compatibility specialist checks how a legacy installer behaves on Windows Vista.

label: Windows XP Media Center Edition
entry_text: Windows XP Media Center Edition was an edition of Windows XP designed for media playback and related home-entertainment functions.
example: A user browses recorded television in a legacy Media Center setup.

label: Windows XP Professional x64 Edition
entry_text: Windows XP Professional x64 Edition was Microsoft’s 64-bit x86-compatible edition of Windows XP Professional.
example: A technician checks whether an older workstation has compatible 64-bit drivers.

label: Winemaking
entry_text: Winemaking is the production of wine through fermentation and related preparation, maturation and finishing steps.
example: A producer compares how different maturation vessels influence a wine’s character.

label: WinJS
entry_text: WinJS is a JavaScript library that supplies controls and utilities for building user interfaces, originally for Windows apps.
example: A maintainer reviews a legacy app’s WinJS list control before replacing its interface.

label: WKWebView
entry_text: WKWebView is Apple’s embeddable WebKit view for displaying web content in an application.
example: A developer displays an HTML help page inside an iOS app.

label: Women's Health and Cancer Rights Act
entry_text: The Women's Health and Cancer Rights Act is a U.S. law that requires qualifying health coverage offering mastectomy benefits to cover specified related care.
example: A benefits specialist reviews plan materials for required post-mastectomy reconstruction coverage.

label: Word embedding
entry_text: A word embedding is a numerical vector that places a word in a space where distances or directions can reflect learned patterns in its usage.
example: A search system uses nearby vectors to find terms used in similar contexts.

label: Word processing
entry_text: Word processing is the creation, editing and formatting of text documents using software.
example: An author applies heading styles and reviews tracked edits before exporting a report.

label: Word VBA
entry_text: Word VBA uses Visual Basic for Applications within Microsoft Word to automate tasks and control document objects.
example: An editor runs a macro that applies consistent formatting to recurring headings.

label: word2vec
entry_text: word2vec is a set of neural methods for learning word vectors by predicting words or their contexts from a corpus.
example: An analyst trains word vectors on customer reviews to compare words used in similar contexts.

label: Workers' compensation claims
entry_text: Workers’ compensation claims are requests for benefits under a program covering qualifying work-related injury or illness.
example: A claims specialist documents an accident report and reviews the supporting records.
sense_note: Eligibility and procedures vary by jurisdiction.

label: Workflow automation
entry_text: Workflow automation uses software to carry out predefined steps or transitions with reduced manual intervention.
example: A completed form automatically routes to the appropriate reviewer.

label: Workflow management
entry_text: Workflow management designs, coordinates and monitors how work moves among people and systems.
example: A manager tracks which approval step is delaying new requests.

label: Workforce optimisation
entry_text: Workforce optimisation uses staffing data and practices to align schedules, skills and deployment with service demand and other constraints.
example: A contact center adjusts shift coverage to match predicted peak call times.

label: Working with children aged 0-5
entry_text: Working with children aged 0–5 involves providing developmentally appropriate care and learning support for infants, toddlers and preschoolers.
example: A caregiver adapts a group activity so toddlers can participate safely and independently.

label: Writing
entry_text: Communicating effectively in writing as appropriate for the needs of the audience.

label: Writing outlines
entry_text: Writing outlines organizes a proposed text into main points, supporting details and a logical sequence.
example: A writer groups evidence under three section headings before drafting an essay.

label: WSDL2Java
entry_text: WSDL2Java refers to tools that generate Java code or bindings from a Web Services Description Language document.
example: A developer generates client bindings for an existing SOAP service.
sense_note: The label can refer to similarly named commands from different toolkits, including Apache Axis and Apache CXF.

label: wxGTK
entry_text: wxGTK is the wxWidgets implementation for systems using the GTK graphical toolkit.
example: A developer builds a wxWidgets desktop application with the GTK backend on Linux.

label: wxPerl
entry_text: wxPerl provides Perl bindings for building graphical applications with wxWidgets.
example: A maintainer updates the controls in a legacy Perl desktop application.

label: wxPython
entry_text: wxPython provides Python bindings for the wxWidgets graphical user interface toolkit.
example: A developer creates a desktop form with native-looking menus and buttons.

label: Wyse Management Suite
entry_text: Wyse Management Suite centrally configures and manages supported Dell endpoints such as thin clients.
example: An administrator assigns a common configuration profile to a group of thin clients.

label: Xanthoproteic reaction
entry_text: The xanthoproteic reaction is a qualitative color reaction that indicates the presence of certain aromatic amino acid residues in a sample.
example: A chemistry class relates the observed qualitative color change to aromatic groups in proteins.

label: Xbox Live Vision
entry_text: Xbox Live Vision was a camera accessory for the Xbox 360 that supported compatible games and video features.
example: A player uses the camera for video chat in a supported legacy Xbox experience.

label: Xcalibur
entry_text: Xcalibur is Thermo Scientific software for acquiring and processing data from compatible mass spectrometry instruments.
example: An analyst reviews a recorded chromatogram and its associated mass spectra.
sense_note: Interpreted as Thermo Scientific Xcalibur.

label: XtraGrid
entry_text: XtraGrid is a DevExpress grid control for displaying and editing structured data in Windows Forms applications.
example: A developer adds column filtering to an order table.
sense_note: The older XtraGrid name is associated with the DevExpress WinForms Data Grid.

label: Yahoo Messenger
entry_text: Yahoo Messenger was an instant messaging service that supported conversations and presence information.
example: A user could see whether a contact was online before starting a chat.

label: YARA
entry_text: YARA describes and matches patterns in files or data for tasks such as identifying known types of suspicious content.
example: A security analyst checks files gathered in an authorized investigation against reviewed detection rules.

label: Yardi
entry_text: Yardi provides software for managing real estate operations, accounting and property records.
example: A property manager uses a Yardi application to reconcile occupancy and rent records.
sense_note: The label is a vendor and product family, not one specific application.

label: Yellow Dog Linux
entry_text: Yellow Dog Linux was a Linux distribution developed for systems including PowerPC hardware.
example: An archivist boots a compatible older machine to inspect an application built on Yellow Dog Linux.

label: Youth mentoring
entry_text: Youth mentoring is a supportive relationship in which a mentor helps a young person build skills, confidence and direction over time.
example: A mentor helps a teen plan and reflect on a first community project.

label: YunOS
entry_text: YunOS was an operating system developed by Alibaba for connected devices including smartphones.
example: A mobile software archivist identifies a device that originally ran YunOS.
sense_note: Names and product branding changed over time.

label: z/OS
entry_text: z/OS is IBM’s operating system for mainframes, designed to support enterprise workloads such as transactions and batch processing.
example: An operator checks the results of an overnight batch job on a z/OS system.

label: Z-Wave
entry_text: Z-Wave is a low-power wireless communications technology used to connect compatible automation devices.
example: A home automation controller receives status updates from a compatible door sensor.

label: Zemax OpticStudio
entry_text: Zemax OpticStudio is software for designing and analyzing optical systems through modeling and ray tracing.
example: An engineer compares lens designs to reduce image distortion.

label: ZENworks Asset Management
entry_text: ZENworks Asset Management inventories hardware and software and supports tracking software licenses and usage.
example: An IT team compares installed applications with its license entitlements.

label: zeroheight
entry_text: zeroheight is a platform for publishing and maintaining design-system documentation.
example: A design systems team documents when to use a particular button component.

label: Zerto
entry_text: Zerto provides replication and orchestration tools for recovering workloads after disruptions or moving them between environments.
example: An infrastructure team tests whether a replicated workload can be recovered in a designated environment.

label: Zetafax
entry_text: Zetafax is a software platform for sending, receiving and managing faxes through a networked service.
example: An office routes incoming faxes to an internal inbox.

label: ZFS
entry_text: ZFS integrates a filesystem and volume management, with features such as data checksums, snapshots and pooled storage.
example: An administrator takes a read-only snapshot so a prior file version can be recovered.
